1.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
1.rest: — "Chochmah is the brain, which is thought within; Binah is the heart, and with it the heart understands; and of these two it is written, 'The hidden things belong to Hashem our God' (Devarim 29:28)."

2.label: Menachos 29b
2.rest: — "Why was the World to Come created with a yud? Because its righteous are few. And why is its head bent? Because its righteous have their heads bent on account of their deeds, for their deeds are not like one another's."

3.label: Berachos 61a
3.rest: — "A person has two kidneys: one counsels him for good and one counsels him for evil. It stands to reason that the good one is at his right and the evil one at his left, as it is written, 'The heart of a wise man is at his right, and the heart of a fool at his left' (Koheles 10:2)."

4.label: Shabbos 63a
4.rest: — "What is meant by 'Length of days is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor' (Mishlei 3:16)?… Rather: for those who go to the right with it, there is length of days, and all the more so riches and honor; for those who go to the left with it, there are riches and honor, but not length of days." Rashi: those who go to the right — who probe its reasons precisely, or who occupy themselves with it for its own sake; to the left — who do not toil in it as needed.

5.label: Tanchuma, Mishpatim 19
5.rest: — "'A thousand shall fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right' (Tehillim 91:7): the left, which is not extended in mitzvos, fells only a thousand harmful spirits; the right, which is extended in mitzvos, fells ten thousand."

6.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 69, 111a
6.rest: — Chochmah is read as ko'ach mah, "the power of 'what'": the power of the letters of the work of Creation.

7.label: Zohar I 1b (Introduction)
7.rest: — "And there is another below, called Mah. What is between them? The first, hidden one is called Mi… Once a person asks and searches, to gaze and to know from level to level until the end of all levels — once he reaches there: Mah (what)? What have you known? What have you gazed upon? What have you searched out? Everything is hidden as at first."

8.label: Bechoros 55a
8.rest: — "The essence (zachrusa) of the blood is the liver, in line with Rabbi Yitzchak, for Rabbi Yitzchak said: A liver that dissolved defiles in the measure of a revi'is."

9.label: Berachos 61b
9.rest: — "The lung draws in all kinds of liquids; the liver becomes angry; the gall casts a drop into it and calms it; the spleen laughs; the gizzard grinds; the stomach sleeps; the nose awakens."

10.label: Bava Basra 58b
10.rest: — "'At the head of all death am I, blood; at the head of all life am I, wine'… Rather it should be written: At the head of all illnesses am I, blood; at the head of all remedies am I, wine."

11.label: Zohar III 234a (Pinchas, Ra'aya Meheimna)
11.rest: — "The liver is the level of Esav. Esav is Edom: it gathers all the blood, clear and turbid, and does not distinguish between good and bad. The heart is Israel, which distinguishes between good and bad, between impure blood and pure blood, and takes only the clearest and cleanest of that blood, like one who separates food from waste."

12.label: Zohar II 182b (Tetzaveh)
12.rest: — "And if you say, what of the anger of the Sages? The anger of the Sages is good on every side, for we learned that Torah is fire and the Torah heats him, as it is written, 'Is not My word like fire?' The anger of the Sages is over words of Torah, to give honor to the Torah, and all of it is for the service of the Holy One."

13.label: Taanis 4a
13.rest: — "Rava said: A young Torah scholar who flares up — it is the Torah that heats him, as it says, 'Is not My word like fire, says Hashem?' (Yirmeyahu 23:29). And Rav Ashi said: Any Torah scholar who is not as hard as iron is not a Torah scholar, as it says, 'and like a hammer that shatters rock.'"

14.label: Sanhedrin 37a
14.rest: — “A person stamps many coins with one seal, and they are all alike; but the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, stamped every person with the seal of Adam the first man, and no one is like his fellow. Therefore every individual must say: For my sake the world was created.” The Mishnah joins individual worth with the incomparable greatness of the Creator. Rav Tzadok explains this responsibility through the particular contribution for which each person is needed.

15.label: Shabbos 31b
15.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said: The Holy One, blessed be He, created His world only so that they should fear Him, as it says, 'And God has made it so, that they should fear before Him' (Koheles 3:14)."

16.label: Devarim Rabbah 7:8
16.rest: — "Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said: From where do you say that had Israel been lacking even one person, the Shechinah would not have been revealed to them? As it is written, 'For on the third day Hashem will descend before the eyes of all the people upon Mount Sinai' (Shemos 19:11)."

17.label: Sotah 21b
17.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Words of Torah endure only in one who makes himself as one who is not, as it says, 'And wisdom — from where (me'ayin) shall it be found?' (Iyov 28:12)." Rashi: from one who makes himself as nothing (ayin).

18.label: Taanis 7a
18.rest: — "Rabbi Chanina bar Idi said: Why are the words of Torah likened to water, as it is written, 'Ho, all who are thirsty, go to the water' (Yeshayahu 55:1)? To tell you: just as water leaves a high place and goes to a low place, so the words of Torah endure only in one whose mind is humble."

19.label: Sukkah 13a
19.rest: — "Hyssop — but not Greek hyssop, not kochali hyssop, not wilderness hyssop, not Roman hyssop, and not any hyssop that has a qualifying name."

20.label: Menachos 37a
20.rest: — Tefillin are placed on the weaker hand: "Rav Ashi said: From 'yadchah' (your hand, Shemos 13:16), written with a hei — the weak hand (yad keihah)." And: "A left-handed person puts tefillin on his right hand, which is his left."

21.label: Taz, Orach Chaim 46:2
21.rest: — "Yisrael" is mentioned in this blessing [Ozer Yisrael bigevurah] and in Oter Yisrael, unlike the others, because the others are for the benefit of the whole world, while these two are unique to Israel, being for modesty: the belt, so that his heart should not see his nakedness, and the head-covering, as it says (Shabbos 156b), "Cover your head, so that the fear of your Master be upon you."

22.label: Shabbos 156b
22.rest: — The astrologers told the mother of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak that her son would be a thief. "She would not let him uncover his head. She said to him: Cover your head, so that the fear of Heaven may be upon you, and ask for mercy." Rashi: that the evil inclination not rule over you.

23.label: Shabbos 77b
23.rest: — "Sudara (scarf) — 'Sod Hashem lirei'av,' the secret of Hashem is for those who fear Him (Tehillim 25:14)."

24.label: Kiddushin 31a
24.rest: — "Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: It is forbidden for a person to walk four cubits with upright stature, as it says, 'The whole earth is full of His glory' (Yeshayahu 6:3). Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua would not walk four cubits with his head uncovered; he said: The Shechinah is above my head."

25.label: Arachin 16a
25.rest: — "The turban atones for the haughty… the belt atones for thoughts of the heart, upon the place where it lies, as it is written, 'and they shall be upon the heart of Aharon' (Shemos 28:30)."

26.label: Zevachim 19a
26.rest: — On "They shall not gird themselves where one sweats" (Yechezkel 44:18): "Rav Ashi said: Huna bar Nasan told me: Once I was standing before King Izgadar, and my belt had ridden up, and he pulled it down for me and said to me: 'A kingdom of priests and a holy nation' (Shemos 19:6) is written of you."

27.label: Avos 4:1
27.rest: — "Ben Zoma says: Who is wise? One who learns from every person… Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination, as it says, 'Better is one slow to anger than a mighty man, and one who rules his spirit than one who captures a city' (Mishlei 16:32)."

28.label: Shabbos 88a
28.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said: When Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear,' a heavenly voice went forth and said: Who revealed to My children this secret which the ministering angels use, as it is written, 'mighty in strength, who do His word, to hearken to the voice of His word' (Tehillim 103:20)? Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said: Why are Israel likened to an apple tree (Shir HaShirim 2:3)? Just as the apple's fruit comes before its leaves, so Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear.'"

29.label: Avodah Zarah 3a, 4b
29.rest: — "'Which I command you today, to do them' (Devarim 7:11): today to do them, and not tomorrow to do them; today to do them, and tomorrow to receive their reward."

30.label: Shabbos 151b
30.rest: — "And Shlomo too said in his wisdom: 'Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come' — these are the days of old age; 'and the years arrive of which you will say, I have no desire in them' (Koheles 12:1) — these are the days of Mashiach, in which there is neither merit nor guilt."

31.label: Yoma 69b
31.rest: — "'And they cried out with a loud voice to Hashem their God' (Nechemiah 9:4). What did they say? … Woe, woe! This is the one who destroyed the Sanctuary, burned the Temple, killed all the righteous and exiled Israel from their land, and still he dances among us! Did You give him to us for any reason but that we receive reward through him? We want neither him nor his reward."

32.label: Berachos 6a
32.rest: — "From where do we know that tefillin are a strength for Israel? As it is written, 'And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of Hashem is called upon you, and they shall fear you' (Devarim 28:10); and it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says: These are the tefillin that are in the head."

33.label: Megillah 16b
33.rest: — “'The Jews had light, joy, gladness, and honor.' Rav Yehudah said: 'Light' is Torah, as it is said, 'For a commandment is a lamp and Torah is light.' 'Joy' is the festival, as it is said, 'You shall rejoice in your festival.' 'Gladness' is circumcision, as it is said, 'I rejoice over Your word.'” The next line identifies 'honor' with tefillin, specifically the tefillin of the head. The Gemara establishes the Torah meaning of light; the feminine form orah as an allusion to the Oral Torah is Rav Tzadok's reading.

34.label: Megillah 16b
34.rest: — “'And honor'—these are tefillin, as it is said: 'All the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of Hashem is called upon you, and they shall fear you.' Rabbi Eliezer the Great says: These are the tefillin of the head.” The maamar now develops the 'honor' clause, beyond its earlier treatment of light and joy. The head-tefillin image permits Rav Tzadok's association with the supernal crown.

35.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 33
35.rest: — "When Israel said before Mount Sinai, 'All that Hashem has spoken we will do and we will hear' (Shemos 24:7), immediately six hundred thousand ministering angels descended with belts and crowns in their hands… Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: One hundred and twenty myriads of ministering angels descended with the Holy One: sixty myriads tying on crowns, and sixty myriads girding them with belts."

36.label: Rashi, Bereishis 1:1
36.rest: — "'Bereishis' — for the sake of the Torah, which is called 'the beginning (reishis) of His way' (Mishlei 8:22), and for the sake of Israel, who are called 'the beginning (reishis) of His produce' (Yirmeyahu 2:3)."

37.label: Nazir 23b
37.rest: — "Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: A transgression for its own sake is greater than a mitzvah not for its own sake. But Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: A person should always occupy himself with Torah and mitzvos even not for their own sake, for from not for its own sake he comes to for its own sake."

38.label: Bava Metzia 33b
38.rest: — "'Declare to My people their transgression' (Yeshayahu 58:1) — these are Torah scholars, whose unintentional errors are counted as deliberate; 'and to the house of Yaakov their sins' — these are the amei ha'aretz, whose deliberate sins are counted as unintentional."

39.label: Rosh Hashanah 11a
39.rest: — "On Rosh Hashanah the servitude of our fathers in Egypt ceased; in Nissan they were redeemed, and in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed" — the view of Rabbi Eliezer, who derives that the world was created in Tishrei from "Let the earth sprout grass… fruit tree" (Bereishis 1:11).

40.label: Sanhedrin 97b
40.rest: — "Rav said: All the ends have passed, and the matter depends only on teshuvah and good deeds… Rabbi Eliezer says: If Israel do teshuvah they are redeemed, and if not they are not redeemed. Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: If they do not do teshuvah they are not redeemed?! Rather, the Holy One sets up a king over them whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's, and Israel do teshuvah, and He brings them back to the good."

41.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 27a (s.v. kemaan)
41.rest: — Both views are the words of the living God: in Tishrei it arose in His thought to create the world, and it was not actually created until Nissan.

42.label: Shabbos 49a
42.rest: — "Rabbi Yannai said: Tefillin require a clean body, like Elisha, the man of wings. What is it? Abaye said: That he not pass wind in them; Rava said: That he not sleep in them."

43.label: Shabbos 12a
43.rest: — "Rabbah bar Rav Huna said: A person must touch his tefillin every single hour — a kal vachomer from the tzitz: if of the tzitz, which has only one mention of the Name, the Torah said, 'And it shall be upon his forehead always' (Shemos 28:38) — that he not divert his mind from it — then tefillin, which have many mentions, all the more so."

44.label: Shabbos 130a
44.rest: — "Every mitzvah for which Israel did not give themselves over to death, such as tefillin, is still weak in their hands; for Rabbi Yannai said: Tefillin require a clean body, like Elisha, the man of wings."

45.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 17a (s.v. karkafta)
45.rest: — "'A skull that has not put on tefillin': if he engages in Torah, he is like one who puts on tefillin, for the Mechilta says that one who engages in Torah is exempt from tefillin. And Rabbeinu Tam explains that here [it speaks of one] to whom the mitzvah is despised… but if he fears to put them on because a clean body is required, like Elisha Baal Kenafayim, [he is not included]."

46.label: Berachos 4a
46.rest: — Though Yaakov had been promised, "Behold, I am with you" (Bereishis 28:15), he was afraid (Bereishis 32:8), for he said: perhaps sin will cause it.

47.label: Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer 46
47.rest: — On Rosh Chodesh Elul the Holy One said to Moshe, "Come up to Me on the mountain," and they sounded the shofar throughout the camp, so that they would not again stray after idolatry; and the Holy One was exalted with that shofar, as it says, "God has gone up with a teruah" (Tehillim 47:6). Therefore the Sages instituted that the shofar be blown on Rosh Chodesh Elul every year (cited by the Tur, Orach Chaim 581).

48.label: Midrash Tehillim 47:2
48.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah bar Nachman said in the name of Reish Lakish: When the Holy One goes up to judge and sits on the throne to judge — once they blow the shofar, He rises and turns the attribute of judgment into the attribute of mercy, as it says, 'Hashem with the sound of the shofar' (Tehillim 47:6)."

49.label: Shabbos 31b
49.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: The Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world but the fear of Heaven alone, as it says, 'And now, Israel, what does Hashem your God ask of you but to fear' (Devarim 10:12); and it is written, 'And He said to man: Behold (hen), the fear of Hashem is wisdom' (Iyov 28:28) — for in Greek they call 'one' hen."

50.label: Kiddushin 32b
50.rest: — "Rav Ashi said: Even according to the one who says that a nasi who forgoes his honor, his honor is forgone — a king who forgoes his honor, his honor is not forgone, as it says, 'You shall surely set a king over you' (Devarim 17:15): that his awe be upon you."

51.label: Rema, Orach Chaim 1:1
51.rest: — "When a person takes to heart that the great King, the Holy One, blessed be He, whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and sees his deeds, as it says, 'Can a man hide in secret places that I shall not see him? says Hashem' (Yirmeyahu 23:24) — immediately awe and submission will come upon him, in dread of Hashem Yisbarach, and he will be ashamed before Him constantly."

52.label: Ramban, Devarim 30:6
52.rest: — In the days of Mashiach, choosing the good will be natural to them; the heart will not desire what is not fitting and will not want it at all — and this is the circumcision of the heart mentioned here.

53.label: Sanhedrin 98a
53.rest: — "He went to [Mashiach] and said: Peace upon you, my master and teacher. He said: Peace upon you, son of Levi. He said: When will the master come? He said: Today. He came to Eliyahu, who asked: What did he tell you? — 'Peace upon you, son of Levi.' He said: He has assured you and your father of the World to Come… He said: This is what he told you: 'Today — if you will hearken to His voice' (Tehillim 95:7)." Rashi: had you not been perfect tzaddikim he would not have greeted you and mentioned your father.

54.label: Devarim Rabbah 2:12
54.rest: — "He said to him: The gates of prayer are sometimes open and sometimes locked, but the gates of teshuvah are always open… Just as this pool is sometimes open and sometimes locked, so the gates of prayer are sometimes open and sometimes locked; but the sea is always open — so the hand of the Holy One is always open to receive penitents."

55.label: Shabbos 88a
55.rest: — “Six hundred thousand ministering angels came and tied two crowns to each one of Yisrael … and when Yisrael sinned, they removed them … and Moshe merited and took them all.”

56.label: Shabbos 151b
56.rest: — "And Shlomo too said in his wisdom: 'Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come' — these are the days of old age; 'and the years arrive of which you will say, I have no desire in them' (Koheles 12:1) — these are the days of Mashiach, in which there is neither merit nor guilt."

57.label: Yoma 69b
57.rest: — "'And they cried out with a loud voice to Hashem their God' (Nechemiah 9:4). What did they say? … Woe, woe! This is the one who destroyed the Sanctuary, burned the Temple, killed all the righteous and exiled Israel from their land, and still he dances among us! Did You give him to us for any reason but that we receive reward through him? We want neither him nor his reward."

58.label: Avodah Zarah 5a
58.rest: — "Our Rabbis taught: 'Who would grant that they had such a heart' (Devarim 5:26) — Moshe said to Israel: Ingrates, children of ingrates! When the Holy One said to Israel, 'Who would grant that they had such a heart,' they should have said: You grant it!" Rashi: they do not acknowledge the good done them.

59.label: Tosafos, Avodah Zarah 5a (s.v. kefuyei tovah)
59.rest: — "He called them ingrates because they did not want to say 'You grant it,' since they did not want to acknowledge Him for it."

60.label: Shabbos 88b
60.rest: — "Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: At each utterance that came from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, the souls of Israel left them, as it says, 'My soul went out when He spoke' (Shir HaShirim 5:6). If their souls left at the first utterance, how did they receive the second? He brought down the dew with which He will revive the dead in the future and revived them, as it says, 'A generous rain You shed, O God' (Tehillim 68:10)."

61.label: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 5:5
61.rest: — "He does not know with a knowledge that is outside Him, like people, who and their knowledge are two; rather He, may His Name be exalted, and His knowledge are one, and a person's mind cannot grasp this clearly. And just as a person cannot grasp and find the truth of the Creator, as it says, 'For man shall not see Me and live' (Shemos 33:20), so a person cannot grasp and find the Creator's knowledge. This is what the prophet said: 'For My thoughts are not your thoughts, nor your ways My ways' (Yeshayahu 55:8)."

62.label: Sotah 12a
62.rest: — “The Sages say: When Moshe was born, the whole house filled with light. Here it is written, She saw that he was good; and there it is written, God saw the light, that it was good.” The association of good with light is explicit in the Gemara. Rav Tzadok reads Moshe's original spiritual portion through this image of light preceding encounter with evil.

63.label: Taanis 31a
63.rest: — "In the future the Holy One will make a dance for the righteous, and He will sit among them in Gan Eden, and each one will point with his finger, as it says, 'And it shall be said on that day: Behold, this is our God, for whom we hoped, that He would save us' (Yeshayahu 25:9)."

64.label: Avodah Zarah 5b
64.rest: — "Even Moshe Rabbeinu hinted it to Israel only after forty years, as it says, 'And I led you forty years in the wilderness' (Devarim 29:4), and it is written, 'But Hashem did not give you a heart to know' (Devarim 29:3). Rabbah said: Learn from this that a person does not grasp his teacher's mind until forty years."

65.label: Avodah Zarah 5b
65.rest: — "Rabbah said: Learn from this that a person does not grasp the mind of his teacher until forty years." Rashi: the full depth of his understanding; for Moshe did not hint this to Israel until after forty years, as it says, "And Hashem did not give you a heart to know… until this day" (Devarim 29:3).

66.label: Zohar III 273a (Ra'aya Meheimna, Eikev)
66.rest: — "The second: to break bread over two loaves on Shabbos, which allude to the two Tablets of the Torah that were given on Shabbos."

67.label: Shabbos 86b
67.rest: — “All agree that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbos.”

68.label: Berachos 6b
68.rest: — "Whoever usually comes to the synagogue and one day does not come, the Holy One, blessed is He, asks after him: 'Who among you fears Hashem…' (Yeshayahu 50:10)." Rashi: who fears Hashem — who used to come to Him. Berachos 9b — "The pious would finish [Shema] with sunrise… What is the verse? 'They shall fear You with the sun.'" Rashi: the mitzvah is to pray at sunrise. (The 10a reference could not be located.)

69.label: Yoma 86b
69.rest: — "Rabbi Meir used to say: Great is teshuvah, for on account of one individual who repents the whole world is forgiven, as it says, 'I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely, for My anger has turned away from him' (Hoshea 14:5) — it does not say 'from them' but 'from him.'"

70.label: Rashi, Vayikra 26:6
70.rest: — "'And I will give peace in the land' — lest you say: here is food and here is drink — if there is no peace, there is nothing. Therefore it says after all this, 'and I will give peace in the land.' From here, that peace outweighs everything."

71.label: Avodah Zarah 5a
71.rest: — David was not fit for that deed [with Bas Sheva], "but it was to tell you that if an individual sinned, one says to him: Go to the individual; and if a community sinned, one says to them: Go to the community." Rashi: it was a decree of the King, to give an opening to penitents.

72.label: Berachos 5a
72.rest: — “Rabbi Yochanan said: ... Whoever can occupy himself with Torah but does not do so, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings ugly sufferings upon him and troubles him, as it is said, I became mute in silence; I was silent from good, and my pain was stirred up. Good means nothing other than Torah, as it is said, For I have given you a good teaching; do not abandon My Torah.” Rav Tzadok draws on the identification of good with Torah when reading a good heart as a heart shaped by Torah.

73.label: Eruvin 100b
73.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Had the Torah not been given, we would have learned modesty from the cat, [not to] steal from the ant, [chastity in] relations from the dove, and proper conduct from the rooster, who first appeases and then mates."

74.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
74.rest: — "Chesed is the right arm, Gevurah the left arm, Tiferes the body, Netzach and Hod the two thighs, Yesod the completion of the body, the sign of the holy covenant; Malchus is the mouth — we call it the Oral Torah."

75.label: Chullin 16a
75.rest: — "From where do we know that slaughter is with something detached? As it says, 'And Avraham took the knife to slaughter' (Bereishis 22:10)… The verse comes to teach us the alacrity of Avraham."

76.label: Sotah 10b
76.rest: — "Rather, read 'vayakri' — this teaches that Avraham Avinu caused the Name of the Holy One to be called by the mouth of every passerby. How? After they had eaten and drunk, they stood to bless him; he said to them: Did you eat of mine? You ate of the God of the world! Thank, praise and bless the One Who spoke and the world came into being."

77.label: Bereishis Rabbah 39:14
77.rest: — "'And the souls they had made in Charan' (Bereishis 12:5) — Avraham would convert the men, and Sarah would convert the women."

78.label: Tanchuma, Mishpatim 19
78.rest: — "'A thousand shall fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right' (Tehillim 91:7): the left, which is not extended in mitzvos, fells only a thousand harmful spirits; the right, which is extended in mitzvos, fells ten thousand."

79.label: Megillah 19b
79.rest: — "Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: What is meant by 'and upon them, according to all the words that Hashem spoke with you on the mountain' (Devarim 9:10)? This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Moshe the fine points of the Torah, the fine points of the Sofrim, and what the Sofrim would in the future innovate."

80.label: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2
80.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah says: At the time Israel heard 'I am Hashem your God' (Shemos 20:2), the study of Torah was implanted in their heart, and they would learn and not forget. They came to Moshe and said: Moshe our teacher, be an intermediary between us, as it says, 'You speak with us, and we will hear' (Shemos 20:16)… and they returned to learning and forgetting."

81.label: Nedarim 22b
81.rest: — “Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Yehoshua.”

82.label: Shemos Rabbah 27:9
82.rest: — A king gave his servant two cups to carry; a calf gored the servant and broke one of them. "The king said to him: If so, know and be careful with the second. So the Holy One said: Two cups you mixed at Sinai — 'we will do and we will hear'; you broke 'we will do' when you made the calf before Me; be careful with 'we will hear.'"

83.label: Zohar III 160a (Shelach)
83.rest: — "Once a person exerts himself with the will of his heart toward the Holy One, He wants nothing from us but the heart." So too Sanhedrin 106b: "The Merciful One wants the heart."

84.label: Sanhedrin 106b
84.rest: — "And Rav Yehudah would take off one shoe and the rain would come, while we cry out and no one pays attention to us. But the Holy One, blessed be He, wants the heart, as it is written, 'and Hashem sees into the heart' (I Shmuel 16:7)."

85.label: Midrash Tanchuma, Bereishis 2, opening Sheilta
85.rest: — “The house of Israel is obligated to rest on Shabbos. When the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He created it in six days and rested on Shabbos, blessing and sanctifying it, like one who builds a house, finishes its work, and makes a festive day. ... The Merciful One says: Rest on Shabbos just as I rested on it, as it is written: 'He rested on the seventh day; therefore Hashem blessed' it.” This Aramaic opening, explicitly a Sheilta, gives the direct formulation of imitating Divine rest that Rav Tzadok quotes.

86.label: Sanhedrin 99b
86.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said: Every person was created for toil, as it says, 'For man is born to toil' (Iyov 5:7). I do not know whether for toil of the mouth or of labor; when it says, 'for his mouth urges him on' (Mishlei 16:26), it is toil of the mouth. And I still do not know whether toil of Torah or of conversation; when it says, 'This book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth' (Yehoshua 1:8), he was created for the toil of Torah."

87.label: Shabbos 11a
87.rest: — "Companions who were occupied with Torah interrupt for Krias Shema but do not interrupt for prayer. Rabbi Yochanan said: This was taught only of such as Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and his companions, whose Torah is their occupation; but such as we interrupt for Krias Shema and for prayer."

88.label: Rosh Hashanah 35a
88.rest: — "But Rav Yehudah would set his prayer in order and then pray! — Rav Yehudah is different: since he prayed only from thirty days to thirty days, it is like something occasional."

89.label: Berachos 17a
89.rest: — "Rava used to say: The goal of wisdom is teshuvah and good deeds, so that a person should not read and learn and then kick at his father and mother and his teacher… as it says, 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem; good understanding to all who do them' (Tehillim 111:10). It does not say 'to those who do' but 'to those who do them': to those who do them for their own sake."

90.label: Avodah Zarah 19a
90.rest: — "'Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem' — R. Amram said in the name of Rav: Fortunate is one who repents while he is still a man." Rashi: 'while he is a man' — in his youthful strength, hurrying to know his Creator before old age.

91.label: Berachos 5a
91.rest: — “Rabbi Yochanan said: ... Whoever can occupy himself with Torah but does not do so, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings ugly sufferings upon him and troubles him, as it is said, I became mute in silence; I was silent from good, and my pain was stirred up. Good means nothing other than Torah, as it is said, For I have given you a good teaching; do not abandon My Torah.” Rav Tzadok draws on the identification of good with Torah when reading a good heart as a heart shaped by Torah.

92.label: Sanhedrin 99b
92.rest: — “Whoever teaches his fellow’s son Torah, Scripture regards him as if he made him … as if he made the words of Torah, as it says: ‘You shall keep the words of this covenant and do them.’”

93.label: Zohar III 113a (Bechukosai)
93.rest: — "Because he walked in the ways of the Torah, fulfilled the commandments of the Torah and led the kingship as is fitting, as it were he made a Name above. There was no king in the world who merited this like David, who would rise at midnight and praise the Holy One until the holy Name ascended upon its throne… Therefore 'va'asisem osam' (and you shall do — make — them) is written."

94.label: Rosh Hashanah 10b–11a
94.rest: — "Rabbi Eliezer says: In Tishrei the world was created; in Tishrei the Patriarchs were born; in Tishrei the Patriarchs died; on Pesach Yitzchak was born; on Rosh Hashanah Sarah, Rachel and Chanah were remembered; on Rosh Hashanah Yosef went out of prison… In Nissan they were redeemed, and in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed. Rabbi Yehoshua says: In Nissan the world was created…; in Nissan they were redeemed, and in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed."

95.label: Sanhedrin 97b
95.rest: — "Rabbi Eliezer says: If Israel repent they are redeemed, and if not they are not redeemed. Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: If they do not repent they are not redeemed? Rather, the Holy One, blessed is He, sets up a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's, Israel repent, and He brings them back to the good." Another baraisa: "'You shall be redeemed not with money' (Yeshayahu 52:3): not with repentance and good deeds." Rashi: even without repentance they are redeemed.

96.label: Bereishis Rabbah 3:1
96.rest: — "'The opening of Your words gives light' (Tehillim 119:130) — from the opening of Your mouth there was light for us."

97.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 27a (s.v. kemaan)
97.rest: — Both views are the words of the living God: in Tishrei it arose in His thought to create the world, and it was not actually created until Nissan.

98.label: Pesikta DeRav Kahana 23:1
98.rest: — "Rabbi Eliezer taught: On the twenty-fifth of Elul the world was created; and Rav's view accords with this, as it is taught in the shofar blessings of Rav: 'This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day.'"

99.label: Eruvin 41a
99.rest: — “After Rabban Gamliel died, Rabbi Yehoshua entered to overturn his ruling. Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri stood and said: I see that the body follows the head! Throughout Rabban Gamliel's life we established the law according to him; now you wish to overturn his words? Yehoshua, we do not heed you, for the law has already been established according to Rabban Gamliel, and no one disputed the matter.” The proverb occurs in a dispute about maintaining an established ruling after a leader's death. Rav Tzadok applies its image to Rosh Chodesh as the head that directs the month.

100.label: Rosh Hashanah 11a
100.rest: — "On Rosh Hashanah the servitude of our fathers in Egypt ceased; in Nissan they were redeemed, and in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed" — the view of Rabbi Eliezer, who derives that the world was created in Tishrei from "Let the earth sprout grass… fruit tree" (Bereishis 1:11).

101.label: Shabbos 89b
101.rest: — “Rabbi Yitzchak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: If your sins are like these years that have been arranged and have come from the six days of creation until now, they shall become white as snow.” The Gemara expounds shanim as years rather than merely as scarlet. Rav Tzadok relates this wording to the divine ordering of history and to the transformation accomplished by repentance.

102.label: Zohar I 32a (Bereishis)
102.rest: — "That light came forth from within darkness, which was engraved in the hollows of the Hidden of all… the lower darkness, which is called Night, as it is written, 'And the darkness He called Night.'"

103.label: Menachos 45a
103.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah says: This passage Eliyahu is destined to expound."

104.label: Taanis 5b
104.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Yaakov Avinu did not die. He was asked: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed and the buriers buried? He answered: I am expounding a verse, as it says, 'And you, fear not, My servant Yaakov… for behold, I save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity' (Yirmeyahu 30:10) — it compares him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too he is alive." Rashi: he lives forever; they embalmed him because they thought he had died.

105.label: Sotah 13b
105.rest: — "Rabbi Eliezer HaGadol says: Over twelve mil by twelve mil, corresponding to the camp of Israel, a heavenly voice proclaimed, 'And Moshe died' — the great scribe of Israel. And some say: Moshe did not die. It is written here, 'And Moshe died there' (Devarim 34:5), and there, 'And he was there with Hashem' (Shemos 34:28): just as there he stood and served, so here he stands and serves."

106.label: Taanis 5b
106.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Yaakov Avinu did not die. He said to him: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed and the buriers buried? He said: I am expounding a verse."

107.label: Midrash Tehillim 47:2
107.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah bar Nachman said in the name of Reish Lakish: When the Holy One goes up to judge and sits on the throne to judge — once they blow the shofar, He rises and turns the attribute of judgment into the attribute of mercy, as it says, 'Hashem with the sound of the shofar' (Tehillim 47:6)."

108.label: Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer 46
108.rest: — On Rosh Chodesh Elul the Holy One said to Moshe, "Come up to Me on the mountain," and they sounded the shofar throughout the camp, so that they would not again stray after idolatry; and the Holy One was exalted with that shofar, as it says, "God has gone up with a teruah" (Tehillim 47:6). Therefore the Sages instituted that the shofar be blown on Rosh Chodesh Elul every year (cited by the Tur, Orach Chaim 581).

109.label: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2
109.rest: — "The Holy One said to Israel: My children, open for Me one opening of teshuvah, as small as the eye of a needle, and I will open for you openings through which wagons and carriages can enter."

110.label: Zohar I 1a (Introduction)
110.rest: — "Just as a rose has thirteen petals, so the Congregation of Israel has thirteen attributes of mercy surrounding her on every side. So too 'Elokim' here: from the moment it is mentioned, it brings forth thirteen words to surround the Congregation of Israel and guard her."

111.label: Zohar III, Pinchas
111.rest: — "Five strong ones that surround it — these are the fifty gates."

112.label: Zohar III 11b (Vayikra)
112.rest: — "Come and see: ten utterances for the work of Creation, as we learned, 'With ten utterances the world was created'; ten utterances for the giving of the Torah — the Ten Commandments. It is written, 'I am Hashem your God' (Shemos 20:2), and in the work of Creation, 'Let there be light, and there was light' (Bereishis 1:3) — this is the faith of the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called 'light.'"

113.label: Rosh Hashanah 32a
113.rest: — "The 'And He said's of the Creation account are nine! — 'Bereishis' is also an utterance, as it is written, 'By the word of Hashem the heavens were made' (Tehillim 33:6)." Rashi: although "and He said" is not written there, it is as though it were, for heaven too was created by speech and not by hand.

114.label: Chagigah 12a
114.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said: With the light that the Holy One created on the first day, Adam could see from one end of the world to the other. When the Holy One looked at the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion and saw that their deeds were corrupt, He arose and hid it from them."

115.label: Zohar III 233b (Pinchas)
115.rest: — "'Hear, O Israel, Hashem our God, Hashem' (Devarim 6:4): these are the five leaves of the rose; 'One' — this is the main stem and root of all, to which those thirteen leaves are bound. The secret of the testimony to the Unity: five words, 'Shema Yisrael Hashem Elokeinu Hashem,' are five strong leaves of the rose, root and foundation, bound to it; this is 'One,' the main stem and root of all."

116.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
116.rest: — "Chesed is the right arm, Gevurah the left arm, Tiferes the body, Netzach and Hod the two thighs, Yesod the completion of the body, the sign of the holy covenant; Malchus is the mouth — we call it the Oral Torah."

117.label: Rashi, Shemos 31:3
117.rest: — "'With wisdom' — what a person hears from others and learns; 'and with understanding' — that he understands a matter from his own heart, from what he has learned; 'and with knowledge' — ruach hakodesh."

118.label: Tanchuma, Noach 3
118.rest: — "'A great light' (Yeshayahu 9:1) — the light that was created on the first day, which the Holy One, blessed be He, hid away for those who toil in the Oral Torah by day and by night, in whose merit the world stands, as it says, 'If not for My covenant day and night…' (Yirmeyahu 33:25). Which covenant is practiced by day and by night? This is Talmud."

119.label: Zohar III 131a (Idra Rabba)
119.rest: — "We learned: all the hairs, both of the head and of the beard, are white as snow… because they are the strength of strengths, to bring down those thirteen attributes [of mercy] from the Ancient of Ancients" — the tikkunim of Arich Anpin.

120.label: Shabbos 89b
120.rest: — “Rabbi Yitzchak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: If your sins are like these years that have been arranged and have come from the six days of creation until now, they shall become white as snow.” The Gemara expounds shanim as years rather than merely as scarlet. Rav Tzadok relates this wording to the divine ordering of history and to the transformation accomplished by repentance.

121.label: Zohar II 184a, Tetzaveh
121.rest: — “There is no light except that which emerges from within darkness; for when this side is subdued, the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted above.”

122.label: Bava Kamma 55a
122.rest: — “Rabbi Yehoshua said: One who sees tet in his dream has a favorable sign.... Rather, it is because Scripture first opened with it for good: from ‘In the beginning’ until ‘God saw the light,’ tet is not written.” The Gemara discusses tet’s first occurrence in tov. Rav Tzadok applies that principle to qof’s first occurrence in vayikra in Genesis 1:5.

123.label: Zohar I 2b (Introduction)
123.rest: — "The letter tes came before Him and said: 'Create the world with me, for through me You are called good (tov) and upright.' He said to it: 'I will not create the world with you, for your goodness is hidden and concealed within you, as it says, "How great is Your goodness which You have hidden for those who fear You" (Tehillim 31:20). Since it is hidden within you, it has no portion in this world that I wish to create, but in the World to Come.'"

124.label: Eichah Rabbah 1:51
124.rest: — A Jew was plowing when his ox lowed. An Arab passing by said to him: Son of Yehudah, unyoke your ox, for the Temple of the Jews has been destroyed. It lowed a second time; he said: Yoke your ox, for the redeemer of the Jews has been born — on that very day.

125.label: Zohar III, Pinchas
125.rest: — "Five strong ones that surround it — these are the fifty gates."

126.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 36, 77b
126.rest: — "Two thousand years of tohu — 'and the earth was tohu'; two thousand of Torah — 'and the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters' (Bereishis 1:2), and water means nothing but Torah; 'the face of the waters' — its two faces, the positive and the negative commandments, white and red, right and left… 'Let there be light' — this is Pesach, the light of the fourteenth; 'and there was light' — this is Rosh Hashanah."

127.label: Bava Basra 8a
127.rest: — "'Though they study (yisnu) among the nations, now I will gather them; and they shall be relieved a little from the burden of king and princes' (Hoshea 8:10). Ulla said: This verse was said in Aramaic: if they all study, now I will gather them; and if only a few of them, they will be relieved of the burden of king and princes."

128.label: Taanis 26b (Mishnah)
128.rest: — "'On the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart' (Shir HaShirim 3:11): 'the day of his wedding' — this is the Giving of the Torah." Rashi: this is Yom Kippur, on which the last tablets were given.

129.label: Rashi, Devarim 10:10
129.rest: — "'Like the first days' — just as the first [forty days] were in favor, so the last were in favor; but the middle ones were in anger."

130.label: Zohar III 11a (Vayikra)
130.rest: — "And so it is written of Moshe: 'Ehyeh' at first — the concealment of all: I am the One Who I am; afterward 'asher Ehyeh' — I am ready to be revealed; afterward the last 'Ehyeh' — this is when Imma is pregnant, and it is still hidden. When is it revealed? At the time it is written, 'Go and gather the elders of Israel and say to them: Hashem, the God of your fathers…' (Shemos 3:16)."

131.label: Zohar I 117a (Vayera)
131.rest: — "And in the six hundredth year of the sixth [millennium] the gates of wisdom above and the springs of wisdom below will be opened, and the world will be prepared to enter the seventh… and your sign: 'In the six hundredth year of Noach's life… all the springs of the great deep were split open' (Bereishis 7:11)."

132.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pesach Eliyahu)
132.rest: — "They are called in this arrangement: Chesed, the right arm; Gevurah, the left arm; Tiferes, the body; Netzach and Hod, the two thighs; Yesod, the completion of the body, the sign of the holy covenant; Malchus, the mouth — we call it the Oral Torah."

133.label: Zohar I 207a (Vayigash)
133.rest: — "What is 'heavens'? The secret of the Patriarchs, and the secret of the Patriarchs is Yaakov, who includes them all, for Yaakov is the choicest of the Patriarchs... And because he ascended into the World to Come, one beautiful branch went out from him, from which all lights go out: Yosef the tzaddik, who gives sustenance to the whole world."

134.label: Bava Kamma 55a
134.rest: — "Rather, because Scripture opened with it for good at first: from 'Bereishis' until 'And God saw the light, that it was good (tov)' (Bereishis 1:4), no tes is written." Rashi: the first tes written in the Torah was said for good.

135.label: Sifrei, Devarim 53 (Re'eh)
135.rest: — "So Moshe said to Israel: You see the wicked prospering in this world? For two or three days they prosper, and in the end they come to nothing… You see the righteous suffering in this world? For two or three days they suffer, and in the end they rejoice, as it says, 'to do you good at your end' (Devarim 8:16)."

136.label: Tanchuma, Noach 3
136.rest: — "'According to (al pi) these words' (Shemos 34:27) — this is the Oral Torah, which is hard to learn and involves great suffering, and it is likened to darkness, as it says, 'The people who walk in darkness have seen a great light' (Yeshayahu 9:1): these are the masters of the Talmud, who have seen a great light, for the Holy One, blessed be He, illuminates their eyes in what is forbidden and permitted, impure and pure."

137.label: Zohar I 47b (Bereishis)
137.rest: — “‘And God finished on the seventh day’: this is Torah she'b'al peh, which is the seventh day.”

138.label: Bava Kamma 17a
138.rest: — "And water means only Torah, as it says, 'Ho, all who are thirsty, go to the water' (Yeshayahu 55:1)."

139.label: Zohar I 129a (Chayei Sarah)
139.rest: — "When he grew old and entered the supernal levels as is fitting, as it is written, 'And Avraham was old,' then he 'came into days' — into those supernal days, the days known in the secret of faith; 'and Hashem blessed Avraham with everything (bakol)' — from where all blessings and all good issue."

140.label: Zohar I 133b (Chayei Sarah)
140.rest: — "'And Avraham gave all that he had to Yitzchak' (Bereishis 25:5)… Here water was included in fire, and fire in water. At first fire was included in water — when? At the time he bound Yitzchak to execute judgment upon him; and now water was included in fire, so that all be the secret of supernal faith."

141.label: Rosh Hashanah 16a
141.rest: — "Why did the Torah say to pour water on the festival? The Holy One said: Pour water before Me on the festival, so that the rains of the year be blessed for you. And say before Me on Rosh Hashanah Malchiyos, Zichronos and Shofaros: Malchiyos — so that you crown Me King over you; Zichronos — so that your remembrance rise before Me for good; and with what? With the shofar."

142.label: Rosh Hashanah 11a
142.rest: — "On Rosh Hashanah the servitude of our fathers in Egypt ceased; in Nissan they were redeemed, and in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed" — the view of Rabbi Eliezer, who derives that the world was created in Tishrei from "Let the earth sprout grass… fruit tree" (Bereishis 1:11).

143.label: Sanhedrin 97b
143.rest: — "Rav said: All the ends have passed, and the matter depends only on teshuvah and good deeds… Rabbi Eliezer says: If Israel do teshuvah they are redeemed, and if not they are not redeemed. Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: If they do not do teshuvah they are not redeemed?! Rather, the Holy One sets up a king over them whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's, and Israel do teshuvah, and He brings them back to the good."

144.label: Taanis 15a
144.rest: — "Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I too say: not all are for light and not all are for gladness. The righteous are for light, and the upright for gladness: the righteous for light, as it is written, 'Light is sown for the righteous' (Tehillim 97:11); and the upright for gladness, as it is written, 'and for the upright of heart, gladness.'"

145.label: Shabbos 88a
145.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said: When Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear,' a heavenly voice went forth and said: Who revealed to My children this secret which the ministering angels use, as it is written, 'mighty in strength, who do His word, to hearken to the voice of His word' (Tehillim 103:20)? Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said: Why are Israel likened to an apple tree (Shir HaShirim 2:3)? Just as the apple's fruit comes before its leaves, so Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear.'"

146.label: Berachos 5a
146.rest: — "Whoever is able to occupy himself with Torah and does not, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings upon him ugly sufferings that disturb him, as it says, 'I was mute with silence, I was still from good, and my pain was stirred' (Tehillim 39:3) — and 'good' means only Torah, as it says, 'For I have given you good teaching; do not forsake My Torah' (Mishlei 4:2)."

147.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 36, 77b
147.rest: — "Two thousand years of tohu — 'and the earth was tohu'; two thousand of Torah — 'and the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters' (Bereishis 1:2), and water means nothing but Torah; 'the face of the waters' — its two faces, the positive and the negative commandments, white and red, right and left… 'Let there be light' — this is Pesach, the light of the fourteenth; 'and there was light' — this is Rosh Hashanah."

148.label: Bava Kamma 82a
148.rest: — "'And they went three days in the wilderness and found no water' (Shemos 15:22): the expounders of allusions said: Water means nothing but Torah, as it says, 'Ho, all who are thirsty, go to the water' (Yeshayahu 55:1)."

149.label: Zohar II 60a (Beshalach)
149.rest: — "And we have learned that the Holy One, blessed is He, is called Torah; 'water' means only Torah, and Torah means only the Holy One, blessed is He."

150.label: Sanhedrin 103b
150.rest: — "Our Rabbis taught: Menasheh would study fifty-five facets in Toras Kohanim, corresponding to the years of his reign; Achav, eighty-five; Yeravam, one hundred and three." Rashi: every year he would innovate in the book of Vayikra and expound it with his dialectic.

151.label: Pesachim 119a
151.rest: — "What is 'and for covering the Ancient (mechaseh atik)' (Yeshayahu 23:18)? This is one who covers the things that the Ancient of Days covered — and what are they? The secrets of the Torah. And some say: this is one who reveals the things that the Ancient of Days covered — and what are they? The reasons of the Torah." Rashi: the secrets are Maaseh Merkavah and Maaseh Bereishis.

152.label: Chagigah 13a
152.rest: — "'Honey and milk are under your tongue' (Shir HaShirim 4:11) — matters sweeter than honey and milk should remain under your tongue."

153.label: Shabbos 88a
153.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said: When Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear,' a heavenly voice went forth and said: Who revealed to My children this secret which the ministering angels use, as it is written, 'mighty in strength, who do His word, to hearken to the voice of His word' (Tehillim 103:20)? Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said: Why are Israel likened to an apple tree (Shir HaShirim 2:3)? Just as the apple's fruit comes before its leaves, so Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear.'"

154.label: Midrash Tanchuma, Kedoshim 2
154.rest: — “Like a king who betrothed a woman and said: Since you are consecrated to my name, I am king and you are queen.”

155.label: Tanchuma, Kedoshim 2
155.rest: — Before I created My world the ministering angels praised Me through you… When Yaakov came they said, "This is he," and He said, "Yes"; at that hour the Holy One sanctified Israel to His Name: "Since you were sanctified to My Name before I created the world, be holy as I am holy."

156.label: Zohar III 133b (Idra Rabba)
156.rest: — "The seventh tikkun: the hair breaks off, and two apples are seen, in the offering of fragrance, beautiful and fair to behold."

157.label: Zohar I (Vayeitzei) and elsewhere
157.rest: — "For through the arousal from below, there is arousal above, and from this each one is sustained as is fitting."

158.label: Tikkunei Zohar (77b)
158.rest: — "'Let there be light' — this is Pesach, the night of the fourteenth; 'and there was light' — Rosh Hashanah, of which it says 'and it was the day.'" These words stand in Tikkun 36 (77b); the printed reference says Tikkun 30.

159.label: Midrash Tehillim 80
159.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: We have nothing but the shining of Your face; save us and we shall be saved."

160.label: Eruvin 41a
160.rest: — “After Rabban Gamliel died, Rabbi Yehoshua entered to overturn his ruling. Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri stood and said: I see that the body follows the head! Throughout Rabban Gamliel's life we established the law according to him; now you wish to overturn his words? Yehoshua, we do not heed you, for the law has already been established according to Rabban Gamliel, and no one disputed the matter.” The proverb occurs in a dispute about maintaining an established ruling after a leader's death. Rav Tzadok applies its image to Rosh Chodesh as the head that directs the month.

161.label: Shabbos 88a
161.rest: — "'Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest': Why is Israel likened to an apple tree? To tell you: just as the apple tree's fruit comes before its leaves, so Israel put 'we will do' before 'we will hear.'" Rashi: its fruit buds before its leaves, unlike other trees.

162.label: Chullin 92a
162.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: This nation is likened to a vine: its branches are the householders; its clusters are the Torah scholars; its leaves are the amei ha'aretz; its tendrils are the empty ones in Israel… Let the clusters pray for the leaves, for were it not for the leaves, the clusters would not survive."

163.label: Sanhedrin 99b
163.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: Whoever teaches his fellow's son Torah, Scripture regards him as though he made him… Rabbi Elazar says: As though he made the words of Torah, as it says, 'And you shall keep the words of this covenant and do (make) them' (Devarim 29:8). Rava said: As though he made himself, as it says, 'and do them (osam)' — do not read osam but atem (yourselves)."

164.label: Sanhedrin 8a
164.rest: — “The section of inheritances was fit to be written through Moshe Rabbeinu, but the daughters of Tzelafchad merited that it be written through them. The section of the wood-gatherer was fit to be written through Moshe Rabbeinu, but the wood-gatherer incurred guilt, and it was written through him. This teaches that guilt is brought about through one who is guilty, and merit through one who is worthy.” The Gemara establishes that a particular person's merit can become the occasion for a Torah section's revelation. Rav Tzadok develops this into the individual's role in bringing his or her Torah-root into the world.

165.label: Yoma 28b
165.rest: — "Rav said: Avraham Avinu fulfilled the entire Torah, as it says, 'Because Avraham listened to My voice and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes and My Torahs' (Bereishis 26:5). Rav Shimi bar Chiya said to Rav: Perhaps only the seven mitzvos? — There was milah too! — Perhaps seven and milah? — If so, why 'My commandments and My Torahs'?"

166.label: Chagigah 14b
166.rest: — "Ben Azzai gazed and died; of him the verse says, 'Precious in the eyes of Hashem is the death of His pious ones' (Tehillim 116:15). Ben Zoma gazed and was harmed; of him the verse says, 'Have you found honey? Eat what suffices you, lest you be sated with it and vomit it' (Mishlei 25:16). Acher cut the shoots. Rabbi Akiva came out in peace."

167.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 41, 81a
167.rest: — In "Bereishis" are the letters of Tishrei, and this is the second arm, the second day; "He made (yashes) darkness His hiding place" (Tehillim 18:12): remove yashes from bereishis and reish remains — Rosh Hashanah.

168.label: Zohar III 100a (Emor)
168.rest: — "And Rivkah said to Yaakov her son… and she commanded him to awaken with his delicacies; and Yaakov awakened below, clothed in prayers and supplications, and 'the voice is the voice of Yaakov' (Bereishis 27:22) in that shofar that rises."

169.label: Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 583:2
169.rest: — "They eat the head of a ram, to say: May we be a head and not a tail, and in remembrance of the ram of Yitzchak."

170.label: Sanhedrin 37a
170.rest: — On the rows of students before the Sanhedrin: "But let him say to them: Until now I sat at the head, and now you seat me at the tail! Abaye said: They say to him: Be a tail to lions, and do not be a head to foxes."

171.label: Tanchuma, Nitzavim 2
171.rest: — "'Your heads, your tribes' (Devarim 29:9) — even though I appointed over you heads, elders and officers, you are all equal before Me, as it says, 'every man of Israel.' Another explanation: you are all guarantors for one another; even one righteous man among you — all of you stand in his merit."

172.label: Taanis 31a
172.rest: — "Ulla of Bira said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle dance for the righteous, and He will sit among them in Gan Eden, and each one will point with his finger, as it says, 'And it shall be said on that day: Behold, this is our God; we hoped to Him and He saved us… let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation' (Yeshayahu 25:9)."

173.label: Tikkunei Zohar (Introduction and elsewhere)
173.rest: — "And of them it is said, 'Your heads, your tribes, your elders and your officers, every man of Israel' (Devarim 29:9) — these are five; 'your little ones, your wives, and your convert… from the hewer of your wood to the drawer of your water' — these are five others": the ten levels of Israel corresponding to the ten sefiros, "your heads" first among them.

174.label: Zohar III 65b (Acharei Mos)
174.rest: — "The Yud at first is the totality of all, hidden on every side... The upper tip of the Yud alludes to Ayin (Nothingness)." Zohar III 10b (Vayikra): "The Yud of the holy Name is tied with three knots: one tip above, one below and one in the middle. The tip above is Kesser Elyon, highest of all the highest, head of all heads."

175.label: Zohar III 99b (Emor)
175.rest: — "Then the second sound rises, strong, to break and shatter the force of anger… and in this the one who blows must direct his heart and will to break the power and strength of harsh judgment, as it is written, 'Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah' (Tehillim 89:16)."

176.label: Kerisos 6a
176.rest: — "Abaye said: Now that you have said that an omen is meaningful, a person should make a habit of eating at the start of the year gourd, fenugreek, leek, beet and dates."

177.label: Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 583:1
177.rest: — "A person should make a habit of eating on Rosh Hashanah fenugreek, leek, beet, dates and gourd; and when he eats fenugreek he should say: May it be Your will that our merits increase…" Rema: "Some have the custom of eating a sweet apple in honey and saying: May a sweet year be renewed for us."

178.label: Zohar III 271b, Eikev (Ra’aya Mehemna)
178.rest: — “‘Come, eat of my bread’ — this is the Written Torah; ‘and drink of the wine I mixed’ — this is the wine of the Oral Torah.”

179.label: Beitzah 16a
179.rest: — "A person's sustenance is allotted to him from Rosh Hashanah… Rabbi Abahu said: What is the verse? 'Blow the shofar at the new moon, at the covered time for our festival day' (Tehillim 81:4) — which festival is it on which the moon is covered? This is Rosh Hashanah; and it is written, 'For it is a statute for Israel, a judgment of the God of Yaakov' (81:5)."

180.label: Bava Kamma 82a
180.rest: — "'They went three days in the wilderness and found no water' (Shemos 15:22): the expounders of reshumos [Rashi: verses] said: Water means only Torah, as it says, 'Ho, all who thirst, go to the water.' Since they went three days without Torah they grew weary, so the prophets among them enacted that they read the Torah on Shabbos, Monday and Thursday."

181.label: Zohar II 60a (Beshalach)
181.rest: — "And we have learned that the Holy One, blessed is He, is called Torah; 'water' means only Torah, and Torah means only the Holy One, blessed is He."

182.label: Mechilta, Beshalach, Shirah 3
182.rest: — "'This is my God and I will glorify Him' (Shemos 15:2). Rabbi Eliezer says: From where do you say that a maidservant saw at the Sea what Yeshayahu and Yechezkel did not see? For it says, 'and through the prophets I was imaged' (Hoshea 12:11)… When the Holy One, blessed be He, was revealed at the Sea, no one needed to ask, 'Which is the King?'"

183.label: Mechilta, Beshalach, Shirah 3
183.rest: — "'This is my God' (Shemos 15:2): Rabbi Eliezer says: From where do you say that a maidservant saw at the sea what Yeshayahu and Yechezkel did not see?…"

184.label: Zohar III 153a (Behaaloscha)
184.rest: — "'And they embittered their lives with hard labor' (Shemos 1:14) — with kushya, difficult questioning; 'with mortar (chomer)' — with kal vachomer; 'and with bricks (levenim)' — with the clarification (libun) of halachah."

185.label: Mechilta, Beshalach, Vayassa 1
185.rest: — "'There He set for them a statute and a judgment' (Shemos 15:25): 'a statute' — this is Shabbos; 'and a judgment' — this is honoring father and mother."

186.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 36 (77b)
186.rest: — "'Let there be light' — this is Pesach, the night [or] of the fourteenth; 'and there was light' — Rosh Hashanah, of which it is said 'and it was [vayehi] the day'; here vayehi and there vayehi, and everywhere vayehi is a term of distress." Or l'arba'ah asar is the Mishnah's term for the night of the fourteenth (Pesachim 2a).

187.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17b (Pasach Eliyahu)
187.rest: — "But not that You have a known Tzedek, which is judgment, nor a known Mishpat, which is mercy, nor any of these attributes at all."

188.label: Zohar III 113b (Bechukosai)
188.rest: — "'Fortunate are those who keep justice (mishpat), who do charity (tzedakah) at all times' (Tehillim 106:3): 'who do tzedakah' — this is the Holy One, blessed be He; as it were, one makes Him."

189.label: Pesachim 68b
189.rest: — "One verse says, 'an assembly to Hashem your God,' and one verse says, 'an assembly shall it be to you.' Rabbi Eliezer holds: either all of it for Hashem or all of it for you; Rabbi Yehoshua holds: divide it — half for Hashem and half for you." The Gemara continues: all agree that on Atzeres (Shavuos) "for you" is also needed. Rashi: that one rejoices on it with food and drink.

190.label: Beitzah 15b
190.rest: — "Rabbi Eliezer says: A person has on Yom Tov only either eating and drinking or sitting and learning. Rabbi Yehoshua says: Divide it: half for Hashem and half for you."

191.label: Tosafos, Beitzah 15b (s.v. o)
191.rest: — On the story of Rabbi Eliezer, who expounded the laws of Yom Tov all day and on parting told his students, "Go, eat rich foods and drink sweet drinks" (Nechemiah 8:10): Tosafos ask, but Rabbi Eliezer holds that Yom Tov is "either entirely for Hashem or entirely for you"!

192.label: Eruvin 13b
192.rest: — "For two and a half years Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel disputed: these say, It would have been better for man not to have been created than to have been created; and these say, It is better for man to have been created than not to have been created. They took a count and concluded: It would have been better for man not to have been created; now that he has been created, let him examine his deeds — some say, let him weigh his deeds."

193.label: Tikkunei Zohar 69a
193.rest: — "…bound to the Tree of Life, and not to the Tree of Death, which is the vine through which Adam HaRishon sinned; for one said it was wheat and one said it was a vine, and all is true."

194.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 39
194.rest: — "Just as the shofar of the Holy One is whole, so the shofar of Rosh Hashanah must be whole. Why? Because on Rosh Hashanah they are redeemed from the Angel of Death… And why do Israel sound the shofar on Rosh Hashanah? So that the Holy One will judge them with mercy and acquit them."

195.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 16b (s.v. kedei), citing the Yerushalmi
195.rest: — When the Satan hears the sound of the shofar the first time, he is alarmed; when he hears it a second time, he says: Surely this is the great shofar that is to be blown, and the time has come for me to be swallowed up.

196.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 32a (s.v. maschil baTorah)
196.rest: — And if you ask: everywhere it is implied that Nevi'im take precedence over Kesuvim, as it says (Megillah 31a), "written in the Torah, repeated in the Nevi'im, and tripled in the Kesuvim," yet here the verses of Kesuvim come first and then the Nevi'im! One may answer: because the verses of Tehillim, Mishlei and Iyov preceded the Nevi'im.

197.label: Bava Basra 22a
197.rest: — "Abaye said: I punished him, for he would say to the Rabbis: Instead of gnawing bones at Abaye's house, come eat fat meat at Rava's house." Rashi: come and learn clear, ample halachos with Rava.

198.label: Avodah Zarah 5b
198.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Bena'ah: What is meant by 'Fortunate are you who sow beside all waters, who send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey' (Yeshayahu 32:20)? Fortunate are Israel: when they occupy themselves with Torah and acts of kindness, their inclination is delivered into their hand, and they are not delivered into the hand of their inclination… 'sowing' means only charity…, and 'water' means only Torah."

199.label: Berachos 5a–b
199.rest: — Whoever occupies himself with Torah and acts of kindness [and buries his children] is forgiven all his sins. The Gemara (5b) explains: "Granted Torah and kindness, as it is written, 'Through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned' (Mishlei 16:6): 'kindness' is acts of kindness… and 'truth' is Torah, as it is said, 'Buy truth and do not sell it.'"

200.label: Tanchuma, Toldos 1 (so too end of Vayechi)
200.rest: — "Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said: Great is peace, for the Torah recorded invented words for the sake of peace. Which? 'Thus shall you say to Yosef: Please, forgive the transgression of your brothers' (Bereishis 50:17) — and we do not find that [Yaakov] commanded any of these things."

201.label: Shevuos 16a
201.rest: — "Why did they not sanctify it? Because one may add to the city and to the courtyards only with a king, a prophet, the Urim VeTumim, the Sanhedrin of seventy-one, two thanksgiving offerings and song."

202.label: Sefer Yetzirah 6
202.rest: — "The heart in the soul is like a king in war."

203.label: Sanhedrin 38a
203.rest: — "Zerubavel — so called because he was sown (zarua) in Bavel; and he is Nechemiah ben Chachalyah."

204.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
204.rest: — "Chochmah is the brain within; Binah is the heart, and with it the heart understands."

205.label: Zohar II 184b (Tetzaveh)
205.rest: — "Come and see: the lower world stands always to receive, and it is called a precious stone; and the upper world gives to it only according to how it stands: if it stands with a shining face from below, so they shine upon it from above; and if it stands in sadness, they give it judgment correspondingly."

206.label: Rosh Hashanah 27a
206.rest: — "Like whom do we pray today, 'This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day'? Like Rabbi Eliezer, who said the world was created in Tishrei." Tosafos there (s.v. kemaan) explain that both views are the words of the living God: in Tishrei it arose in thought to create, and it was not created until Nissan.

207.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 27a (s.v. kemaan)
207.rest: — Both views are the words of the living God: in Tishrei it arose in His thought to create the world, and it was not actually created until Nissan.

208.label: Yevamos 121b
208.rest: — "Rabbi Abba said: Even so, his son died of thirst, as it says, 'And round about Him it storms greatly (nis'arah)' (Tehillim 50:3) — this teaches that the Holy One is exacting with those around Him to a hairsbreadth (se'arah)."

209.label: Zohar I 151a (Vayetzei)
209.rest: — "'Then Hashem shall be my God' (Bereishis 28:21) — even mercy, when I return in peace, I will set before me as judgment… for I serve before Him constantly."

210.label: Taanis 5b
210.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Yaakov Avinu did not die. He was asked: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed and the buriers buried? He answered: I am expounding a verse, as it says, 'And you, fear not, My servant Yaakov… for behold, I save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity' (Yirmeyahu 30:10) — it compares him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too he is alive." Rashi: he lives forever; they embalmed him because they thought he had died.

211.label: Yevamos 61a
211.rest: — "The graves of idolaters do not defile in a tent, as it says, 'And you, My flock, the flock of My pasture, you are adam' (Yechezkel 34:31) — you are called adam, and idolaters are not called adam."

212.label: Sukkah 55b
212.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said: These seventy bulls — corresponding to whom? Corresponding to the seventy nations. The single bull — why? Corresponding to the unique nation." Rashi: to atone for them, so that rain fall throughout the world.

213.label: Mechilta, Beshalach, Amalek 2
213.rest: — "Rabbi Eliezer said: The Holy One swore by His Throne of Glory that if a convert comes from any of the nations of the world, they accept him; but from Amalek and his house they do not accept him."

214.label: Zohar III 4a (Vayikra)
214.rest: — The blessings of the Amidah correspond to the supernal levels: "Chesed is the level of Avraham, and the two blessings correspond to it — one 'Magen Avraham'…" and so for each of the Avos.

215.label: Rema, Orach Chaim 1:1
215.rest: — "When a person takes to heart that the great King, the Holy One, blessed be He, whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and sees his deeds, as it says, 'Can a man hide in secret places that I shall not see him? says Hashem' (Yirmeyahu 23:24) — immediately awe and submission will come upon him, in dread of Hashem Yisbarach, and he will be ashamed before Him constantly."

216.label: Pesachim 88a
216.rest: — “Rabbi Elazar said: What is meant by 'Many peoples shall go and say: Come, let us ascend Hashem's mountain, to the house of the God of Yaakov'? Is He the God of Yaakov and not the God of Avraham and Yitzchak? Rather, it is unlike Avraham, in whose case 'mountain' is written: 'As it will be said today: On Hashem's mountain He will be seen'; and unlike Yitzchak, in whose case 'field' is written: 'Yitzchak went out to meditate in the field.' Rather, it is like Yaakov, who called it a house: 'He called the name of that place Beis El.'” The Gemara identifies the patriarchal places of prayer with the future Temple. Rav Tzadok relates its 'field' to the field beside Machpelah in the Zohar; that identification is his synthesis of the sources.

217.label: Sukkah 52a
217.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: A person's inclination renews itself against him every day, as it says, 'only evil all the day' (Bereishis 6:5). And Reish Lakish said: A person's inclination overpowers him every day and seeks to kill him… and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him, he could not withstand it."

218.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 55, 88b
218.rest: — "'God has gone up with the teruah' (Tehillim 47:6) — this is Rosh Hashanah, of which it is said, 'He does not look upon iniquity in Yaakov… Hashem his God is with him, and the teruah of the King is in him' (Bamidbar 23:21): here you have it — teruah is in Yaakov… 'Blow the shofar at the new moon' (Tehillim 81:4) — this is tekiah… Malchiyos — from the side of Malchus…; Zichronos — 'zachor' is for the male (zachar), and this is the brain."

219.label: Sukkah 52b
219.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: A person's inclination overpowers him every day and seeks to kill him… and were it not for the Holy One, blessed is He, Who helps him, he could not overcome it, as it says, 'Hashem will not abandon him into his hand' (Tehillim 37:33)." Rashi: "every day" — its evil increases daily.

220.label: Menachos 36b
220.rest: — "Our Rabbis taught: 'Your hand' (Shemos 13:16) — this is the left. You say the left; perhaps it is the right? The verse says, 'My hand too founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens' (Yeshayahu 48:13)" — "hand" said alongside "right hand" is the left.

221.label: Zohar II 175b (Terumah)
221.rest: — "'And the middle bar in the midst of the boards, bolting from end to end' (Shemos 26:28) — this is Yaakov… who holds this side and holds that side. What is 'a perfect man (ish tam)'? As the Targum renders, shelim — complete on both sides, toward Atika Kaddisha and toward Ze'eir Anpin, toward supernal Chesed and supernal Gevurah."

222.label: Zohar II 14b–15a (Shemos)
222.rest: — "He made Avraham in the secret of Chochmah, Yitzchak in the secret of Tevunah, and Yaakov in the secret of Da'as."

223.label: Berachos 24b
223.rest: — "One who makes his voice heard in his prayer is of those of little faith; one who raises his voice in his prayer is of the false prophets."

224.label: Sanhedrin 64a
224.rest: — "'And they cried out with a loud voice to Hashem their God' (Nechemiah 9:4). What did they say? … Woe, woe! This is the one who destroyed the House, burned the Sanctuary, killed the righteous and exiled Israel from their land, and still he dances among us! Did You give him to us for any reason but that we receive reward through him? We want neither him nor his reward."

225.label: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 3:4
225.rest: — "Even though the blowing of the shofar on Rosh Hashanah is a decree of Scripture, there is a hint in it, as if to say: Awake, you sleepers, from your sleep, and you who slumber, rouse yourselves from your slumber; search your deeds and return in teshuvah, and remember your Creator — you who forget the truth in the vanities of the time and err all your year in vanity and emptiness that neither profit nor save."

226.label: Shemos Rabbah 30:9 (and parallels)
226.rest: — "The ways of the Holy One are not like those of flesh and blood: a human being instructs others to do and does nothing himself; but the Holy One is not so — what He Himself does, He tells Israel to do and to keep."

227.label: Arachin 16b
227.rest: — "Until where is the extent of suffering? … even if he put his hand into his pocket to take out three coins and took out only two."

228.label: Zohar I 219b (Vayechi)
228.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah said: There is no sin in the world that has no teshuvah except this one, and there is no wicked person who does not see the face of the Shechinah except this one, as it is written, 'Evil shall not dwell with You' (Tehillim 5:5)."

229.label: Berachos 62b
229.rest: — Rabbi Elazar was saved when a Persian who had pushed him was killed by a serpent; he applied to it, "'And I will give man (adam) in your place' (Yeshayahu 43:4) — do not read adam but Edom."

230.label: Chagigah 15a
230.rest: — “He created righteous people and wicked people; He created Gan Eden and Gehinnom. Each person has two portions, one in Gan Eden and one in Gehinnom. If the righteous person merits, he takes his own portion and his fellow's portion in Gan Eden. If the wicked person is found guilty, he takes his own portion and his fellow's portion in Gehinnom.” Rav Tzadok interprets ‘his fellow’ through the correspondence of soul-roots and the separation of the good and evil that had become intermixed.

231.label: Zohar III 99b (Emor)
231.rest: — "With these sounds below Israel give strength to mercy from below, and the great shofar is aroused above; therefore we must prepare a shofar on this day and arrange sounds, with intent, in order to arouse that other shofar in which the sounds above are included."

232.label: Berachos 17a
232.rest: — “Master of the universe, it is revealed and known before You that our desire is to do Your will. What prevents us? The leaven in the dough and the subjugation of kingdoms. May it be Your will to save us from their hands, so that we may return to perform the statutes of Your will with a whole heart.” Rabbi Alexandri's prayer distinguishes Israel's underlying desire from the internal and external obstacles to its expression. Rav Tzadok uses that distinction in answering Amalek's accusation.

233.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 6, 22a
233.rest: — "They are not from the side of those of whom it is said, 'men of valor, God-fearing, men of truth, hating gain' (Shemos 18:21); rather, all of them cry out in prayer on Yom Kippur like dogs: Give, give us sustenance, forgiveness, atonement and life — 'inscribe us for life!' — and they are brazen like dogs."

234.label: Bava Basra 8a
234.rest: — "Rebbi opened his storehouses in years of drought. He said: Let masters of Scripture, Mishnah, Talmud, halachah and aggadah enter, but let amei ha'aretz not enter. Rabbi Yonasan ben Amram pushed his way in. He said to him: Rebbi, sustain me. He said: My son, have you read Scripture? He said: No. Have you learned Mishnah? He said: No. If so, with what shall I sustain you? He said: Sustain me like a dog and like a raven. He sustained him." Rashi: for the Holy One has pity on them.

235.label: Rosh Hashanah 10b–11a
235.rest: — "Rabbi Eliezer says: In Tishrei the world was created; in Tishrei the Patriarchs were born; in Tishrei the Patriarchs died; on Pesach Yitzchak was born; on Rosh Hashanah Sarah, Rachel and Chanah were remembered; on Rosh Hashanah Yosef went out of prison… In Nissan they were redeemed, and in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed. Rabbi Yehoshua says: In Nissan the world was created…; in Nissan they were redeemed, and in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed."

236.label: Rosh Hashanah 16b
236.rest: — "Rabbi Kruspedai said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Three books are opened on Rosh Hashanah: one of the completely wicked, one of the completely righteous, and one of the intermediate. The completely righteous are written and sealed immediately for life; the completely wicked are written and sealed immediately for death; the intermediate are held in suspense from Rosh Hashanah until Yom Kippur: if they merit, they are written for life; if they do not merit, they are written for death."

237.label: Rosh Hashanah 32a
237.rest: — "The 'And He said's of the Creation account are nine! — 'Bereishis' is also an utterance, as it is written, 'By the word of Hashem the heavens were made' (Tehillim 33:6)." Rashi: although "and He said" is not written there, it is as though it were, for heaven too was created by speech and not by hand.

238.label: Zohar III 79b (Acharei Mos)
238.rest: — "It is written of Chanah, 'And she prayed al Hashem' (I Shmuel 1:10) — 'al' (above), precisely, for children depend on the holy mazal."

239.label: Rosh Hashanah 27a
239.rest: — "Like whom do we pray today, 'This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day'? Like Rabbi Eliezer, who said the world was created in Tishrei." Tosafos there (s.v. kemaan) explain that both views are the words of the living God: in Tishrei it arose in thought to create, and it was not created until Nissan.

240.label: Rashi, Bereishis 1:1
240.rest: — "'God (Elokim) created' — and it does not say 'Hashem created,' for at first it arose in His thought to create it with the attribute of judgment; He saw that the world would not endure, and He put the attribute of mercy first and joined it to the attribute of judgment."

241.label: Avos 6:11
241.rest: — "Everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world, He created only for His glory, as it says, 'Everyone who is called by My Name, and for My glory I created him, I formed him, also I made him' (Yeshayahu 43:7); and it says, 'Hashem shall reign forever and ever' (Shemos 15:18)."
