242.label: Zohar III 290a (Idra Zuta, Haazinu)
242.rest: — “Because He is concealed and not revealed, He is not called ‘You’ but is called ‘He.’ … Atika Kadisha, who is concealed, is called ‘He.’”

243.label: Tanchuma, Chukas 8
243.rest: — "Things that were not revealed to Moshe were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues; 'and every precious thing his eye beheld' (Iyov 28:10) — this is Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues."

244.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
244.rest: — "Chochmah is the brain, which is thought within; Binah is the heart, and with it the heart understands; and of these two it is written, 'The hidden things belong to Hashem our God' (Devarim 29:28)."

245.label: Vayikra Rabbah 29:7
245.rest: — "Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina: A parable of a prince who had a case before his father. His father said to him: If you wish to be vindicated before me in judgment today, appoint so-and-so as your advocate. So the Holy One said to Israel: My children, if you wish to be vindicated before Me in judgment on this day, mention the merit of the fathers, and you will be vindicated. 'On the first (be'echad)' — this is Avraham, as it says, 'Avraham was one (echad)' (Yechezkel 33:24)."

246.label: Berachos 7b
246.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: From the day the Holy One created the world, there was no person who called the Holy One 'Master' until Avraham came and called Him Master, as it says, 'And he said: My Master, Hashem God, by what shall I know that I will inherit it?' (Bereishis 15:8)."

247.label: Zohar III 11b (Vayikra)
247.rest: — "The ninth is Kel Shaddai, who said to the world 'Enough (dai)'… for sufficiency comes to the world only from the Tzaddik, the foundation of the world. The tenth is Adnus, for 'the law of the kingdom is law' (dina d'malchusa dina), and this is to wage the King's wars in the world; this is the lower Gevurah, and this is Tzedek."

248.label: Rosh Hashanah 16a
248.rest: — "Why did the Torah say to pour water on the festival? The Holy One said: Pour water before Me on the festival, so that the rains of the year be blessed for you. And say before Me on Rosh Hashanah Malchiyos, Zichronos and Shofaros: Malchiyos — so that you crown Me King over you; Zichronos — so that your remembrance rise before Me for good; and with what? With the shofar."

249.label: Chullin 7b
249.rest: — Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair declined to eat at Rebbi's table, saying: "Israel are holy: there is one who wishes [to host] and does not have, and one who has and does not wish."

250.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 55, 88b
250.rest: — "'God has gone up with the teruah' (Tehillim 47:6) — this is Rosh Hashanah, of which it is said, 'He does not look upon iniquity in Yaakov… Hashem his God is with him, and the teruah of the King is in him' (Bamidbar 23:21): here you have it — teruah is in Yaakov… 'Blow the shofar at the new moon' (Tehillim 81:4) — this is tekiah… Malchiyos — from the side of Malchus…; Zichronos — 'zachor' is for the male (zachar), and this is the brain."

251.label: Yoma 34b
251.rest: — "What is 'one'? The choicest (meyuchad) of his flock."

252.label: Pesachim 56a
252.rest: — "Yaakov wished to reveal to his sons the end of days, and the Shechinah departed from him… His sons said to him: 'Hear, Israel, Hashem is our God, Hashem is One' — they said: Just as in your heart there is only One, so in our heart there is only One. At that moment Yaakov Avinu opened and said: Blessed is the Name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever."

253.label: Pesachim 50a
253.rest: — “‘And His name One’—is His name not One now? Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: The world to come is unlike this world. In this world it is written with Yud–Heh and read with Alef–Dalet; in the world to come all is one: It is read with Yud–Heh and written with Yud–Heh.” The Gemara contrasts the written four-letter Name with its substituted pronunciation. Rav Tzadok asks why the shorter Name can be pronounced while the complete Name is withheld, and answers through the unification represented by the letters.

254.label: Zohar III 230a (Pinchas, Ra'aya Meheimna)
254.rest: — "He is truth (emes), and She is faith (emunah)."

255.label: Zohar I 129a–b, Chayei Sarah
255.rest: — “Avraham drew near to Him, and this was his yearning all his days. Avraham did not draw near in one day or at one time; his deeds brought him near each day, from level to level, until he rose through his levels. When he grew old and entered the higher levels fittingly, it says, 'Avraham was old'; then he 'came into the days'—those supernal days, those days known in the mystery of faith. ... Fortunate are the masters of repentance, for in one hour, one day, one moment, they draw near to the Holy One, blessed be He, as even completely righteous people did not over many years.” The source explicitly interprets Avraham's age through entry into supernal days, reached through his life's deeds. The maamar reads that attainment as purification of his attribute up to its highest root; its discussion of renewed Torah exertion draws on the same ascent.

256.label: Zohar I 219a (Vayechi)
256.rest: — "Rabbi Shimon said: We have learned that the Holy One has two children, one male and one female. The male He gave to Yaakov, as it is written, 'My son, My firstborn, Israel'… The daughter He gave to Avraham, as it is written, 'And Hashem blessed Avraham with everything (bakol)' — Avraham had a daughter, and Bakol was her name."

257.label: Zohar III 98b (Emor)
257.rest: — "'In the seventh month, on the first of the month' (Vayikra 23:24): Rabbi Yitzchak opened: 'Blow the shofar at the new moon, at the covered time for our festival day' (Tehillim 81:4). Fortunate are Israel, for the Holy One drew them near to Him out of all the idolatrous nations and chose them, and from a distant place He drew them near, as it is written, 'Your fathers dwelt of old beyond the River' (Yehoshua 24:2) — to show that from a distant place He chose them and drew them near."

258.label: Sanhedrin 38a
258.rest: — "'Wisdom has built her house' (Mishlei 9:1) — this is the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He, Who created the whole world with wisdom; 'she has hewn out her seven pillars' — these are the seven days of Creation; 'she has slaughtered her meat, mixed her wine, and also set her table' — these are the seas and rivers and all the needs of the world."

259.label: Zohar II (Terumah, Raaya Mehemna)
259.rest: — "When [the lower Shechinah] receives from Binah, which is the World to Come, then certainly a person has no knowledge of the Holy One or of any of His attributes until he enters through this gate, of which it is said, 'This is the gate to Hashem' (Tehillim 118:20)."

260.label: Raaya Mehemna, Zohar III 232a (Pinchas)
260.rest: — "… vav, the son of yud-hei, from Binah… 'Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding' (Mishlei 4:5) — for there is no kaneh lower than both of them, which are yud — Chochmah, hei — Binah."

261.label: Menachos 29b
261.rest: — "As Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai expounded: These are the two worlds that the Holy One created, one with hei and one with yud… This world was created with hei and the World to Come with yud."

262.label: Zohar Chadash, Toldos
262.rest: — Corresponding to the seven supernal days, He created on earth seven true tzaddikim, each corresponding to his day, the fathers of the world: Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov, Yosef, Moshe, Aharon and David; they are called "the ancient mountains," for they depend on those seven supernal days — the six days of Bereishis and the seventh that stands before them; as it says, "And the house of David shall be like God" (Zecharyah 12:8).

263.label: Shabbos 88a
263.rest: — "'And they stood at the foot of the mountain' (Shemos 19:17): Rav Avdimi bar Chama bar Chasa said: This teaches that the Holy One held the mountain over them like a barrel and said to them: If you accept the Torah, good; and if not, there will be your burial. Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: From here there is a great protest against the Torah. Rava said: Even so, they accepted it again in the days of Achashverosh, as it is written, 'The Jews established and accepted' (Esther 9:27) — they established what they had already accepted."

264.label: Rashi, Yehoshua 24
264.rest: — Yehoshua saw that they would one day protest in the days of Yechezkel and say, "Let us be like the nations"; therefore he made it weighty upon them now. "Do not say: what we accepted in the days of Moshe was in order to enter the Land — behold, in Yehoshua's days you had already entered, and you accepted it."

265.label: Shabbos 88a
265.rest: — “Nevertheless, they accepted it anew in the days of Achashveirosh.”

266.label: Megillah 14a
266.rest: — "Rava said: Granted there, 'Praise, servants of Hashem' (Tehillim 113:1) — and not servants of Pharaoh; but here, 'Praise, servants of Hashem' — and not servants of Achashverosh? We are still servants of Achashverosh!"

267.label: Kiddushin 18a
267.rest: — "Rav Chiya bar Avin said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: An idolater inherits his father by Torah law, as it is written, 'For I have given Mount Seir to Esav as an inheritance' (Devarim 2:5). But perhaps an apostate Jew is different! Rather, from here: 'For I have given Ar to the children of Lot as an inheritance' (Devarim 2:9)."

268.label: Gittin 56a
268.rest: — Nero Caesar, seeing the signs that the Holy One wished to destroy His House, "fled and converted, and Rabbi Meir descended from him."

269.label: Avodah Zarah 9a
269.rest: — "It was taught in the school of Eliyahu: The world is to exist for six thousand years: two thousand years of tohu, two thousand years of Torah, two thousand years the days of Mashiach." The Gemara reckons the two thousand years of Torah from Avraham's time in Charan.

270.label: Yoma 28b
270.rest: — "Rav said: Avraham Avinu fulfilled the entire Torah, as it says, 'Because Avraham listened to My voice and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes and My Torahs' (Bereishis 26:5). Rav Shimi bar Chiya said to Rav: Perhaps only the seven mitzvos? — There was milah too! — Perhaps seven and milah? — If so, why 'My commandments and My Torahs'?"

271.label: Zohar III 80b–81a (Kedoshim)
271.rest: — "He said to him: 'The fear of Hashem' is written, not Torah! He answered: So it is indeed, for the Torah comes from the side of Gevurah… as it is written, 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem' (Tehillim 111:10)." Yitzchak, the "Fear of Yitzchak," is the chariot of Gevurah.

272.label: Berachos 5b
272.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Granted Torah and kindness, as it is written, 'Through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned' (Mishlei 16:6): 'kindness' is acts of kindness… and 'truth' is Torah, as it is said, 'Buy truth and do not sell it' (Mishlei 23:23)."

273.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 16b (s.v. kedei), citing the Yerushalmi
273.rest: — When the Satan hears the sound of the shofar the first time, he is alarmed; when he hears it a second time, he says: Surely this is the great shofar that is to be blown, and the time has come for me to be swallowed up.

274.label: Zohar III 266b (Vaeschanan)
274.rest: — "'A great shofar will be sounded' (Yeshayahu 27:13): what does it matter whether it is great or small? Rather, it is that supernal shofar through which slaves always go out to freedom; this is the Yovel of the supernal Yovel, great and mighty; and when it is aroused, all the freedom of the worlds is aroused through it — and that is called 'the great shofar.'"

275.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a
275.rest: — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

276.label: Bava Basra 8a
276.rest: — "'Though they study (yisnu) among the nations, now I will gather them; and they shall be relieved a little from the burden of king and princes' (Hoshea 8:10). Ulla said: This verse was said in Aramaic: if they all study, now I will gather them; and if only a few of them, they will be relieved of the burden of king and princes."

277.label: Sanhedrin 86a
277.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: An anonymous Mishnah is Rabbi Meir; an anonymous Tosefta is Rabbi Nechemiah; an anonymous Sifra is Rabbi Yehudah; an anonymous Sifrei is Rabbi Shimon — and all of them follow Rabbi Akiva."

278.label: Eruvin 13b
278.rest: — “It was taught: His name was not Rabbi Meir, but Rabbi Nehorai. Why was he called Rabbi Meir? Because he illuminated the eyes of the Sages in halachah. And his name was not Nehorai, but Rabbi Nechemyah—or, some say, Rabbi Elazar ben Arach. Why was he called Nehorai? Because he enlightened the eyes of the Sages in halachah.” The statement establishes Rabbi Meir's extraordinary illuminating power in Torah. Rav Tzadok emphasizes that this greatness did not make vigilance unnecessary.

279.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 33b (s.v. shiur)
279.rest: — The Aruch explains (entry arav) that those who are stringent sound thirty while seated, thirty in the silent prayer and thirty in the repetition, corresponding to the hundred cries that Sisera's mother cried; and ten more at the end of the whole prayer — a hundred in all.

280.label: Rosh Hashanah 33b
280.rest: — "Abaye said: In this they certainly disagree: it is written, 'It shall be a day of teruah for you' (Bamidbar 29:1), and we translate, 'a day of yevava'; and it is written of Sisera's mother, 'Through the window she looked forth and wailed (vateyabev), the mother of Sisera' (Shoftim 5:28). One master holds it is groaning, and one master holds it is wailing."

281.label: Asarah Maamaros (Rama MiPano), Maamar Chikur Din 5:11
281.rest: — Shemaya and Avtalyon came from Sancheriv, and Rabbi Akiva from Sisera; the final letters of "Light is sown for the tzaddik and for the upright of heart, joy" (Tehillim 97:11) spell his name, for he is of the foundation of the Oral Torah, from its source in the supernal Pele.

282.label: Nazir 23b
282.rest: — "'Blessed above women be Yael, the wife of Chever the Keini; above women in the tent she shall be blessed' (Shoftim 5:24) — who are the women in the tent? Sarah, Rivkah, Rachel and Leah."

283.label: Zohar III 231b (Pinchas)
283.rest: — "'Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah' (Tehillim 89:16): it does not say 'who hear' or 'who blow' the teruah, but 'who know' the teruah — for the wise who dwell in the air of the Holy Land know the teruah, the secret of the teruah… and all who know the secret of the teruah will come near to walk in the light of the face of the Holy One; and this is the primordial light that the Holy One hid away for the righteous."

284.label: Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 3
284.rest: — “The Holy One, blessed be He, did not write in the Torah, 'for the sake of these words,' or 'on account of these words,' or 'because of these words,' but rather 'by the mouth of these words.' This is the Oral Torah, which is difficult to learn and involves great hardship; it is compared to darkness, as it is said: 'The people walking in darkness have seen a great light.' These are the masters of Talmud, who have seen a great light, for the Holy One, blessed be He, enlightens their eyes regarding what is forbidden and permitted, impure and pure.” The verse is Isaiah 9:1 in the Hebrew numbering. The Midrash explicitly connects the darkness of demanding study with the light of discerning Torah.

285.label: Zohar III 98b (Emor)
285.rest: — "'In the seventh month, on the first of the month' (Vayikra 23:24): Rabbi Yitzchak opened: 'Blow the shofar at the new moon, at the covered time for our festival day' (Tehillim 81:4). Fortunate are Israel, for the Holy One drew them near to Him out of all the idolatrous nations and chose them, and from a distant place He drew them near, as it is written, 'Your fathers dwelt of old beyond the River' (Yehoshua 24:2) — to show that from a distant place He chose them and drew them near."

286.label: Makkos 24a
286.rest: — "Yeshayahu came and based them on two, as it says, 'Keep justice and do righteousness' (Yeshayahu 56:1). Amos came and based them on one, as it says, 'Seek Me and live' (Amos 5:4)… Rather, Chavakuk came and based them on one, as it says, 'And the righteous one shall live by his faith' (Chavakuk 2:4)."

287.label: Bechoros 55b
287.rest: — "'And the fourth river is the Pras' (Bereishis 2:14)" — it is the Pras spoken of from the beginning, from the six days of Creation.

288.label: Sukkah 20a
288.rest: — “At first, when the Torah was forgotten from Yisrael, Ezra came up from Bavel and established it.”

289.label: Sukkah 44a
289.rest: — "But Rabbi Yochanan said: 'What I called yours is really theirs!'" Rashi: Rabbi Yochanan had thought the Torah belonged to the people of Eretz Yisrael, who were never exiled; but when Rav Kahana came he saw that it belongs to the people of Bavel, for although they were exiled, the "craftsmen and smiths" who went into exile with Yechonyah — mighty in the battle of Torah — preserved it.

290.label: Zohar III 99b (Emor)
290.rest: — "When people return from their sins, they must sound the shofar below, and that voice rises above; then another, supernal shofar is aroused, mercy is aroused and judgment departs. We must show an action with the shofar to arouse that other shofar."

291.label: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 3:4
291.rest: — "Even though the blowing of the shofar on Rosh Hashanah is a decree of Scripture, there is a hint in it, as if to say: Awake, you sleepers, from your sleep, and you who slumber, rouse yourselves from your slumber; search your deeds and return in teshuvah, and remember your Creator — you who forget the truth in the vanities of the time and err all your year in vanity and emptiness that neither profit nor save."

292.label: Zohar III 99a–b (Emor)
292.rest: — "When that supernal shofar, in which is the light of all, departs and does not shine upon the children, then judgment is aroused… and this shofar is called the ram of Yitzchak, the might of Yitzchak, the praise of the Avos; when that great shofar departs and does not nurse the children, Yitzchak is strengthened and prepared for judgment in the world."

293.label: Shabbos 89b
293.rest: — "Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonasan: What is meant by 'For You are our Father, for Avraham did not know us, and Israel does not recognize us; You, Hashem, are our Father, our Redeemer from of old is Your Name' (Yeshayahu 63:16)? In the future the Holy One will say to Avraham: Your children have sinned against Me. He will say before Him: Master of the world, let them be wiped out for the sanctification of Your Name…" — until Yitzchak pleads for them.

294.label: Rosh Hashanah 23b
294.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Between each one there were eight parsaos… But today they are much more! Abaye said: The roads have simply been blocked up for them." Rashi: and travelers go by a crooked way.

295.label: Sukkah 49a
295.rest: — "Rabbi Yosi says: The shissin were hollowed out and descended to the depths, as it says, 'Let me sing for my beloved… and He planted it with choice vines, and built a tower in its midst, and also hewed out a winepress in it' (Yeshayahu 5:1–2): 'and He planted it with choice vines' — this is the Beis HaMikdash; 'and built a tower in its midst' — this is the altar; 'and also hewed out a winepress in it' — these are the shissin."

296.label: Megillah 3a
296.rest: — "Since they did not see, why were they frightened? Even though they themselves did not see, their mazal saw."

297.label: Moed Katan 28a
297.rest: — "Rava said: Life, children and sustenance do not depend on merit; rather, the matter depends on mazal. For Rabbah and Rav Chisda were both righteous Rabbis: one master prayed and rain came, and the other master prayed and rain came."

298.label: Rosh Hashanah 10b–11a
298.rest: — "Rabbi Eliezer says: In Tishrei the world was created; in Tishrei the Patriarchs were born; in Tishrei the Patriarchs died; on Pesach Yitzchak was born; on Rosh Hashanah Sarah, Rachel and Chanah were remembered; on Rosh Hashanah Yosef went out of prison… In Nissan they were redeemed, and in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed. Rabbi Yehoshua says: In Nissan the world was created…; in Nissan they were redeemed, and in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed."

299.label: Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah 20
299.rest: — "The Holy One brought Sancheriv into the world only in the merit of Ashur, who was an upright man and held to the counsel of Avraham Avinu" [in separating from the builders of the Tower].

300.label: Menachos 110a
300.rest: — "Rav Shimi bar Chiya challenged Rav: 'From the rising of the sun to its setting My Name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to My Name' (Malachi 1:11)! He said to him: Shimi, is it you? They call Him 'the God of gods.'"

301.label: Ramban, Hasagos on Sefer HaMitzvos, Aseh 1
301.rest: — "This faith in this utterance is not wondrous nor far off… it is the acceptance of His kingship, faith in the Divine," as the Mechilta says on "You shall have no other gods before Me."

302.label: Pesachim 113b
302.rest: — "Six things were said of the horse: it loves immorality, loves war, has a haughty spirit, despises sleep, eats much and excretes little; and some say it even seeks to kill its master in battle."

303.label: Rosh Hashanah 29b
303.rest: — "Rabbi Levi bar Lachma said in the name of Rabbi Chama bar Chanina: One verse says, 'a Shabbos, a remembrance of teruah' (Vayikra 23:24), and one verse says, 'a day of teruah it shall be for you' (Bamidbar 29:1). There is no difficulty: here, when Yom Tov falls on Shabbos; there, when Yom Tov falls on a weekday."

304.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 29b (s.v. ha lav melachah)
304.rest: — "It is difficult: on the contrary! If it were a melachah no verse would be needed, since it is derived from 'you shall do no melachah'; it is because it is not a melachah that a verse is needed. And it seems to me: if it is not a melachah, it is obvious that it is not forbidden; but if it is a melachah, a verse is needed — for one might have thought it permitted, since it is written 'a day of blowing it shall be for you,' even on Shabbos."

305.label: Shabbos 20a
305.rest: — "They lower the Pesach offering [into the oven at nightfall]. Why? Because the members of the group are diligent (zerizin)."

306.label: Beitzah 11b
306.rest: — Replacing a bandage is permitted in the Mikdash, "because there is no shevus in the Mikdash."

307.label: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 3:4
307.rest: — "Even though the blowing of the shofar on Rosh Hashanah is a decree of Scripture, there is a hint in it, as if to say: Awake, you sleepers, from your sleep, and you who slumber, rouse yourselves from your slumber; search your deeds and return in teshuvah, and remember your Creator — you who forget the truth in the vanities of the time and err all your year in vanity and emptiness that neither profit nor save."

308.label: Taanis 8b
308.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: Sun on Shabbos is charity for the poor, as it says, 'And for you who fear My Name a sun of righteousness shall shine, with healing in its wings' (Malachi 3:20)." Rashi explains "those who fear My Name" as those who keep the Shabbos.

309.label: Yerushalmi, Demai 4:1
309.rest: — On the Mishnah that one may ask an untrustworthy seller on Shabbos whether produce was tithed and eat on his word, the Yerushalmi explains: the awe of Shabbos is upon the am ha'aretz, and he does not lie.

310.label: Zohar III 232a (Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas)
310.rest: — "Imma Ila'ah is tekiah from the side of Avraham, shevarim from the side of Yitzchak, teruah from the side of Yaakov; the lower Shechinah is the knot of them all — that is, kuf for tekiah, shin for shevarim, reish for teruah; and all of them are tripled toward the Shechinah."

311.label: Raaya Mehemna, Zohar III 109b (Behar)
311.rest: — As a man without a wife is half a body and the Shechinah does not rest upon him, so when the Holy One is not joined with the Shechinah in all Israel, the Cause of Causes does not rest there… "and when the Holy One draws near with His Shechinah, this verse will be fulfilled: 'On that day Hashem will be One and His Name One' (Zecharyah 14:9), and the Cause of Causes will rest upon them."

312.label: Zohar II 204a (Vayakhel)
312.rest: — “Shabbos: shin–bas. The shin is the secret of the three Avos, who unite with the only daughter, and she is crowned with them.”

313.label: Zohar III 99b (Emor)
313.rest: — "With these sounds below Israel give strength to mercy from below, and the great shofar is aroused above; therefore we must prepare a shofar on this day and arrange sounds, with intent, in order to arouse that other shofar in which the sounds above are included."

314.label: Eruvin 96a
314.rest: — "Rabbi Akiva says: One might think a person should put on tefillin on Shabbos and festivals; the verse says, 'And it shall be for you a sign upon your hand' (Shemos 13:9) — [days] that require a sign; these are excluded, for they themselves are a sign." Rashi: Shabbos and festivals are themselves a sign between the Holy One and Israel.

315.label: Zohar III 231b (Pinchas)
315.rest: — "'Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah' (Tehillim 89:16): it does not say 'who hear' or 'who blow' the teruah, but 'who know' the teruah — for the wise who dwell in the air of the Holy Land know the teruah, the secret of the teruah… and all who know the secret of the teruah will come near to walk in the light of the face of the Holy One; and this is the primordial light that the Holy One hid away for the righteous."

316.label: Rosh Hashanah 32a
316.rest: — "These ten Malchiyos — corresponding to what? Rebbi said: Corresponding to the ten praises that David said in the book of Tehillim… Rav Yosef said: Corresponding to the Ten Commandments… Rabbi Yochanan said: Corresponding to the ten utterances with which the world was created."

317.label: Zohar III 11b (Vayikra)
317.rest: — "Ten utterances for the act of Creation… ten utterances for the Giving of the Torah — the Ten Commandments. It is written, 'I am Hashem your G-d,' and in the act of Creation, 'Let there be light, and there was light.' This faith in the Holy One is called light: 'Hashem is my light' (Tehillim 27:1)." Yehi Or stands parallel to Anochi.

318.label: Rosh Hashanah 16a
318.rest: — "Why did the Torah say to pour water on the festival? The Holy One said: Pour water before Me on the festival, so that the rains of the year be blessed for you. And say before Me on Rosh Hashanah Malchiyos, Zichronos and Shofaros: Malchiyos — so that you crown Me King over you; Zichronos — so that your remembrance rise before Me for good; and with what? With the shofar."

319.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
319.rest: — "Kesser Elyon is the crown of kingship (Kesser Malchus), and of it is said, 'He declares the end from the beginning' (Yeshayahu 46:10); and it is the skull of the tefillin."

320.label: Zohar II 52b (Beshalach)
320.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: Then, when everything was illuminated as one, the sea performed supernal laws, and upper and lower were delivered into its hand; therefore all is as hard before the Holy One as the splitting of the Red Sea. Why? Because the splitting of the Red Sea depends on Atika."

321.label: Taanis 31a
321.rest: — "Ulla of Bira said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle dance for the righteous, and He will sit among them in Gan Eden, and each one will point with his finger, as it says, 'And it shall be said on that day: Behold, this is our God; we hoped to Him and He saved us… let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation' (Yeshayahu 25:9)."

322.label: Zohar III 290a (Idra Zuta, Haazinu)
322.rest: — “Because He is concealed and not revealed, He is not called ‘You’ but is called ‘He.’ … Atika Kadisha, who is concealed, is called ‘He.’”

323.label: Zohar III 79b (Acharei Mos)
323.rest: — "Rabbi Shimon said: It is written, 'And it shall be, from one month to its month and from one Shabbos to its Shabbos' (Yeshayahu 66:23) — why weigh one against the other? Because all ascend to one level, one is joined to the other, and the joy of one with the other is found only when the Holy Atika is revealed; and then there is joy for all."

324.label: Zohar III 231b (Pinchas)
324.rest: — "'Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah' (Tehillim 89:16): it does not say 'who hear' or 'who blow' the teruah, but 'who know' the teruah — for the wise who dwell in the air of the Holy Land know the teruah, the secret of the teruah… and all who know the secret of the teruah will come near to walk in the light of the face of the Holy One; and this is the primordial light that the Holy One hid away for the righteous."

325.label: Kiddushin 40a
325.rest: — "A good thought the Holy One joins to deed… Rav Assi said: Even if a person thought to do a mitzvah and was prevented and did not do it, Scripture regards him as though he did it."

326.label: Rosh Hashanah 27a
326.rest: — "Rava — some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi — said: What is the verse? 'With trumpets and the sound of the shofar sound a teruah before the King, Hashem' (Tehillim 98:6) — before the King, Hashem, we require trumpets and the sound of the shofar, but elsewhere, not."

327.label: Taanis 26b (Mishnah)
327.rest: — "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: There were no festive days for Israel like the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur, on which the daughters of Yerushalayim would go out in borrowed white garments, so as not to shame one who had none… And so it says, 'Go forth and gaze, O daughters of Tziyon, upon King Shlomo, upon the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart' (Shir HaShirim 3:11): 'on the day of his wedding' — this is the giving of the Torah; 'and on the day of the joy of his heart' — this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash, may it be rebuilt speedily in our days."

328.label: Zohar III 65b (Acharei Mos)
328.rest: — "Come and see: the yud at first is the sum of all, hidden on every side, its paths not opened, the sum of male and female; the upper crownlet (kotza) of the yud alludes to Ayin (Nothingness). Afterwards the yud brings forth that river which flows and goes out from it… 'And a river goes out from Eden' (Bereishis 2:10)."

329.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 36
329.rest: — "'In Your light we shall see light' (Tehillim 36:10) — what light does the Congregation of Israel await? This is the light of Mashiach."

330.label: Shabbos 118b
330.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: Had Israel kept the first Shabbos, no nation or tongue would have ruled over them… Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: Were Israel to keep two Shabbosos according to their law, they would immediately be redeemed, as it says, 'Thus says Hashem to the eunuchs who keep My Shabbosos' (Yeshayahu 56:4), and it is written after it, 'I will bring them to My holy mountain' (56:7)."

331.label: Sifrei, Haazinu 306
331.rest: — "Another explanation: 'Give ear (ha'azinu), O heavens' — because Moshe was close to the heavens, he said 'Give ear, O heavens'; and because he was far from the earth, he said 'and let the earth hear the words of my mouth.' Yeshayahu came and matched it: 'Hear, O heavens' (Yeshayahu 1:2) — for he was far from the heavens; 'and give ear, O earth' — for he was close to the earth."

332.label: Zohar III 232a (Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas)
332.rest: — "Imma Ila'ah is tekiah from the side of Avraham, shevarim from the side of Yitzchak, teruah from the side of Yaakov; the lower Shechinah is the knot of them all — that is, kuf for tekiah, shin for shevarim, reish for teruah; and all of them are tripled toward the Shechinah."

333.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 55, 88b
333.rest: — "'God has gone up with the teruah' (Tehillim 47:6) — this is Rosh Hashanah, of which it is said, 'He does not look upon iniquity in Yaakov… Hashem his God is with him, and the teruah of the King is in him' (Bamidbar 23:21): here you have it — teruah is in Yaakov… 'Blow the shofar at the new moon' (Tehillim 81:4) — this is tekiah… Malchiyos — from the side of Malchus…; Zichronos — 'zachor' is for the male (zachar), and this is the brain."

334.label: Zohar II 92b (Yisro)
334.rest: — "Zachor — a place that has no forgetting, and forgetting does not exist in it… but below there is forgetting, a place where remembering is needed."

335.label: Pesachim 23a
335.rest: — "Rav Shemaya said: There it is different, for the verse says 'your harvest' — your harvest shall be yours."

336.label: Rosh Hashanah 34a
336.rest: — "Rabbi Abahu instituted in Caesarea: tekiah, three shevarim, teruah, tekiah. Whichever way you look at it: if it is wailing, let him do tekiah-teruah-tekiah; and if it is groaning, let him do tekiah-shevarim-tekiah!"

337.label: Pesachim 66a
337.rest: — "They said to him: Rebbi, if one forgot and did not bring a knife on the eve of Shabbos, what is the law? He said to them: This halachah I heard and have forgotten; but leave it to Israel — if they are not prophets, they are the sons of prophets."

338.label: Zohar III 99b (Emor)
338.rest: — The first sound rises, splits the firmaments, reaches Avraham and rests upon his head, and he is aroused and prepares the Throne; the second, the strong one, breaks the harsh judgments and reaches the place of Yitzchak; the third rises, mercy is aroused, and it reaches the head of Yaakov, and Avraham and Yaakov take hold of Yitzchak, one on each side, so that his strength cannot go out.

339.label: Zohar III 232a (Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas)
339.rest: — "Imma Ila'ah is tekiah from the side of Avraham, shevarim from the side of Yitzchak, teruah from the side of Yaakov; the lower Shechinah is the knot of them all — that is, kuf for tekiah, shin for shevarim, reish for teruah; and all of them are tripled toward the Shechinah."

340.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 55, 88b
340.rest: — "'God has gone up with the teruah' (Tehillim 47:6) — this is Rosh Hashanah, of which it is said, 'He does not look upon iniquity in Yaakov… Hashem his God is with him, and the teruah of the King is in him' (Bamidbar 23:21): here you have it — teruah is in Yaakov… 'Blow the shofar at the new moon' (Tehillim 81:4) — this is tekiah… Malchiyos — from the side of Malchus…; Zichronos — 'zachor' is for the male (zachar), and this is the brain."

341.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 36
341.rest: — "'In Your light we shall see light' (Tehillim 36:10) — what light does the Congregation of Israel await? This is the light of Mashiach."

342.label: Berachos 34a
342.rest: — "Rabbi Chanina said: The first [blessings] are like a servant who sets out praise before his master; the middle ones are like a servant who requests a reward from his master; the last are like a servant who has received a reward from his master, takes his leave and goes."

343.label: Sanhedrin 91b
343.rest: — "So too the Holy One brings the soul, casts it into the body, and judges them together, as it says, 'He calls to the heavens above, and to the earth, to judge His people' (Tehillim 50:4): 'He calls to the heavens above' — this is the soul; 'and to the earth, to judge His people' — this is the body."

344.label: Tikkunei Zohar 13, 29a
344.rest: — “Yaakov is the image of the central pillar from the outside. But was not Moshe there? Rather, he was from the inner side: this one from the body, that one from the soul.”

345.label: Zohar II 92b (Yisro)
345.rest: — "Zachor — a place that has no forgetting, and forgetting does not exist in it… but below there is forgetting, a place where remembering is needed."

346.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 55, 88b
346.rest: — "'God has gone up with the teruah' (Tehillim 47:6) — this is Rosh Hashanah, of which it is said, 'He does not look upon iniquity in Yaakov… Hashem his God is with him, and the teruah of the King is in him' (Bamidbar 23:21): here you have it — teruah is in Yaakov… 'Blow the shofar at the new moon' (Tehillim 81:4) — this is tekiah… Malchiyos — from the side of Malchus…; Zichronos — 'zachor' is for the male (zachar), and this is the brain."

347.label: Rosh Hashanah 16b
347.rest: — "Rabbi Kruspedai said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Three books are opened on Rosh Hashanah: one of the completely wicked, one of the completely righteous, and one of the intermediate. The completely righteous are written and sealed immediately for life; the completely wicked are written and sealed immediately for death; the intermediate are held in suspense from Rosh Hashanah until Yom Kippur: if they merit, they are written for life; if they do not merit, they are written for death."

348.label: Avos 2:1
348.rest: — "Consider three things and you will not come into the hands of sin: know what is above you — an eye that sees, an ear that hears, and all your deeds are written in a book."

349.label: Chagigah 3a
349.rest: — “Rava expounded: What is meant by ‘How beautiful are your steps in sandals, daughter of the generous one’? How beautiful are Israel’s feet when they go up for the festival pilgrimage. ‘Daughter of the generous one’—the daughter of Avraham our father, who is called generous, as it is said, ‘The generous ones of the peoples gathered, the people of the God of Avraham.’ ‘The God of Avraham,’ and not the God of Yitzchak and Yaakov? Rather, the God of Avraham, who was the first of the converts.” The Gemara explains why this verse names Avraham particularly. Rav Tzadok compares this particular naming with the Zohar’s inclusive application to the patriarchs.

350.label: Berachos 5a
350.rest: — "'Good' means nothing but Torah, as it says, 'For I have given you good teaching; do not forsake My Torah' (Mishlei 4:2)."

351.label: Rosh Hashanah 32a
351.rest: — "[The ten verses of each blessing correspond to what?]… Rav Yosef said: Corresponding to the Ten Commandments that were said to Moshe at Sinai. Rabbi Yochanan said: Corresponding to the ten utterances with which the world was created."

352.label: Rosh Hashanah 31a
352.rest: — "On the sixth day they would say, 'Hashem reigns; He is clothed in majesty' (Tehillim 93:1), because He completed His work and reigned over them; on the seventh they would say, 'A psalm, a song for the Shabbos day' (Tehillim 92:1) — for the day that is entirely Shabbos."

353.label: Rosh Hashanah 16a
353.rest: — "Why did the Torah say to pour water on the festival? The Holy One said: Pour water before Me on the festival, so that the rains of the year be blessed for you. And say before Me on Rosh Hashanah Malchiyos, Zichronos and Shofaros: Malchiyos — so that you crown Me King over you; Zichronos — so that your remembrance rise before Me for good; and with what? With the shofar."

354.label: Rosh Hashanah 32a
354.rest: — "Ten utterances? They are nine! — 'Bereishis' is also an utterance, as it is written, 'By the word of Hashem the heavens were made' (Tehillim 33:6)."

355.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
355.rest: — "You are exalted above all the exalted, hidden from all the hidden; no thought can grasp You at all."

356.label: Shabbos 146a
356.rest: — "When the serpent came upon Chavah it injected impurity into her; Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai — their impurity ceased."

357.label: Zohar III 18b (Vayikra)
357.rest: — "I found in the book of Rav Hamnuna Saba, in the prayers of Rosh Hashanah, that he would say: the prayer and the sound of the shofar — that sound which the righteous man brings forth from his spirit and his soul through the shofar rises above; and on that day accusers stand above, and when that sound rises they are scattered."

358.label: Sanhedrin 59a
358.rest: — “Rabbi Yochanan said: A gentile who occupies himself with Torah is liable to death, as it is said: 'Moshe commanded us the Torah, an inheritance'—it is our inheritance, not theirs.” The same discussion cites Rabbi Meir: a gentile who studies Torah is like a High Priest, and explains that statement as referring to the seven commandments incumbent upon them. The passage therefore distinguishes Israel's covenantal Torah inheritance from the study appropriate to the nations' own obligations; it does not exclude that study.

359.label: Bava Basra 10b
359.rest: — "Rabbi Yehoshua answered: 'Righteousness exalts a nation' (Mishlei 14:34) — this is Israel…; 'and the kindness of the nations is sin' — all the charity and kindness that the idolatrous nations do is a sin for them, for they do it only so that their kingdom may endure, as it says, '…redeem your sins with charity… perhaps there will be a lengthening of your tranquility' (Daniel 4:24)."

360.label: Berachos 3a
360.rest: — "And not only this, but when Israel enter the synagogues and study halls and answer 'May His great Name be blessed,' the Holy One shakes His head and says: Fortunate is the King who is praised thus in His house! What is there for the Father who exiled His children, and woe to the children who were exiled from their Father's table."

361.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 41, 81a
361.rest: — In "Bereishis" are the letters of Tishrei, and this is the second arm, the second day; "He made (yashes) darkness His hiding place" (Tehillim 18:12): remove yashes from bereishis and reish remains — Rosh Hashanah.

362.label: Zohar I 135a (Midrash HaNe'elam, Toldos)
362.rest: — "'Let us rejoice and be glad in You' (Shir HaShirim 1:4) — and not in eating… and that feast prepared for the future, may we have a portion to enjoy of it; and this is the joy and the laughter. 'And these are the generations of Yitzchak' — that the righteous will laugh (yitzchaku) in the time to come. 'Avraham begot Yitzchak' — the merit of the soul begets this laughter and joy in the world."

363.label: Shabbos 31b
363.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said: The Holy One, blessed be He, created His world only so that they should fear Him, as it says, 'And God has made it so, that they should fear before Him' (Koheles 3:14)."

364.label: Avos 6:11
364.rest: — "Everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world, He created only for His glory, as it says, 'Everyone who is called by My Name, and for My glory I created him, I formed him, also I made him' (Yeshayahu 43:7); and it says, 'Hashem shall reign forever and ever' (Shemos 15:18)."

365.label: Kiddushin 32b
365.rest: — "Rav Ashi said: Even according to the one who says that a nasi who forgoes his honor, his honor is forgone — a king who forgoes his honor, his honor is not forgone, as it says, 'You shall surely set a king over you' (Devarim 17:15): that his awe be upon you."

366.label: Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah 3
366.rest: — "David the King further said: I feared out of my joy, and I rejoiced out of my fear, and my love rose above them all."

367.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
367.rest: — "Chochmah is the brain, which is thought within; Binah is the heart, and with it the heart understands; and of these two it is written, 'The hidden things belong to Hashem our God' (Devarim 29:28)."

368.label: Rosh Hashanah 26a
368.rest: — "Ulla said: This is the reason of the Rabbis [for disqualifying a cow's horn]: an accuser cannot become a defender." Rashi: like the gold of the Calf, the horn of a cow is an accuser, recalling the Calf. "And Rabbi Yosi will say to you… that applies within [the Holy of Holies], but this shofar is outside."

369.label: Zohar II 121a (Mishpatim)
369.rest: — "It is written, 'And wisdom (chochmah) — from where (me'ayin) shall it be found?' (Iyov 28:12): the Torah came forth from Chochmah, from the place called Kodesh; and Chochmah came forth from the place called Kodesh HaKodashim."

370.label: Zohar II, Beshalach 64b
370.rest: — “Rabbi Abba said: What is meant by ‘Is the Lord in our midst, or nothing?’ Were Israel fools who did not know this matter? Had they not seen the Divine Presence before them and the clouds of glory surrounding them? ... Rather, Rabbi Shimon said this: They wished to know the difference between the Ancient One, concealed beyond all concealment, who is called Nothing, and Zeir Anpin, who is called the Lord. ... Why, then, were they punished? Because they made a separation and put it to a test. They said: If it is this One, we will ask in one manner; if it is this One, we will ask in another manner. Therefore, immediately, ‘Amalek came.’” The Zohar interprets Israel's question at Massah as a question about the degree from which Divine governance was being revealed. It explicitly names the concealed Atika as Ayin.

371.label: Mishnah, Keilim 1:6
371.rest: — "There are ten levels of sanctity: the Land of Israel is holier than all the lands…" — rising, level by level, to the Holy of Holies.

372.label: Berachos 7a
372.rest: — "R. Yishmael ben Elisha said: Once I entered the innermost sanctum to offer incense, and I saw Achtriel Yah, Hashem of Hosts, seated on a high and exalted throne. He said to me: Yishmael My son, bless Me. I said: May it be Your will that Your mercy conquer Your anger… and that You deal with Your children with the attribute of mercy. And He nodded His head to me."

373.label: Zohar II 54a, Beshalach
373.rest: — “Rabbi Abba said: I considered all the praises with which they praised the Holy One, blessed be He, and all began with ‘Then’: ‘Then Solomon said’; ‘Then Joshua spoke’; ‘Then Israel sang.’ Why? All the miracles and mighty deeds done for Israel occur when the light of the Holy Ancient One shines in His crowns, engraved and marked in az—in the alef. The alef pierces the darkness and illumines every side. When the alef's illumination joins and reaches the zayin—what is the zayin? 'Hashem's sword is filled with blood'—then He performs miracles and mighty deeds, because alef has joined with zayin. This is song, song on every side; this is 'Then Moshe sang.'” The Zohar reads az, 'then,' through its letters, alef and zayin. Rav Tzadok applies the same joining of supernal illumination with the lower levels to the future 'Then our mouth shall be filled with laughter.'

374.label: Zohar III 224a (Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas)
374.rest: — "Shemirah is certainly in the heart… therefore 'Shamor' is in the heart and not in any other place; and remembrance (zechirah) is in the male, in the brain that rides upon and rules the heart, and there is no remembrance except in the brain. Therefore 'Zachor' is for the male and 'Shamor' for the female."

375.label: Zohar II 92b (Yisro)
375.rest: — "Zachor — a place that has no forgetting, and forgetting does not exist in it… but below there is forgetting, a place where remembering is needed."

376.label: Zohar III 65b (Acharei Mos)
376.rest: — "The Yud at first is the totality of all, hidden on every side... The upper tip of the Yud alludes to Ayin (Nothingness)." Zohar III 10b (Vayikra): "The Yud of the holy Name is tied with three knots: one tip above, one below and one in the middle. The tip above is Kesser Elyon, highest of all the highest, head of all heads."

377.label: Rosh Hashanah 26a
377.rest: — Against the rule that an accuser cannot become a defender, the Gemara raises the blood of the bull brought into the Holy of Holies, and answers: since it has changed, it has changed.

378.label: Zohar II 52a (Beshalach)
378.rest: — "Rabbi Yeisa said: I found this secret in the Tekiata of Rav in Bavel, of Rav Hamnuna Saba: three times 'Uvechein' — Uvechein, Uvechein, Uvechein — corresponding to these three; and so is the order."

379.label: Pri Etz Chaim, Shaar Rosh Hashanah 7
379.rest: — "'Uvechein yiskadash' corresponds to Avraham, who sanctified His Name, may He be blessed, in the world — Chesed, the letters of the verse 'Vayisa'; 'Uvechein ten pachdecha' — this is the Fear of Yitzchak, Gevurah, corresponding to the seventy-two letters of the verse 'Vayavo,' which is read in reverse; 'Uvechein ten kavod' — corresponding to Yaakov, who said, 'Blessed is the Name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever.'"

380.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 39
380.rest: — "Be careful to take shofars on Rosh Hashanah and sound a teruah before the Holy One, and He will have mercy through them and vindicate you in judgment. From where? From what we read: 'Sing joyously to God our strength; shout to the God of Yaakov' (Tehillim 81:2). Thus Rabbi Tanchuma bar Abba opened: 'He has not beheld iniquity in Yaakov' (Bamidbar 23:21) — why did Bilam mention Yaakov, and not Avraham or Yitzchak? Because he saw that from Avraham came forth dross — Yishmael and the sons of Keturah."

381.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 40
381.rest: — "For thus I arranged for you that you blow the shofar on Rosh Hashanah, so that you tremble at the blowing of the shofar and prepare yourselves for teshuvah, as the prophet said, 'Shall a shofar be blown in a city and the people not tremble?' (Amos 3:6)."

382.label: Avodah Zarah 19a
382.rest: — "'Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem' — R. Amram said in the name of Rav: Fortunate is one who repents while he is still a man." Rashi: 'while he is a man' — in his youthful strength, hurrying to know his Creator before old age.

383.label: Rema, Orach Chaim 1:1
383.rest: — "When a person takes to heart that the great King, the Holy One, blessed be He, whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and sees his deeds, as it says, 'Can a man hide in secret places that I shall not see him? says Hashem' (Yirmeyahu 23:24) — immediately awe and submission will come upon him, in dread of Hashem Yisbarach, and he will be ashamed before Him constantly."

384.label: Berachos 17a
384.rest: — "Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that our will is to do Your will. And who prevents us? The leaven in the dough and the subjugation to the kingdoms." Rashi: the leaven in the dough is the evil inclination in our hearts, which sours us.

385.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 55, 88b
385.rest: — "The Central Pillar includes both of them — Hashem is His Name; and it is the sound of the shofar from the side of Imma Ila'ah, who is the shofar: tekiah is from the side of the right, shevarim from the side of the left, and the chain, which is teruah, from the side of both of them."

386.label: Pesachim 56a
386.rest: — "Yaakov wished to reveal the End to his sons, and the Shechinah departed from him. He said: Perhaps, Heaven forbid, there is a flaw in my bed… His sons said to him: 'Hear, Yisrael, Hashem is our God, Hashem is One.' They said: Just as in your heart there is only One, so in our heart there is only One. At that moment Yaakov said: Baruch Shem kevod malchuso l'olam va'ed." Rashi: they said "Shema Yisrael" to their father.

387.label: Sukkah 52a
387.rest: — "Yeshayahu called it 'stumbling block,' as it says, 'Pave, pave, clear the way, remove the stumbling block from the way of My people' (Yeshayahu 57:14); Yechezkel called it 'stone,' as it says, 'And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh' (Yechezkel 36:26); Yoel called it 'the hidden one (tzefoni)' — this is the evil inclination, which is hidden and stands in a person's heart."

388.label: Sukkah 52b
388.rest: — "Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: A person's inclination overpowers him every day and seeks to kill him, as it says, 'The wicked one watches the righteous and seeks to kill him' (Tehillim 37:32); and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him, he could not overcome it, as it says, 'Hashem will not abandon him into his hand' (Tehillim 37:33)."

389.label: Sanhedrin 98a
389.rest: — "He went to [Mashiach] and said: Peace upon you, my master and teacher. He said: Peace upon you, son of Levi. He said: When will the master come? He said: Today. He came to Eliyahu, who asked: What did he tell you? — 'Peace upon you, son of Levi.' He said: He has assured you and your father of the World to Come… He said: This is what he told you: 'Today — if you will hearken to His voice' (Tehillim 95:7)." Rashi: had you not been perfect tzaddikim he would not have greeted you and mentioned your father.

390.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 22, 67a
390.rest: — "The hei of 'hashishi' is Malchus, the seventh, and she is called av (cloud), and upon her the vav rides to redeem Israel… for she includes the three Avos, on whom the seventy-two Names depend… And this is the secret of Shabbos — bas and shin: the shin is Vayisa, Vayavo, Vayet, which are included in the bas."

391.label: Zohar II 204a (Vayakhel)
391.rest: — “Shabbos: shin–bas. The shin is the secret of the three Avos, who unite with the only daughter, and she is crowned with them.”

392.label: Taanis 15a
392.rest: — "Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I too say: not all are for light and not all are for gladness. The righteous are for light, and the upright for gladness: the righteous for light, as it is written, 'Light is sown for the righteous' (Tehillim 97:11); and the upright for gladness, as it is written, 'and for the upright of heart, gladness.'"

393.label: Zohar II 44a (Beshalach)
393.rest: — "'And it was the day, and he came there' (II Melachim 4:11) — which day was this? Come and see: that day was the festival of Rosh Hashanah, on which the barren of the world are remembered."

394.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 36, 77b
394.rest: — "Two thousand years of tohu — 'and the earth was tohu'; two thousand of Torah — 'and the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters' (Bereishis 1:2), and water means nothing but Torah; 'the face of the waters' — its two faces, the positive and the negative commandments, white and red, right and left… 'Let there be light' — this is Pesach, the light of the fourteenth; 'and there was light' — this is Rosh Hashanah."

395.label: Rosh Hashanah 16b
395.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: Every year that is poor at its beginning becomes rich at its end, as it says, 'From the beginning (meireishis) of the year' — 'meirashis' (from poverty) is written — 'until the end (acharis)': it will have a good end." Rashi: Israel make themselves poor on Rosh Hashanah, to speak supplications and prayer.

396.label: Zohar III 231b (Pinchas)
396.rest: — "On the days of Rosh Hashanah the court sets up a throne for the King to judge the whole world… We learned: 'And the judgment of His people Israel, each day's matter on its day' (I Melachim 8:59) — 'day on its day,' what is it? These are the two days of Rosh Hashanah. Why two days? Because they are two courts joined as one: the upper judgment, which is harsh, and the lower judgment, which is soft."

397.label: Yoma 72b
397.rest: — "Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonasan: What is meant by 'Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?' (Mishlei 17:16)? Woe to Torah scholars who occupy themselves with Torah but have no fear of Heaven."

398.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
398.rest: — "Chochmah is the brain within; Binah is the heart, and with it the heart understands."

399.label: Rosh Hashanah 29b
399.rest: — "Rabbi Levi bar Lachma said in the name of Rabbi Chama bar Chanina: One verse says, 'a Shabbos, a remembrance of teruah' (Vayikra 23:24), and one verse says, 'a day of teruah it shall be for you' (Bamidbar 29:1). There is no difficulty: here, when Yom Tov falls on Shabbos; there, when Yom Tov falls on a weekday."

400.label: Rosh Hashanah 30b
400.rest: — "And if witnesses came from Minchah onward, they would treat that day as holy and the next day as holy."

401.label: Shabbos 138b
401.rest: — On "they shall roam to seek the word of Hashem and shall not find it" (Amos 8:12): "'The word of Hashem' — this is halachah; 'the word of Hashem' — this is the End [of days]; 'the word of Hashem' — this is prophecy." Rashi: halachah, as in "to tell you the word of Hashem" (Devarim 5:5), meaning Torah.

402.label: Sotah 49a
402.rest: — "Rabbi Ila bar Yevarechyah said: Two Torah scholars walking on the road with no words of Torah between them are fit to be burned by fire, as it says, 'And it was, as they went on, walking and talking, behold a chariot of fire' (II Melachim 2:11) — because there was speech; had there been no speech, they would have been fit to be burned." Rashi: talking in words of Torah.

403.label: Zohar III 231b (Pinchas)
403.rest: — "'Blow the shofar at the new moon (bachodesh), at the covered time (bakeseh)' (Tehillim 81:4): 'bachodesh' — this is the soft court, called chodesh; 'bakeseh' — the throne (kes) of the upper world… Further, 'bakeseh' — this is the harsh judgment, the Fear of Yitzchak, a judgment always concealed and not revealed; 'for it is a statute' — the soft judgment; 'a judgment' — the harsh one; and both together — therefore two days."

404.label: Zohar III 231b (Pinchas)
404.rest: — "'Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah' (Tehillim 89:16): it does not say 'who hear' or 'who blow' the teruah, but 'who know' the teruah — for the wise who dwell in the air of the Holy Land know the teruah, the secret of the teruah… and all who know the secret of the teruah will come near to walk in the light of the face of the Holy One; and this is the primordial light that the Holy One hid away for the righteous."

405.label: Rosh Hashanah 18a
405.rest: — "'Seek Hashem while He may be found' (Yeshayahu 55:6) — for an individual, when? Rabbah bar Avuha said: These are the ten days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur."

406.label: Midrash Tehillim 27
406.rest: — "The Rabbis interpret the verses as Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur: 'my light' — on Rosh Hashanah; 'and my salvation' — on Yom Kippur… The Satan in gematria is 364: all the days of the year he has permission to accuse, except on Yom Kippur… 'In this (be-zos) I trust' — Rabbi Levi said: … 'With this (be-zos) shall Aharon come into the Sanctuary' (Vayikra 16:3)."

407.label: Midrash Tehillim 27
407.rest: — "A man lights a lamp in his palace, and everyone uses its light; but the Holy One is not so — My children shall see, and those who hate Me shall not see. And He already made such an example in Egypt."

408.label: Midrash Tehillim 27
408.rest: — "'Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path' (Tehillim 119:105)… David said: When I begin words of Torah, I begin with a little, and they flow forth; and when I enter into it, many gates open for me. Therefore it says 'a lamp to my feet,' and afterward 'a light to my path.'"

409.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a
409.rest: — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

410.label: Rosh Hashanah 19b
410.rest: — "Rabbi Chanina bar Kahana said: From the days of Ezra onward we have not found Elul made a full (thirty-day) month."

411.label: Avos 5:17
411.rest: — "Every dispute that is for the sake of Heaven will endure in the end, and one that is not for the sake of Heaven will not endure in the end. Which is a dispute for the sake of Heaven? The dispute of Hillel and Shammai. And which is not for the sake of Heaven? The dispute of Korach and all his company."

412.label: Eruvin 13b
412.rest: — "Rabbi Abba said in the name of Shmuel: For three years Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel disputed: these said, The halachah follows us, and these said, The halachah follows us. A heavenly voice went forth and said: These and these are the words of the living God, and the halachah follows Beis Hillel."

413.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 32a (s.v. maschil baTorah)
413.rest: — And if you ask: everywhere it is implied that Nevi'im take precedence over Kesuvim, as it says (Megillah 31a), "written in the Torah, repeated in the Nevi'im, and tripled in the Kesuvim," yet here the verses of Kesuvim come first and then the Nevi'im! One may answer: because the verses of Tehillim, Mishlei and Iyov preceded the Nevi'im.

414.label: Zohar III 99b (Emor)
414.rest: — "With these sounds below Israel give strength to mercy from below, and the great shofar is aroused above; therefore we must prepare a shofar on this day and arrange sounds, with intent, in order to arouse that other shofar in which the sounds above are included."

415.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 16b (s.v. kedei), citing the Yerushalmi
415.rest: — When the Satan hears the sound of the shofar the first time, he is alarmed; when he hears it a second time, he says: Surely this is the great shofar that is to be blown, and the time has come for me to be swallowed up.

416.label: Berachos 6a
416.rest: — "Rabbi Avin bar Rav Ada said in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak: From where do we know that the Holy One puts on tefillin? As it says, 'Hashem has sworn by His right hand and by the arm of His strength' (Yeshayahu 62:8)… And what is written in the tefillin of the Master of the world? 'And who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth' (I Divrei HaYamim 17:21)… The Holy One said to Israel: You have made Me one entity in the world, and I shall make you one entity in the world."

417.label: Bava Basra 58a
417.rest: — “Adam before the Shechinah was like a monkey before a man.”

418.label: Zohar III 283b (Vayeilech)
418.rest: — "'And Moshe went' — where did he go? Rather, he 'went' like a body without an arm, as you say, 'And they went without strength before the pursuer' (Eichah 1:6); for Aharon, the right arm, had died, and the body sought to depart. All the days of Moshe, the sun shone in the world."

419.label: Shabbos 152a
419.rest: — "'For man goes to his eternal home' (Koheles 12:5). Rabbi Yitzchak said: This teaches that each and every tzaddik is given a dwelling according to his honor. A parable: a king entered a city with his servants. When they enter, they all enter by one gate; when they lodge, each is given a dwelling according to his honor."

420.label: Makkos 7b
420.rest: — "Rabbi Abahu asked Rabbi Yochanan: If he was going up a ladder and a rung slipped out from under him, fell and killed — what is the law? … He said to him: You have already touched on a descent that is for the sake of an ascent."

421.label: Tanchuma, Vayeilech 2
421.rest: — "'Have I not written for you excellent things in counsels (mo'etzos) and knowledge' (Mishlei 22:20) — mo'etzos in gematria is 606; together with the seven mitzvos of the sons of Noach, 613."

422.label: Nedarim 22b
422.rest: — “Had Yisrael not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Yehoshua alone, for it contains the arrangement of Eretz Yisrael.”

423.label: Makkos 11a
423.rest: — "Why was the passage of the cities of refuge said in harsh language, as it is written, 'And Hashem spoke (vaydaber) to Yehoshua, saying: Speak to the Children of Israel, saying: Assign for yourselves the cities of refuge' (Yehoshua 20:1–2)? Because they are of the Torah." Rashi: everywhere in Yehoshua it says "vayomer," but here "vaydaber," and dibbur is a harsh expression.

424.label: Zohar I 234b (Vayechi)
424.rest: — "'And he said' — what is 'and he said'? As they explained: like 'and he said in his heart,' 'and you shall say in your heart' (Yeshayahu 49:21) — saying in a whisper… 'And I will tell (ve'agidah) you' — what is ve'agidah? It is the secret of wisdom."

425.label: Rashi, Shemos 31:3
425.rest: — "'With wisdom' — what a person hears from others and learns; 'and with understanding' — that he understands a matter from his own heart, from what he has learned; 'and with knowledge' — ruach hakodesh."

426.label: Bava Basra 12a
426.rest: — "Amemar said: And a sage is greater than a prophet, as it says, 'And a prophet (nevi) has a heart of wisdom' (Tehillim 90:12) — who depends on whom? The lesser on the greater." The Ramban there explains that the Sages' wisdom is a form of ruach hakodesh.

427.label: Bava Basra 12a–b
427.rest: — proving that a sage is greater than a prophet: "Rava said: Know that this is so, for a great man states a matter and it is then stated in the name of Rabbi Akiva bar Yosef in accordance with him." Rashi: one cannot say they simply share one mazal, for Rabbi Akiva was far wiser than he.

428.label: Kiddushin 49b
428.rest: — “Ten measures of wisdom descended to the world: the Land of Israel took nine, and the whole world took one. Ten measures of beauty descended to the world: Jerusalem took nine, and the whole world took one.” The first statement grounds Rav Tzadok's association of the Land with Torah wisdom. The measure is the Gemara's figurative language, not a numerical survey.

429.label: Gittin 60b
429.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah bar Nachmani, the interpreter of Reish Lakish, expounded: It is written, 'Write for yourself these words' (Shemos 34:27), and it is written, 'for according to (al pi) these words' — how so? Words that are written you may not say by heart; words that are oral you may not say in writing."

430.label: Megillah 7a
430.rest: — "Esther sent to the Sages: Write me down for the generations. They sent back to her: 'Have I not written for you shalishim' (Mishlei 22:20) — three times and not four." Rashi: in three places the war of Amalek is to be mentioned in the Torah.

431.label: Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6
431.rest: — "Things that were not revealed to Moshe were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues: 'And every precious thing his eye beheld' (Iyov 28:10) — this is Rabbi Akiva."

432.label: Zohar III 29b (Tzav)
432.rest: — "So Torah scholars, the children of the King and the Queen, are called Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim. They have nothing of their own, for they are not craftsmen like other servants… their reward is in this world and in the World to Come, to delight them with every kind of food and drink and to honor them with fine garments, like Shabbos, of which it is said, 'Honor it with clean clothing'; whatever a person does for Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim he should do for them."

433.label: Zohar II 60a (Beshalach)
433.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said: They went out to the wilderness to gaze upon the Holy One, and He removed His glorious radiance from there; they went to look for the Holy One and did not find Him. And we learned that the Holy One is called Torah, and water means only Torah, and Torah is none other than the Holy One, blessed be He."

434.label: Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 3
434.rest: — “Israel did not accept the Torah until the Holy One, blessed be He, held the mountain over them like a barrel.” The Tanchuma ties this coercion to the Oral Torah.

435.label: Midrash Tehillim 19
435.rest: — "Rabbi Tanchuma explained it as the six orders of the Mishnah: 'The Torah of Hashem is perfect' — this is the order of Nashim; 'the testimony of Hashem is faithful' — this is the order of Zera'im, for one believes in the Life of the worlds and sows; 'the fear of Hashem is pure' — this is the order of Taharos, which separates impurity from purity…"

436.label: Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah 1
436.rest: — "'To guard the way of the Tree of Life' (Bereishis 3:24): 'the way' — this is derech eretz; 'the Tree of Life' — this teaches that derech eretz preceded the Tree of Life; and the Tree of Life is nothing but Torah, as it says, 'It is a tree of life to those who grasp it' (Mishlei 3:18)."

437.label: Zohar I 27a
437.rest: — The Holy One places one who repents and toils in Torah "in His garden, which is the Shechinah, 'to work it' — with positive mitzvos, 'and to guard it' — with negative mitzvos." Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 21 (62a), says the same of Adam: "'to work it' — with positive commandments, 'and to guard it' — with negative commandments."

438.label: Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer 19
438.rest: — "'It is good to give thanks (lehodos) to Hashem' (Tehillim 92:2): Adam HaRishon said: From me all generations will learn that whoever confesses his sins and forsakes them is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom."

439.label: Pesachim 54a
439.rest: — "Seven things were created before the world was created, and these are they: Torah, teshuvah, Gan Eden, Gehinnom, the Throne of Glory, the Beis HaMikdash, and the name of Mashiach."

440.label: Zohar I, Mikeitz 202a
440.rest: — “We learned: A person should always rouse the good inclination against the evil inclination and strive against it. If it departs from him, well; if not, he should occupy himself with Torah, for there is nothing that breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death in order to break it.” The Zohar gives a sequence of active resistance, Torah and remembrance of death. Rav Tzadok emphasizes the Oral Torah's lived study as the means of transforming the inward enemy.

441.label: Berachos 6a
441.rest: — "From where do we know that the Holy One, blessed is He, puts on tefillin? As it says, 'Hashem has sworn by His right hand and by the arm of His strength' (Yeshayahu 62:8): 'His right hand' — this is Torah… 'the arm of His strength' — these are tefillin, as it says, 'Hashem will give strength (oz) to His people' (Tehillim 29:11)."

442.label: Zohar III 269a (Vaeschanan)
442.rest: — All four portions are included in the left arm, called "strength," as it is written, "And by the arm of His strength" (Yeshayahu 62:8); "and strength (oz) is nothing but Torah, and strength is nothing but tefillin."

443.label: Zevachim 116a
443.rest: — The nations asked Bilam, "What is the sound of this tumult that we heard? He said to them: He has a precious treasure in His storehouse, which was stored with Him nine hundred and seventy-four generations before the world was created, and He wishes to give it to His children, as it says, 'Hashem will give strength to His people' (Tehillim 29:11). Immediately they all opened and said, 'Hashem will bless His people with peace.'"

444.label: Tanchuma, Noach 3
444.rest: — "'A great light' (Yeshayahu 9:1) — the light that was created on the first day, which the Holy One, blessed be He, hid away for those who toil in the Oral Torah by day and by night, in whose merit the world stands, as it says, 'If not for My covenant day and night…' (Yirmeyahu 33:25). Which covenant is practiced by day and by night? This is Talmud."

445.label: Tamid 28a
445.rest: — "Rebbi says: Which is the straight path a person should choose for himself? Let him love rebuke… And some say: Let him hold fast to surpassing faith (emunah yeseirah), as it says, 'My eyes are upon the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with Me' (Tehillim 101:6)." [No Rashi on this amud.]

446.label: Berachos 5a
446.rest: — “Rabbi Yochanan said: ... Whoever can occupy himself with Torah but does not do so, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings ugly sufferings upon him and troubles him, as it is said, I became mute in silence; I was silent from good, and my pain was stirred up. Good means nothing other than Torah, as it is said, For I have given you a good teaching; do not abandon My Torah.” Rav Tzadok draws on the identification of good with Torah when reading a good heart as a heart shaped by Torah.

447.label: Shabbos 86b
447.rest: — “All agree that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbos.”

448.label: Zohar I 47b (Bereishis)
448.rest: — "'And God finished on the seventh day' (Bereishis 2:2) — this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day, and through it the world was completed, for it is the sustenance of all; 'His work that He had done' — and not all His work, for the Written Torah brought forth everything by the power of the writing that came forth from Chochmah."

449.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
449.rest: — "Chesed is the right arm, Gevurah the left arm, Tiferes the body, Netzach and Hod the two thighs, Yesod the completion of the body, the sign of the holy covenant; Malchus is the mouth — we call it the Oral Torah."

450.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 18 (34b)
450.rest: — "'Keser' is the supreme Keser; 'Hashem our God' — Abba and Imma; 'Holy, holy, holy' — the three Avos; 'Hashem Tzevaos' — the bris milah and the two thighs of truth; 'the whole earth is full of His glory' — this is the Shechinah."

451.label: Eruvin 54a
451.rest: — "The school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov taught: Wherever it says netzach, selah or va'ed, it has no interruption forever: netzach — as it is written, 'For I will not contend forever, nor be angry lanetzach' (Yeshayahu 57:16)…"

452.label: Shabbos 151b
452.rest: — "And Shlomo too said in his wisdom: 'Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come' — these are the days of old age; 'and the years arrive of which you will say, I have no desire in them' (Koheles 12:1) — these are the days of Mashiach, in which there is neither merit nor guilt."

453.label: Zohar II 178b (Sifra DiTzniusa)
453.rest: — "The hei was a dalet at first; and once it was impregnated with the yud within it, it gave birth and brought forth the vav."

454.label: Berachos 17a
454.rest: — "When the Rabbis took leave of the house of Rabbi Ami — some say, of Rabbi Chanina — they said to him: May you see your world in your lifetime, and may your end be for the life of Olam Haba, and your hope for all generations; may your heart meditate understanding, your mouth speak wisdom, and your eyes shine with the light of Torah."

455.label: Kiddushin 49b
455.rest: — "On condition that I am righteous — even if he is completely wicked, she is betrothed, for perhaps he thought thoughts of teshuvah in his mind. On condition that I am wicked — even if he is completely righteous, she is betrothed, for perhaps he thought of idolatry in his mind."

456.label: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 2:2
456.rest: — "And what is teshuvah? That the sinner abandon his sin, remove it from his thoughts and resolve in his heart never to do it again, as it says, 'Let the wicked abandon his way' (Yeshayahu 55:7); and also regret the past…; and He Who knows hidden things will testify about him that he will never return to this sin."

457.label: Yoma 86b
457.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: Great is teshuvah, for deliberate sins become for him like unintentional ones, as it says, 'Return, Israel, to Hashem your God, for you have stumbled in your iniquity' (Hoshea 14:2)… But Reish Lakish said: Great is teshuvah, for deliberate sins become for him like merits, as it says, 'And when the wicked turns from his wickedness and does justice and righteousness, on account of them he shall live' (Yechezkel 33:19)! There is no difficulty: here, from love; there, from fear."

458.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 44
458.rest: — "Rabbeinu HaKadosh expounded: Great is the power of teshuvah, for as soon as a person thinks in his heart to do teshuvah, immediately it rises — not ten mil, not twenty, not a hundred, but a journey of five hundred years; and not to the first firmament but to the seventh; and not only to the seventh, but it stands before the Throne of Glory. So Hoshea says, 'Return, Israel, unto (ad) Hashem your God' (Hoshea 14:2)."

459.label: Yoma 86a; Tzidkas HaTzadik 40; Takanas HaShavin 10:3
459.rest: — transformed sin and the remaining process of atonement: Yoma distinguishes forgiveness through teshuvah from the completion of kapparah: depending on the transgression, Yom Kippur, suffering, or death may still complete the cleansing. Tzidkas HaTzadik explains the highest teshuvah as an illumination in which deliberate sins can be understood as merits within Divine knowledge, while the earlier discussion in this siman nevertheless retains worldly punishment for grave acts. Rav Tzadok is therefore distinguishing two planes: the act’s inner meaning and covenantal root may be transformed, while its visible damage in this world may still require purification. The Gemara states the stages of atonement; this root-versus-appearance formulation is Rav Tzadok’s synthesis.

460.label: Avodah Zarah 17a
460.rest: — Of Elazar ben Durdaya: "He said: The matter depends only on me. He placed his head between his knees and wept aloud until his soul departed. A heavenly voice went forth and said: Rabbi Elazar ben Durdaya is destined for the life of the World to Come." The Gemara applies to him "'All who come to her do not return, nor attain the paths of life' (Mishlei 2:19)," for since he was so deeply attached to that sin, it is like heresy.

461.label: Zohar III 122a (Ra'aya Meheimna, Nasso)
461.rest: — "This commandment is the mitzvah of teshuvah, and this is Binah… Whoever returns in teshuvah, it is as though he returned the hei to the vav, which is ben Yah, and the Name Yud-Hei-Vav-Hei is completed by it; and this is teshuvah — tashuv hei, the hei returns, certainly, to the vav."

462.label: Yerushalmi, Demai 4:1
462.rest: — On the Mishnah that one may ask an untrustworthy seller on Shabbos whether produce was tithed and eat on his word, the Yerushalmi explains: the awe of Shabbos is upon the am ha'aretz, and he does not lie.

463.label: Berachos 17a
463.rest: — "Rava used to say: The goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, so that a person should not read and learn and then kick at his father, mother, teacher… as it says, 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem; good understanding to all who do them.'" Rashi: the essence of Torah is that repentance and good deeds accompany it.

464.label: Mechilta, Yisro, Bachodesh 7
464.rest: — "'Remember' (Shemos 20:8) and 'keep' (Devarim 5:12): remember it before it comes, and keep it after it has gone. From here they said: one adds from the weekday to the holy."

465.label: Berachos 33a
465.rest: — “Any person who has da’as, it is as if the Beis HaMikdash were built in his days.”

466.label: Megillah 17b
466.rest: — "And why did they see fit to say Binah after Kedushah? As it says, 'And they shall sanctify the Holy One of Yaakov and revere the God of Israel' (Yeshayahu 29:23), and next to it, 'And those of errant spirit shall know understanding (binah)' (29:24). And why did they see fit to say Teshuvah after Binah? As it is written, 'and his heart will understand, and he will return and be healed' (Yeshayahu 6:10)."

467.label: Megillah 17b
467.rest: — "And why did they see fit to say Binah after Kedushah? As it says, 'And they shall sanctify the Holy One of Yaakov and revere the God of Israel' (Yeshayahu 29:23), and next to it, 'And those of errant spirit shall know understanding (binah)' (29:24). And why did they see fit to say Teshuvah after Binah? As it is written, 'and his heart will understand, and he will return and be healed' (Yeshayahu 6:10)."

468.label: Mishnah, Nega'im 1:1
468.rest: — "The appearances of nega'im are two, which are four: bahares, intensely white as snow; secondary to it, like the lime of the Sanctuary…"

469.label: Berachos 34b
469.rest: — "Rabbi Abahu said: In the place where baalei teshuvah stand, perfect tzaddikim cannot stand, as it says, 'Peace, peace to the far and to the near' (Yeshayahu 57:19) — first to the far, and then to the near."

470.label: Berachos 61a
470.rest: — "Rav said: The evil inclination resembles a fly and sits between the two openings of the heart, as it says, 'Dead flies make the perfumer's oil putrid' (Koheles 10:1). Shmuel said: It resembles a kind of wheat (chitah), as it says, 'Sin (chatas) crouches at the door' (Bereishis 4:7)."

471.label: Midrash Tehillim 19
471.rest: — "'And I will be clean of great transgression' (Tehillim 19:14) — that great iniquity. Rabbi Levi said: David said before the Holy One: Master of the world, You are a great God, and my sins are great; it befits a great God to forgive great sins, as it says, 'For Your Name's sake, Hashem, forgive my iniquity, for it is great' (Tehillim 25:11)."
