472.label: Rosh Hashanah 18a
472.rest: — "'Seek Hashem while He may be found' (Yeshayahu 55:6) — for an individual, when? Rabbah bar Avuha said: These are the ten days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur."

473.label: Zohar III 94b (Emor)
473.rest: — "'Six days shall work be done' — what is the work of the six days? Rabbi Yosi said: It is written, 'For six days Hashem made the heavens and the earth' (Shemos 31:17), and it is not written 'in six days'; each and every day does its work, and they are called days of work."

474.label: Zohar III 257a (Ra'aya Meheimna)
474.rest: — "'And the Children of Israel shall keep the Shabbos' (Shemos 31:16). The Shechinah is called Shabbos on account of three supernal levels, which are the Shin: three crowns, Kesser, Chochmah and Binah; and she is the Bas (daughter), a fourth to them. In the six days, from Chesed to Yesod, work is done…; but from Binah upward it is rest, delight and cessation of all work."

475.label: Yoma 86b
475.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: Great is teshuvah, for deliberate sins become for him like unintentional ones, as it says, 'Return, Israel, to Hashem your God, for you have stumbled in your iniquity' (Hoshea 14:2)… But Reish Lakish said: Great is teshuvah, for deliberate sins become for him like merits, as it says, 'And when the wicked turns from his wickedness and does justice and righteousness, on account of them he shall live' (Yechezkel 33:19)! There is no difficulty: here, from love; there, from fear."

476.label: Taanis 8a
476.rest: — "Rabbi Ami said: A person's prayer is heard only if he places his soul in his palm… But Shmuel set up an interpreter and expounded: 'They beguiled Him with their mouth and lied to Him with their tongue; their heart was not steadfast with Him, nor were they faithful in His covenant' (Tehillim 78:36–37) — and nevertheless, 'But He, being merciful, forgives iniquity' (78:38)!"

477.label: Rambam, Hilchos Gerushin 2:20
477.rest: — One who does not wish to divorce, "since he wishes to be of Israel, and wishes to do all the mitzvos and keep away from transgressions, and it is his inclination that overpowered him — once he is beaten until his inclination weakens and he says 'I want,' he has divorced willingly."

478.label: Berachos 17a
478.rest: — “Master of the universe, it is revealed and known before You that our desire is to do Your will. What prevents us? The leaven in the dough and the subjugation of kingdoms. May it be Your will to save us from their hands, so that we may return to perform the statutes of Your will with a whole heart.” Rabbi Alexandri's prayer distinguishes Israel's underlying desire from the internal and external obstacles to its expression. Rav Tzadok uses that distinction in answering Amalek's accusation.

479.label: Berachos 11b
479.rest: — "But then, 'Who makes peace and creates evil' (Yeshayahu 45:7) — do we say it as it is written? Rather, it is written 'evil,' and we say 'all things,' as a more refined expression."

480.label: Pesachim 54a
480.rest: — "Rabbi Bena'ah son of Rabbi Ulla said: Why is 'that it was good' not said on the second day? Because on it the fire of Gehinnom was created."

481.label: Shabbos 149b
481.rest: — "'Also to punish the righteous is not good' (Mishlei 17:26) — 'not good' means nothing but evil; and it is written, 'For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You' (Tehillim 5:5)."

482.label: Zohar II 184a
482.rest: — “There is no light except that which comes forth from within darkness.”

483.label: Pesikta DeRav Kahana 24
483.rest: — "'Take words with you' (Hoshea 14:3): Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Nechemiah. Rabbi Yehudah said: Was it not with words that you beguiled Him at Sinai — 'They beguiled Him with their mouth, and lied to Him with their tongue' (Tehillim 78:36)? Rabbi Nechemiah said: 'Take words with you' — bring masters of words, good readers and good expounders, such as Levi ben Sisi and his colleagues."

484.label: Bamidbar Rabbah 7:4
484.rest: — "Rabbi Meir says: … even at the moment they said, 'All that Hashem has spoken we will do and we will hear' (Shemos 24:7), they said one thing with their mouths and another in their hearts, as it says, 'They beguiled Him with their mouth and lied to Him with their tongue, and their heart was not steadfast with Him' (Tehillim 78:36–37)."

485.label: Mechilta, Yisro, Bachodesh 1
485.rest: — "'And Israel encamped there' (Shemos 19:2): wherever it says 'they journeyed… they encamped,' they journeyed in dispute and encamped in dispute; but here they were all of one heart."

486.label: Mishnah, Parah 8:9
486.rest: — "Waters that deceive (mechazvim) are disqualified; these are waters that fail once in seven years."

487.label: Kiddushin 49b
487.rest: — "On condition that I am righteous — even if he is completely wicked, she is betrothed, for perhaps he thought thoughts of teshuvah in his mind. On condition that I am wicked — even if he is completely righteous, she is betrothed, for perhaps he thought of idolatry in his mind."

488.label: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 2:2
488.rest: — "And what is teshuvah? That the sinner abandon his sin, remove it from his thoughts and resolve in his heart never to do it again, as it says, 'Let the wicked abandon his way' (Yeshayahu 55:7); and also regret the past…; and He Who knows hidden things will testify about him that he will never return to this sin."

489.label: Yoma 86b
489.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: Great is teshuvah, for deliberate sins become for him like unintentional ones, as it says, 'Return, Israel, to Hashem your God, for you have stumbled in your iniquity' (Hoshea 14:2)… But Reish Lakish said: Great is teshuvah, for deliberate sins become for him like merits, as it says, 'And when the wicked turns from his wickedness and does justice and righteousness, on account of them he shall live' (Yechezkel 33:19)! There is no difficulty: here, from love; there, from fear."

490.label: Kiddushin 59a–b
490.rest: — "An act removes from [the power of] an act and from a thought; a thought removes neither from an act nor from a thought… Granted that it does not remove from an act, for speech cannot come and nullify an act; but from a thought it should remove!"

491.label: Kesubos 111b
491.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said to him: I expound from another verse, as it is written, 'For Your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth shall cast forth the dead' (Yeshayahu 26:19): whoever makes use of the light of Torah, the light of Torah revives him; and whoever does not make use of the light of Torah, the light of Torah does not revive him."

492.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 12a
492.rest: — "Therefore the masters of the Mishnah established: 'Whoever engages in the dew (tal) of Torah, the dew of Torah revives him'; and this is [the dew] by which we are saved, 'Who makes the dew descend.'"

493.label: Shabbos 88b
493.rest: — “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: With every utterance that came from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, the souls of Israel departed, as it is said, ‘My soul departed when He spoke.’ If their souls departed at the first utterance, how did they receive the second? He brought down the dew with which He will revive the dead in the future and revived them, as it is said, ‘You showered abundant rain, O God; when Your inheritance was weary, You sustained it.’”

494.label: Shabbos 145b; Rashi, s.v. She’einan bimkoman
494.rest: — “Why do the Torah scholars of Bavel distinguish themselves by their appearance? Because they are not in their own place. As people say: 'In my town, my name; outside my town, my clothing.' Rav Yosef taught concerning the verse 'Those who come shall take root in Yaakov; Israel shall blossom and flower': These are the Torah scholars of Bavel, who produce blossoms and flowers for the Torah.” Rashi explains “not in their place” as meaning that they were exiled there from Eretz Yisrael, and explains the proverb: in one’s own city one is recognized by name, whereas in a foreign place one’s clothing supplies the public distinction. This is Rabbi Yochanan’s answer, correcting the earlier suggestion that the dress compensates for a lack of Torah.

495.label: Pirkei Avot 1:1
495.rest: — “Moses received Torah from Sinai and transmitted it to Joshua; Joshua to the elders; the elders to the prophets; and the prophets transmitted it to the Men of the Great Assembly. They said three things: Be deliberate in judgment, raise up many students, and make a fence for Torah.” The transmission culminates in the assembly whose program Rav Tzadok invokes: the expansion of students and the protection of Torah through a fence.

496.label: Yoma 69b
496.rest: — "They sat in fasting three days and three nights, and it was handed over to them. There came forth something like a fiery lion cub from the Holy of Holies. The prophet said to Israel: This is the inclination for idolatry, as it says, 'And he said: This is the wickedness' (Zechariah 5:8)."

497.label: Rashi, Shemos 31:3
497.rest: — "'With wisdom' — what a person hears from others and learns; 'and with understanding' — that he understands a matter from his own heart, from what he has learned; 'and with knowledge' — ruach hakodesh."

498.label: Bava Basra 12a–b
498.rest: — A sage is greater than a prophet: "For a great man says something, and then it is reported in the name of Rabbi Akiva ben Yosef, just like him."

499.label: Zohar II, 88a
499.rest: — “Rabbi Abba said: Blessing is prepared for those supernal days, which are blessed from this day. On this day the head of Zeir Anpin is filled with dew descending from Atika Kadisha, the most concealed of all. He pours it upon the field of holy apples three times from the entrance of Shabbos, so that all will be blessed together.” The threefold flow of dew is the specific basis for linking the three Shabbos meals to the upper and lower modes of receiving blessing.

500.label: Eruvin 21b
500.rest: — "'Good figs' (Yirmeyahu 24) — these are the completely righteous; 'bad figs' — the completely wicked. And lest you say their hope is lost, the verse teaches, 'The dudaim give forth fragrance' (Shir HaShirim 7:14): both these and those are destined to give forth fragrance."

501.label: Kerisos 6b
501.rest: — "Any fast in which the sinners of Israel do not take part is not a fast, for chelbenah has a foul odor, yet Scripture counted it among the spices of the incense."

502.label: Yoma 39b
502.rest: — "The goats in Yericho would sneeze from the fragrance of the incense; the women in Yericho did not need to perfume themselves, from the fragrance of the incense; a bride in Yerushalayim did not need to perfume herself, from the fragrance of the incense."

503.label: Yoma 39b
503.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak ben Tavlai said: Why is it called Levanon? Because it whitens (malbin) the sins of Israel."

504.label: Avodah Zarah 17a
504.rest: — Of Elazar ben Durdaya: "He said: The matter depends only on me. He placed his head between his knees and wept aloud until his soul departed. A heavenly voice went forth and said: Rabbi Elazar ben Durdaya is destined for the life of the World to Come." The Gemara applies to him "'All who come to her do not return, nor attain the paths of life' (Mishlei 2:19)," for since he was so deeply attached to that sin, it is like heresy.

505.label: Rosh Hashanah 32a
505.rest: — "The 'And He said's of the Creation account are nine! — 'Bereishis' is also an utterance, as it is written, 'By the word of Hashem the heavens were made' (Tehillim 33:6)." Rashi: although "and He said" is not written there, it is as though it were, for heaven too was created by speech and not by hand.

506.label: Tanchuma, Vayeshev 4
506.rest: — "When the Holy One created the world, on the first day He created the Angel of Death. From where? Rabbi Berechyah said: Because it says, 'and darkness upon the face of the deep' (Bereishis 1:2) — this is the Angel of Death, who darkens the faces of the creatures."

507.label: Bava Basra 16a
507.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: He is the Satan, he is the evil inclination, he is the Angel of Death. He is the Satan, as it is written, 'And the Satan went out from before Hashem' (Iyov 2:7); he is the evil inclination, as it is written there, 'only evil all day' (Bereishis 6:5)…; he is the Angel of Death, as it is written, 'only guard his soul' (Iyov 2:6)."

508.label: Zohar II 184a (Tetzaveh)
508.rest: — “There is no light except that which comes out of the darkness.”

509.label: Shabbos 89b
509.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: The Holy One said to Israel: If your sins be like these years (shanim), which are arranged and come from the six days of Creation until now, they shall be white as snow (Yeshayahu 1:18)."

510.label: Rosh Hashanah 21b
510.rest: — "Rav and Shmuel both said: Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world, and all were given to Moshe except one, as it says, 'And You made him a little lower than God' (Tehillim 8:6)."

511.label: Menachos 29b
511.rest: — "He said: Master of the world, show him to me. He said: Turn around. He went and sat at the end of eight rows and did not understand what they were saying, and his strength waned. When they reached a certain matter, his students said to him: Rebbi, from where do you know this? He said: It is a halachah to Moshe from Sinai — and Moshe's mind was settled." Rashi: since it was said in his name.

512.label: Berachos 34b
512.rest: — "R. Abahu said: In the place where ba'alei teshuvah stand, the completely righteous cannot stand, as it says, 'Peace, peace, to the far and to the near' — the far first, then the near." This disputes R. Yochanan, who holds the completely righteous are greater. Rashi: "the near" is one who was far from sin all his days, a tzaddik from the start.

513.label: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 5:5
513.rest: — "He does not know with a knowledge that is outside Him, like people, who and their knowledge are two; rather He, may His Name be exalted, and His knowledge are one, and a person's mind cannot grasp this clearly. And just as a person cannot grasp and find the truth of the Creator, as it says, 'For man shall not see Me and live' (Shemos 33:20), so a person cannot grasp and find the Creator's knowledge. This is what the prophet said: 'For My thoughts are not your thoughts, nor your ways My ways' (Yeshayahu 55:8)."

514.label: Zohar Chadash, end of the Tikkunim (Vayera)
514.rest: — Rabbi Yose asked: if a person is decreed righteous or wicked before he comes into the world, how can there be reward and punishment? "Rabbi Shimon said: This question is deep; the early ones disagreed over it, and many stumbled in it because they did not reach the depth of the secret… The secret of it is: all is foreseen, yet permission is granted." He explains: "All is foreseen in thought — the Holy One knows a person's thought — and permission is given to man in deed." He did not decree whether a person will be righteous or wicked; "the secret of the matter is deep: 'the hidden things belong to Hashem our God' (Devarim 29:28)." Rav Tzadok cites this passage for the principle that where there is knowledge there is no choice, and where there is choice there is no grasp of His knowledge (Tzidkas HaTzaddik 40; Takanas HaShavin 6:5; Resisei Layla 50:2).

515.label: Sanhedrin 90b
515.rest: — "The Romans asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananyah: From where do we know that the Holy One revives the dead and knows what will be? He said to them: Both from this verse, as it says, 'And Hashem said to Moshe: Behold, you will lie with your fathers and rise; and this people will go astray' (Devarim 31:16)."

516.label: Zohar I 87b (Lech Lecha)
516.rest: — "Likewise, 'See now that I, I am He' (Devarim 32:39) — to show that there is no separation between above and below."

517.label: Zohar I 22b (Bereishis)
517.rest: — "There is One who is called the Cause of causes, and it is not that which is called the Cause above all causes; for the Cause above all causes has no second from whom to take counsel, for He is singular before all and has no partner."

518.label: Sanhedrin 91b
518.rest: — "Our Rabbis taught: 'I put to death and I bring to life' (Devarim 32:39) — one might think death for one and life for another, as is the way of the world; the verse says, 'I wounded and I will heal' — just as wounding and healing are in one, so death and life are in one. From here is a refutation of those who say the revival of the dead is not from the Torah."

519.label: Berachos 57b
519.rest: — "Three things are a semblance of the World to Come: Shabbos, the sun, and marital union"; and "Shabbos is one-sixtieth of the World to Come." (Rashi has no comment on Shabbos here.)

520.label: Yoma 86a
520.rest: — "Rabbi Levi said: Great is teshuvah, for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory, as it says, 'Return, Israel, unto (ad) Hashem your God' (Hoshea 14:2)."

521.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 44
521.rest: — "Rabbeinu HaKadosh expounded: Great is the power of teshuvah, for as soon as a person thinks in his heart to do teshuvah, immediately it rises — not ten mil, not twenty, not a hundred, but a journey of five hundred years; and not to the first firmament but to the seventh; and not only to the seventh, but it stands before the Throne of Glory. So Hoshea says, 'Return, Israel, unto (ad) Hashem your God' (Hoshea 14:2)."

522.label: Zohar II 88b (Yisro)
522.rest: — Rabbi Shimon said: Whoever completes the three meals on Shabbos, a voice goes out and proclaims of him: "Then you shall delight in Hashem" — this is the first meal…; "and I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father" (Yeshayahu 58:14) — this is the completion, completed in Ze'eir Anpin.

523.label: Sanhedrin 44a
523.rest: — "'Yisrael has sinned' (Yehoshua 7:11) — Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said: Even though he has sinned, he is Yisrael."

524.label: Nedarim 31a
524.rest: — On the Mishnah that one who vows not to benefit from "the seed of Avraham" is forbidden with Jews and permitted with gentiles: "But there is Yishmael! — 'For in Yitzchak shall seed be called to you' (Bereishis 21:12). But there is Esav! — 'In Yitzchak,' and not all of Yitzchak." Rashi: Esav is not called the seed of Yitzchak.

525.label: Sanhedrin 96a
525.rest: — "If at the reward of four steps that I paid to that wicked one, who ran after My honor, you wonder — when I pay the reward of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, who ran before Me like horses, how much more so!"

526.label: Chullin 16a
526.rest: — “Rabbi was teaching: From where do we know that slaughter must be with a detached object? For it is said, He took the knife to slaughter. ... But that verse teaches us Avraham's eagerness.” The Gemara questions whether taking the knife proves a rule about slaughtering implements or simply displays Avraham's eagerness to fulfill the command.

527.label: Zohar II 184a (Tetzaveh)
527.rest: — "There is no light except that which comes out of darkness: when the Other Side is subdued, the Holy One rises above and is glorified in His glory. There is no service of the Holy One except out of darkness, and no good except out of evil."

528.label: Yoma 72b
528.rest: — "Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonasan: What is meant by 'Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?' (Mishlei 17:16)? Woe to Torah scholars who occupy themselves with Torah but have no fear of Heaven."

529.label: Zohar III 230a (Pinchas, Ra'aya Meheimna)
529.rest: — "He is truth (emes), and She is faith (emunah)."

530.label: Shabbos 31b
530.rest: — "Rabbah bar Rav Huna said: Anyone who has Torah but no fear of Heaven is like a treasurer who was given the inner keys but not the outer keys: by what will he enter?" Rashi: fear of Heaven is like the outer doors, through which one enters the inner ones; if he fears Heaven he becomes careful to keep and do, and if not, he cares nothing for his learning.

531.label: Zohar I 11b (Introduction)
531.rest: — "Fear, which is the essence: that a person fear his Master because He is great and rules, the essence and root of all worlds, and all before Him are considered as nothing, as it is said, 'And all the inhabitants of the earth are considered as nothing' (Daniel 4:32)."

532.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a
532.rest: — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

533.label: Zohar III 123b (Ra'aya Meheimna)
533.rest: — "'The hidden things' (Devarim 29:28) — fear and love, which are in the brain and the heart, within the body and the head; 'and the revealed things' — Torah and mitzvah, which are in the body and the head outwardly. For whether a person fears the Holy One or loves Him, no one else knows; it is revealed only between him and his Maker."

534.label: Zohar I 234b (Vayechi)
534.rest: — "'And he said' — what is 'and he said'? As they explained: like 'and he said in his heart,' 'and you shall say in your heart' (Yeshayahu 49:21) — saying in a whisper… 'And I will tell (ve'agidah) you' — what is ve'agidah? It is the secret of wisdom."

535.label: Rashi, Avodah Zarah 54a (s.v. vadai Yisrael mumar)
535.rest: — "For it is impossible that among all the worshippers there not be one apostate, since one who sees Israel's hand brought low inclines his heart to idolatry."

536.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 16b, s.v. Kedei learbev
536.rest: — “The Aruch explains, as in the Yerushalmi: It is written, He shall swallow death forever, and On that day a great shofar shall be sounded. When he hears the shofar once, he is alarmed but not fully alarmed. When he hears it a second time, he says: Surely this is the shofar that shall be sounded as the great shofar, and my time has come to be swallowed up. He becomes confused and has no time to prosecute.” This verifies the teaching through Tosafos quoting the Aruch in the Yerushalmi's name, the intermediary identified in Rav Tzadok's citation. It is not presented as an independently located passage in the extant Yerushalmi.

537.label: Shabbos 88b
537.rest: — "The Holy One said to Moshe: Give them an answer. He said before Him: Master of the world, I am afraid lest they burn me with the breath of their mouths. He said to him: Grasp My Throne of Glory and answer them, as it says, 'He grasps the face of the Throne, He spreads His cloud upon him' (Iyov 26:9)."

538.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 44
538.rest: — "Rabbeinu HaKadosh expounded: Great is the power of teshuvah, for as soon as a person thinks in his heart to do teshuvah, immediately it rises — not ten mil, not twenty, not a hundred, but a journey of five hundred years; and not to the first firmament but to the seventh; and not only to the seventh, but it stands before the Throne of Glory. So Hoshea says, 'Return, Israel, unto (ad) Hashem your God' (Hoshea 14:2)."

539.label: Berachos 34b
539.rest: — "Rabbi Abahu said: In the place where baalei teshuvah stand, perfect tzaddikim cannot stand, as it says, 'Peace, peace to the far and to the near' (Yeshayahu 57:19) — first to the far, and then to the near."

540.label: Tikkunei Zohar 82b
540.rest: — "'Each according to its kind' (Bereishis 1:11) — these are the souls hewn from His Throne of Glory; and these the spirits hewn from the angels; and these the nefashos hewn from the Ofanim."

541.label: Sanhedrin 90a (Mishnah)
541.rest: — "All Israel have a share in the World to Come, as it says, 'And your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of My planting, the work of My hands to be glorified' (Yeshayahu 60:21). And these have no share in the World to Come: one who says there is no resurrection of the dead from the Torah, that the Torah is not from Heaven, and an apikoros."

542.label: Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah 26
542.rest: — "'I am Hashem your God' — this teaches that the Holy One looked at the whole world from beginning to end and foresaw ten men who would kick against Him: Michah, Yeravam, the son of the Israelite woman, the gatherer of sticks, Avshalom, Yoav, Shimshon, Achan, the witnesses against Navos, and Achav. 'I am Hashem your God' — Michah kicked; 'You shall have no other gods' — Yeravam kicked…"

543.label: Bava Metzia 59b
543.rest: — "Rabbi Yehoshua stood on his feet and said: 'It is not in heaven' (Devarim 30:12). What is 'it is not in heaven'? Rabbi Yirmeyah said: For the Torah was already given at Mount Sinai; we pay no heed to a heavenly voice, for You already wrote at Mount Sinai in the Torah, 'Incline after the majority' (Shemos 23:2)." Eliyahu said that the Holy One then smiled and said: "My children have prevailed over Me."

544.label: Pesikta DeRav Kahana 24
544.rest: — "Israel said before the Holy One: Master of the worlds, if we do teshuvah, will You accept us? He said to them: I accepted the teshuvah of Kayin, and shall I not accept yours? A harsh decree had been decreed upon him… and once he did teshuvah, half the decree was withheld from him."

545.label: Yoma 86a; Tzidkas HaTzadik 40; Takanas HaShavin 10:3
545.rest: — transformed sin and the remaining process of atonement: Yoma distinguishes forgiveness through teshuvah from the completion of kapparah: depending on the transgression, Yom Kippur, suffering, or death may still complete the cleansing. Tzidkas HaTzadik explains the highest teshuvah as an illumination in which deliberate sins can be understood as merits within Divine knowledge, while the earlier discussion in this siman nevertheless retains worldly punishment for grave acts. Rav Tzadok is therefore distinguishing two planes: the act’s inner meaning and covenantal root may be transformed, while its visible damage in this world may still require purification. The Gemara states the stages of atonement; this root-versus-appearance formulation is Rav Tzadok’s synthesis.

546.label: Sanhedrin 90a (Mishnah)
546.rest: — "Three kings and four commoners have no portion in the World to Come. The three kings: Yeravam, Achav and Menasheh. Rabbi Yehudah says: Menasheh has a portion in the World to Come, as it says, 'And he prayed to Him, and He heard his supplication and returned him to Yerushalayim to his kingdom' (II Divrei HaYamim 33:13). They said to him: To his kingdom He returned him, but not to the life of the World to Come. The four commoners: Bilam, Doeg, Achitofel and Gechazi."

547.label: Yoma 86b
547.rest: — "What is a baal teshuvah? Rav Yehudah said: For example, a matter of transgression came his way a first and a second time, and he was saved from it. Rav Yehudah indicated: with the same woman, at the same time, in the same place."

548.label: Midrash Tehillim 95
548.rest: — "'Today, if you will listen to His voice' (Tehillim 95:7): Rabbi Levi said: If Israel kept even one Shabbos properly, they would be redeemed immediately, as it says, 'Today, if you will listen to His voice,' and it is written, 'Keep the Shabbos day to sanctify it' (Devarim 5:12)."

549.label: Sanhedrin 98a
549.rest: — "He went to [Mashiach] and said: Peace upon you, my master and teacher. He said: Peace upon you, son of Levi. He said: When will the master come? He said: Today. He came to Eliyahu, who asked: What did he tell you? — 'Peace upon you, son of Levi.' He said: He has assured you and your father of the World to Come… He said: This is what he told you: 'Today — if you will hearken to His voice' (Tehillim 95:7)." Rashi: had you not been perfect tzaddikim he would not have greeted you and mentioned your father.

550.label: Zohar II 89a (Yisro)
550.rest: — "Therefore Shabbos is weighed against the Torah, and whoever keeps the Shabbos is as though he keeps the whole Torah, as it is written, 'Fortunate is the man who does this… who keeps the Shabbos from profaning it' (Yeshayahu 56:2)."

551.label: Shabbos 118b
551.rest: — “Rav Yehudah said in Rav's name: Had Israel observed the first Shabbos, no nation or tongue would have ruled over them, as it says, 'On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather,' followed by 'Amalek came.' Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai's name: If Israel observed two Shabbosos according to their laws, they would be redeemed immediately, as it says, 'Thus says Hashem to the eunuchs who keep My Shabbosos,' followed by 'I shall bring them to My holy mountain.'” The first statement supplies the connection between Shabbos and Amalek; the second explains why Shabbos can also be presented as the route to immediate redemption. Rav Tzadok understands the lasting subjugation as the later fruit of the inward damage Amalek introduced.

552.label: Zohar III 70a (Acharei Mos)
552.rest: — "Rabbi Abba said: 'From the depths I called You, Hashem' (Tehillim 130:1) — there is a hidden place above, and it is the depth of the well, from which rivers and springs go forth on every side; and that depth of depths is called Teshuvah; and whoever wishes to return and be purified of his sins must call to the Holy One from this depth."

553.label: Rosh Hashanah 21b
553.rest: — “Rav and Shmuel disagreed. One said: Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world, and all were given to Moshe except one, as it is said: You made him a little less than God.” The identification of the fiftieth gate particularly with penitents is Rav Tzadok's development here; it is not stated in this sentence of the Gemara.

554.label: Berachos 61a
554.rest: — "Rav said: The evil inclination resembles a fly and sits between the two openings of the heart, as it says, 'Dead flies make the perfumer's oil putrid' (Koheles 10:1). Shmuel said: It resembles a kind of wheat (chitah), as it says, 'Sin (chatas) crouches at the door' (Bereishis 4:7)."

555.label: Sukkah 52b
555.rest: — "Rava said: At first [the evil inclination] is called a wayfarer, then a guest, and finally a man, as it says, 'And a wayfarer came to the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock… to prepare for the guest…, and he took the poor man's lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him' (II Shmuel 12:4)."

556.label: Avodah Zarah 17a
556.rest: — Of Elazar ben Durdaya: "He said: The matter depends only on me. He placed his head between his knees and wept aloud until his soul departed. A heavenly voice went forth and said: Rabbi Elazar ben Durdaya is destined for the life of the World to Come." The Gemara applies to him "'All who come to her do not return, nor attain the paths of life' (Mishlei 2:19)," for since he was so deeply attached to that sin, it is like heresy.

557.label: Yoma 86a–b
557.rest: — The Gemara there brings a series of sayings that open "Great is teshuvah": it brings healing to the world; it reaches up to the Throne of Glory; it overrides a prohibition of the Torah; it turns deliberate sins into unintentional ones, and into merits; it lengthens a person's years; and it brings the redemption near.

558.label: Rosh Hashanah 16b
558.rest: — "Rabbi Kruspedai said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Three books are opened on Rosh Hashanah: one of the completely wicked, one of the completely righteous, and one of the intermediate. The completely righteous are written and sealed immediately for life; the completely wicked are written and sealed immediately for death; the intermediate are held in suspense from Rosh Hashanah until Yom Kippur: if they merit, they are written for life; if they do not merit, they are written for death."

559.label: Niddah 30b
559.rest: — Before birth, "they teach him the entire Torah, as it says, 'And he taught me and said to me: Let your heart hold fast my words; keep my commandments and live' (Mishlei 4:4)… and once he comes into the air of the world, an angel comes, strikes him on his mouth, and makes him forget the entire Torah."

560.label: Avos 2:1
560.rest: — "Consider three things and you will not come into the hands of sin: know what is above you — an eye that sees, an ear that hears, and all your deeds are written in a book."

561.label: Chagigah 15a
561.rest: — “He created righteous people and wicked people; He created Gan Eden and Gehinnom. Each person has two portions, one in Gan Eden and one in Gehinnom. If the righteous person merits, he takes his own portion and his fellow's portion in Gan Eden. If the wicked person is found guilty, he takes his own portion and his fellow's portion in Gehinnom.” Rav Tzadok interprets ‘his fellow’ through the correspondence of soul-roots and the separation of the good and evil that had become intermixed.

562.label: Yoma 86a
562.rest: — "Rabbi Levi said: Great is teshuvah, for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory, as it says, 'Return, Israel, unto (ad) Hashem your God' (Hoshea 14:2)."

563.label: Zohar I 219b (Vayechi)
563.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah said: There is no sin in the world that has no teshuvah except this one, and there is no wicked person who does not see the face of the Shechinah except this one, as it is written, 'Evil shall not dwell with You' (Tehillim 5:5)."

564.label: Reishis Chochmah, Shaar HaKedushah 17
564.rest: — What is said of this sin, that it has no teshuvah, means that his teshuvah is extremely difficult, and he is not given the means to repent, for it requires many afflictions and the penitent grows weary.

565.label: Avodah Zarah 17a
565.rest: — Of Elazar ben Durdaya: "He said: The matter depends only on me. He placed his head between his knees and wept aloud until his soul departed. A heavenly voice went forth and said: Rabbi Elazar ben Durdaya is destined for the life of the World to Come." The Gemara applies to him "'All who come to her do not return, nor attain the paths of life' (Mishlei 2:19)," for since he was so deeply attached to that sin, it is like heresy.

566.label: Yoma 86b
566.rest: — On how many times a sin is forgiven: "Here, for an individual; there, for a community."

567.label: Bava Metzia 84a
567.rest: — "The Rabbis said to him: Is the master not afraid of the evil eye? He said to them: I come from the seed of Yosef, over whom the evil eye does not rule, as it is written, 'Yosef is a fruitful son, a fruitful son by the eye (alei ayin)' (Bereishis 49:22) — and Rabbi Abahu said: Do not read alei ayin but olei ayin, rising above the eye."

568.label: Eruvin 18b
568.rest: — "Rabbi Yirmeyah ben Elazar said: All those years that Adam HaRishon was in excommunication, he begot spirits, demons and lilin, as it says, 'And Adam lived one hundred and thirty years, and begot in his likeness, after his image' (Bereishis 5:3) — implying that until then he had not begotten after his image."

569.label: Bava Metzia 29b
569.rest: — "Abaye said: Tefillin are commonly found at the house of bar Chavu; scrolls are not commonly found."

570.label: Berachos 6a
570.rest: — "Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to Rav Chiya bar Avin: These tefillin of the Master of the world — what is written in them? He said to him: 'And who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land' (I Divrei HaYamim 17:21). And is the Holy One, blessed is He, praised with the praise of Israel? Yes." Rashi: our tefillin contain Shema and the other passages, which praise the Holy One.

571.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
571.rest: — "Chochmah is the brain, which is thought within; Binah is the heart, and with it the heart understands; and of these two it is written, 'The hidden things belong to Hashem our God' (Devarim 29:28)."

572.label: Rema, Orach Chaim 1:1
572.rest: — "When a person takes to heart that the great King, the Holy One, blessed be He, whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and sees his deeds, as it says, 'Can a man hide in secret places that I shall not see him? says Hashem' (Yirmeyahu 23:24) — immediately awe and submission will come upon him, in dread of Hashem Yisbarach, and he will be ashamed before Him constantly."

573.label: Berachos 7b
573.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: From the day the Holy One created the world, there was no person who called the Holy One 'Master' until Avraham came and called Him Master, as it says, 'And he said: My Master, Hashem God, by what shall I know that I will inherit it?' (Bereishis 15:8)."

574.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
574.rest: — "Chesed is the right arm, Gevurah the left arm, Tiferes the body, Netzach and Hod the two thighs, Yesod the completion of the body, the sign of the holy covenant; Malchus is the mouth — we call it the Oral Torah."

575.label: Berachos 6a
575.rest: — "Rabbi Avin bar Rav Ada said in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak: From where do we know that the Holy One puts on tefillin? As it says, 'Hashem has sworn by His right hand and by the arm of His strength' (Yeshayahu 62:8)… And what is written in the tefillin of the Master of the world? 'And who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth' (I Divrei HaYamim 17:21)… The Holy One said to Israel: You have made Me one entity in the world, and I shall make you one entity in the world."

576.label: Shabbos 118b
576.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: Had Israel kept the first Shabbos, no nation or tongue would have ruled over them… Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: Were Israel to keep two Shabbosos according to their law, they would immediately be redeemed, as it says, 'Thus says Hashem to the eunuchs who keep My Shabbosos' (Yeshayahu 56:4), and it is written after it, 'I will bring them to My holy mountain' (56:7)."

577.label: Berachos 6a
577.rest: — "Rabbi Avin bar Rav Ada said in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak: From where do we know that the Holy One puts on tefillin? As it says, 'Hashem has sworn by His right hand and by the arm of His strength' (Yeshayahu 62:8)… And what is written in the tefillin of the Master of the world? 'And who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth' (I Divrei HaYamim 17:21)… The Holy One said to Israel: You have made Me one entity in the world, and I shall make you one entity in the world."

578.label: Bava Basra 58a
578.rest: — "Rabbi Bena'ah said: I gazed at his two heels, and they were like two orbs of the sun. All, compared to Sarah, are like a monkey before a man; Sarah before Chavah is like a monkey before a man; Chavah before Adam is like a monkey before a man; Adam before the Shechinah is like a monkey before a man."

579.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 44 (Shuvah)
579.rest: — "A parable of a king's son who was sick. The doctor said: If he eats of this thing he will be healed. The son was afraid to eat it. His father said to him: Know that it will not harm you — I will eat of it first. So the Holy One said to Israel: You are ashamed to do teshuvah? I will return first, as it says, 'Thus says Hashem: Behold, I return' (Yirmiyahu 30:18)."

580.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 44
580.rest: — "All the prophets call Israel to teshuvah, but none like Hoshea. Yirmeyahu said, 'If you return, Israel, says Hashem, return to Me' (Yirmeyahu 4:1); Yeshayahu said, 'Seek Hashem while He may be found' (Yeshayahu 55:6) — and they do not teach Israel what to say. But Hoshea said, Do teshuvah, and teaches them with what to appease Him: 'Return, Israel… Take with you words and return to Hashem; say to Him: Forgive all iniquity' (Hoshea 14:2–3)."

581.label: Pesikta DeRav Kahana 24
581.rest: — "'Take words with you' (Hoshea 14:3): Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Nechemiah. Rabbi Yehudah said: Was it not with words that you beguiled Him at Sinai — 'They beguiled Him with their mouth, and lied to Him with their tongue' (Tehillim 78:36)? Rabbi Nechemiah said: 'Take words with you' — bring masters of words, good readers and good expounders, such as Levi ben Sisi and his colleagues."

582.label: Rambam, Hilchos Gerushin 2:20
582.rest: — One who does not wish to divorce, "since he wishes to be of Israel, and wishes to do all the mitzvos and keep away from transgressions, and it is his inclination that overpowered him — once he is beaten until his inclination weakens and he says 'I want,' he has divorced willingly."

583.label: Tanchuma Haazinu 4
583.rest: — "One verse says, 'Hashem will lift His face to you' (Bamidbar 6:26), and another says, 'Who does not lift His face' (Devarim 10:17). One who repents — He lifts His face to him. Could this be for all? Scripture says 'to you' — and not to another nation."

584.label: Sanhedrin 58b
584.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: A gentile who rests is liable to death, as it says, 'Day and night they shall not rest' (Bereishis 8:22)." Rashi: who rests from his work for a full day.

585.label: Sukkah 52b
585.rest: — "Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: A person's inclination overpowers him every day and seeks to kill him, as it says, 'The wicked one watches the righteous and seeks to kill him' (Tehillim 37:32); and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him, he could not overcome it, as it says, 'Hashem will not abandon him into his hand' (Tehillim 37:33)."

586.label: Kiddushin 30b
586.rest: — "Rabbi Shimon ben Levi said: A person's inclination overpowers him every day and seeks to kill him, as it says, 'The wicked watches the righteous and seeks to kill him' (Tehillim 37:32); and were it not that the Holy One helps him, he could not withstand it, as it says, 'Hashem will not leave him in his hand' (37:33)."

587.label: Pesachim 113b
587.rest: — "Six things were said of the horse: it loves immorality, loves war, has a haughty spirit, despises sleep, eats much and excretes little; and some say it even seeks to kill its master in battle."

588.label: Berachos 3b
588.rest: — "Rabbi Zeira said: Until midnight [David] would doze like a horse; from then on he would strengthen himself like a lion. Rav Ashi said: Until midnight he occupied himself with words of Torah; from then on, with songs and praises."

589.label: Sanhedrin 96a
589.rest: — "If at the reward of four steps that I paid to that wicked one, who ran after My honor, you wonder — when I pay the reward of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, who ran before Me like horses, how much more so!"

590.label: Yoma 86a: “R’ Chama b’Rabbi Chanina said: Great is teshuvah, for it brings healing to the world, as it says, ‘I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely’ (Hoshea 14:5).” He further contrasts “Return, backsliding children” (implying they were always wayward
590.rest: — teshuvah from love, which makes the very origin as innocent) with “I will heal your backslidings” (implying, as Rashi explains, one healed like a cured baal mum of whom “a trace of his name remains” — teshuvah from fear).

591.label: Midrash Tehillim 51
591.rest: — "'Be gracious to me, O God, according to Your kindness' (Tehillim 51:3) — to whom was David like? To one who had a wound in his hand and came to the physician and said: Can you heal me? He said: Yes, but your payment is small. He said: Please, take all I have, and do the rest of your own, and do kindness with me and have mercy on me. So David said to the Holy One: 'Be gracious to me according to Your kindness' — You are merciful; 'according to the abundance of Your mercies, blot out my transgressions.'"

592.label: Midrash Tehillim 51
592.rest: — "'Against You alone have I sinned' (Tehillim 51:6) — to whom was David like? To one who was broken and came to the physician, and the physician wondered and said: How great is your wound; I am greatly pained for you. He said: You are pained for me? Not for my own sake was I broken, but for the sake of your fee. So he said to the Holy One: 'Against You alone have I sinned' — if You accept me, all transgressors will make peace with You, for they look to me, and I am the witness to all who come into the world."

593.label: Tanchuma, Vayeshev 4
593.rest: — "So Adam said before the Holy One: Master of the world, two thousand years before You created Your world the Torah was with You as a nursling… and it is written in it, 'This is the Torah: a man who dies in a tent' (Bamidbar 19:14). Had You not prepared death for creatures, would You have written so in it? Rather, You came to hang the pretext on me — 'awesome in His dealings (alilah) with mankind' (Tehillim 66:5)."

594.label: Sotah 5a
594.rest: — "'With the crushed and lowly of spirit' (Yeshayahu 57:15): Rav Huna and Rav Chisda — one says, 'With Me is the crushed,' and the other says, 'I am with the crushed.'" Rashi: "With Me is the crushed" — I raise him up until he dwells beside Me; "I am with the crushed" — I lower My Shechinah to be beside him.

595.label: Rosh Hashanah 25a
595.rest: — "Rabbi Chiya saw the old moon still standing on the morning of the twenty-ninth. He threw a clod at it and said: Tonight we are to sanctify you, and you stand here?! Go, hide! Rebbi said to Rabbi Chiya: Go to Ein Tov, sanctify the month, and send me the sign: 'David, King of Israel, lives and endures.'"

596.label: Taanis 5b
596.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Yaakov Avinu did not die. He was asked: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed and the buriers buried? He answered: I am expounding a verse, as it says, 'And you, fear not, My servant Yaakov… for behold, I save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity' (Yirmeyahu 30:10) — it compares him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too he is alive." Rashi: he lives forever; they embalmed him because they thought he had died.

597.label: Yoma 86a
597.rest: — "But one who has chillul Hashem in his hand — teshuvah has no power to suspend, nor Yom Kippur to atone, nor suffering to cleanse; rather all of them suspend, and death cleanses… What is chillul Hashem? Rav said: Such as I, if I take meat from the butcher and do not pay at once. Rabbi Yochanan said: Such as I, if I walk four cubits without Torah and without tefillin."

598.label: Midrash Tehillim 19
598.rest: — "'Who can discern errors?' (Tehillim 19:13): Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai taught: How mighty are the righteous, who know how to win over their Creator and know how to praise! See how David praised his Creator: he began praising with the heavens…; he went on singing, and began to praise with the Torah… The Holy One said to him: David, what do you want?"

599.label: Shabbos 119b
599.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said: From where do we know that speech is like action? For it says, 'By the word of Hashem the heavens were made' (Tehillim 33:6)."

600.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 44
600.rest: — "All the prophets call Israel to teshuvah, but none like Hoshea. Yirmeyahu said, 'If you return, Israel, says Hashem, return to Me' (Yirmeyahu 4:1); Yeshayahu said, 'Seek Hashem while He may be found' (Yeshayahu 55:6) — and they do not teach Israel what to say. But Hoshea said, Do teshuvah, and teaches them with what to appease Him: 'Return, Israel… Take with you words and return to Hashem; say to Him: Forgive all iniquity' (Hoshea 14:2–3)."

601.label: Yoma 86b
601.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: Great is repentance, for deliberate sins become for him like merits… Here, when out of love; there [where they become like errors], when out of fear." (Rashi has no comment on this line.)

602.label: Yoma 86a
602.rest: — "Rabbi Masya ben Charash asked Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah in Rome: Have you heard the four divisions of atonement that Rabbi Yishmael would expound? He said: They are three, and teshuvah is with each one."

603.label: Yoma 86a
603.rest: — "Rabbi Levi said: Great is repentance, for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory, as it says, 'Return, Israel, unto (ad) Hashem your God' (Hoshea 14:2)." Rashi has no comment on this line.

604.label: Pesachim 50b
604.rest: — "Rava contrasted: It is written, 'For Your kindness is great unto the heavens' (Tehillim 57:11), and it is written, 'great above the heavens' (Tehillim 108:5). Here, for those who do it lishmah; there, for those who do it not lishmah — as Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: A person should always occupy himself with Torah and mitzvos even not lishmah, for from not lishmah he comes to lishmah."

605.label: Zohar I 219b (Vayechi)
605.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah said: There is no sin in the world that has no teshuvah except this one, and there is no wicked person who does not see the face of the Shechinah except this one, as it is written, 'Evil shall not dwell with You' (Tehillim 5:5)."

606.label: Rosh Hashanah 18a
606.rest: — "Rava said: With sacrifice and offering it is not atoned for, but it is atoned for with Torah. Abaye said: With sacrifice and offering it is not atoned for, but it is atoned for with Torah and acts of kindness. Rabbah and Abaye descended from the house of Eli: Rabbah, who occupied himself with Torah, lived forty years; Abaye, who occupied himself with Torah and acts of kindness, lived sixty years."

607.label: Nedarim 22b
607.rest: — "Rav Ada son of Rabbi Chanina said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Yehoshua alone, which contains the apportioning of Eretz Yisrael. What is the reason? 'For in much wisdom is much anger' (Koheles 1:18)." Rashi: because they rebelled, much wisdom — the other books — was added, to burden them further.

608.label: Berachos 5a
608.rest: — "Whoever is able to occupy himself with Torah and does not, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings upon him ugly sufferings that disturb him, as it says, 'I was mute with silence, I was still from good, and my pain was stirred' (Tehillim 39:3) — and 'good' means only Torah, as it says, 'For I have given you good teaching; do not forsake My Torah' (Mishlei 4:2)."

609.label: Menachos 110a
609.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: What is meant by 'This is the Torah of the burnt-offering, of the meal-offering, of the sin-offering and of the guilt-offering' (Vayikra 7:37)? Whoever occupies himself with Torah is as though he offered a burnt-offering, a meal-offering, a sin-offering and a guilt-offering."

610.label: Sotah 46a
610.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan ben Shaul said: Why did the Torah say to bring a calf into a valley? The Holy One said: Let something that has not produced fruit come and be beheaded in a place that does not produce fruit, and atone for one whom they did not allow to produce fruit. What fruit? … mitzvos."

611.label: Tanchuma, Noach 2
611.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah HaLevi said: When a person departs the world without children, he is distressed and weeps. The Holy One says to him: Why do you weep — because you produced no fruit in the world? You have fruit more beautiful than children. He says: Master of the world, what fruit did I produce? He says: The Torah, in which it is written, 'The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life' (Mishlei 11:30)."

612.label: Shabbos 88b
612.rest: — "This is what Rava said: For those who go to its right, it is an elixir of life; for those who go to its left, an elixir of death."

613.label: Moed Katan 9b
613.rest: — "Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta took leave of Rebbi. His father said to him: Go to him so that he bless you. He said to him: May it be His will that you not shame and not be shamed. He came to his father; he said to him: What did he say to you? He said: Mere words he said to me."

614.label: Berachos 14a
614.rest: — "'And he shall rest satisfied (save'a); he shall not be visited by evil' (Mishlei 19:23) — do not read save'a but sheva (seven)."

615.label: Nedarim 19b
615.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah says in the name of Rabbi Tarfon: Neither of them is a nazir, for nezirus was given only with clear expression (hafla'ah)."

616.label: Rashi, Arachin 2a (s.v. mufla samuch l'ish)
616.rest: — A boy of twelve years and a day, who is close to manhood… and he is called mufla because they check whether he knows how to express explicitly (lehafli) and to state for whom he vowed and for whom he consecrated.

617.label: Yoma 86a
617.rest: — "Rabbi Levi said: Great is repentance, for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory, as it says, 'Return, Israel, unto (ad) Hashem your God' (Hoshea 14:2)." Rashi has no comment on this line.

618.label: Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 5
618.rest: — "When he mentions the Name, he should intend the meaning of its reading as Adnus — that He is Master of all; and intend its writing with yud-hei — that He was, is and will be; and when he mentions Elokim, he should intend that He is mighty, all-capable, Master of all powers."

619.label: Zohar I 129a–b (Chayei Sarah)
619.rest: — "Fortunate are the masters of teshuvah, for in one hour, in one day, in one moment, they come near to the Holy One — which was not so even for the completely righteous, who came near to the Holy One over many years."

620.label: Yoma 75a
620.rest: — "'White' — for it whitens the sins of Israel." Rashi: since they worried that manna might not fall the next day, they would subject their hearts to the Omnipresent.

621.label: Yoma 76a
621.rest: — "Why did the manna not fall for Israel once a year? … So too Israel: one who had four or five sons would worry and say, Perhaps the manna will not fall tomorrow, and all will die of hunger; thus they were all found directing their hearts to their Father in Heaven."

622.label: Rosh Hashanah 29a (Mishnah)
622.rest: — "'And it was, when Moshe raised his hand, Israel prevailed' (Shemos 17:11) — do the hands of Moshe make war or break war? Rather, to tell you: as long as Israel looked upward and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven, they prevailed; and if not, they fell."

623.label: Bartenura, Rosh Hashanah 3:8
623.rest: — "Since [the Mishnah] spoke above of the intention of the heart, it also teaches this, which contains 'when they direct their hearts to their Father in Heaven, they prevail.'"

624.label: Rosh Hashanah 18a
624.rest: — "'Seek Hashem while He may be found' (Yeshayahu 55:6) — for an individual, when? Rabbah bar Avuha said: These are the ten days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur."

625.label: Yerushalmi, Berachos 5:2
625.rest: — "Rebbi said: I wonder how they abolished 'Who graciously grants knowledge' on Shabbos: if there is no knowledge, from where is there prayer? … If there is no knowledge, from where is there havdalah?"

626.label: Sukkah 52b
626.rest: — "Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: A person's inclination overpowers him every day and seeks to kill him, as it says, 'The wicked one watches the righteous and seeks to kill him' (Tehillim 37:32); and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him, he could not overcome it, as it says, 'Hashem will not abandon him into his hand' (Tehillim 37:33)."

627.label: Sukkah 52a
627.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah expounded: In the time to come the Holy One will bring the evil inclination and slaughter it before the righteous and before the wicked. To the righteous it appears like a high mountain, and to the wicked like a hairsbreadth. These weep and those weep: the righteous weep and say, How were we able to conquer such a high mountain! … And Abaye said: Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than he."

628.label: Chagigah 15a
628.rest: — "… A heavenly voice went forth and said: 'Return, wayward children' (Yirmeyahu 3:14) — except Acher."

629.label: Avos 6:2
629.rest: — "Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Every day a heavenly voice goes forth from Mount Chorev and proclaims: Woe to the creatures for the insult to the Torah… And it says, 'The writing was the writing of God, engraved (charus) on the tablets' (Shemos 32:16) — do not read charus but cheirus (freedom), for there is no free man except one who occupies himself with the study of Torah."

630.label: Zohar II 88b (Yisro)
630.rest: — "Come and see: on all six days of the week, when the hour of the Minchah prayer arrives, harsh judgment rules and all judgments are aroused; but on the day of Shabbos, when the time of the Minchah prayer arrives, the Will of all wills is found, and the Holy Atika reveals His will, and all judgments are subdued, and will and joy are found in all."

631.label: Eichah Rabbah 5:21
631.rest: — "Israel said before the Holy One: Master of the world, it depends on You — 'Bring us back to You, Hashem, and we shall return' (Eichah 5:21). He said to them: It depends on you — 'Return to Me, and I will return to you' (Malachi 3:7)."

632.label: Mechilta, Yisro, Bachodesh 7
632.rest: — "'Remember' (Shemos 20:8) and 'Keep' (Devarim 5:12): remember it before it comes, and keep it after it goes."

633.label: Rashi, Bereishis 1:1
633.rest: — "'Bereishis' — for the sake of the Torah, which is called 'the beginning (reishis) of His way' (Mishlei 8:22), and for the sake of Israel, who are called 'the beginning (reishis) of His produce' (Yirmeyahu 2:3)."

634.label: Yoma 75b
634.rest: — "'Man ate the bread of the mighty (abirim)' (Tehillim 78:25) — bread that the ministering angels eat; the words of Rabbi Akiva. When this was said before Rabbi Yishmael, he said: Go and tell Akiva: Akiva, you erred! Do the ministering angels eat bread? Is it not said, 'I did not eat bread or drink water' (Devarim 9:9)? Rather, 'abirim' means bread absorbed in the 248 limbs (evarim)."

635.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
635.rest: — "Chochmah is the brain, which is thought within; Binah is the heart, and with it the heart understands; and of these two it is written, 'The hidden things belong to Hashem our God' (Devarim 29:28)."

636.label: Shabbos 89b
636.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: The Holy One said to Israel: If your sins be like these years (shanim), which are arranged and come from the six days of Creation until now, they shall be white as snow (Yeshayahu 1:18)."

637.label: Rosh Hashanah 21b
637.rest: — “Rav and Shmuel disagreed. One said: Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world, and all were given to Moshe except one, as it is said: You made him a little less than God.” The identification of the fiftieth gate particularly with penitents is Rav Tzadok's development here; it is not stated in this sentence of the Gemara.

638.label: Berachos 34b
638.rest: — "R. Abahu said: In the place where ba'alei teshuvah stand, the completely righteous cannot stand, as it says, 'Peace, peace, to the far and to the near' — the far first, then the near." This disputes R. Yochanan, who holds the completely righteous are greater. Rashi: "the near" is one who was far from sin all his days, a tzaddik from the start.

639.label: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 5:5
639.rest: — "He does not know with a knowledge that is outside Him, like people, who and their knowledge are two; rather He, may His Name be exalted, and His knowledge are one, and a person's mind cannot grasp this clearly. And just as a person cannot grasp and find the truth of the Creator, as it says, 'For man shall not see Me and live' (Shemos 33:20), so a person cannot grasp and find the Creator's knowledge. This is what the prophet said: 'For My thoughts are not your thoughts, nor your ways My ways' (Yeshayahu 55:8)."

640.label: Avodah Zarah 5a
640.rest: — "As Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonasan: What is meant by 'The utterance of David son of Yishai, and the utterance of the man raised on high (hukam al)' (II Shmuel 23:1)? The utterance of David son of Yishai, who raised up the yoke (ullah) of teshuvah."

641.label: Avodah Zarah 4b
641.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: David was not fit for that deed, nor were Israel fit for that deed. David was not fit for that deed, as it is written, 'And my heart is slain within me' (Tehillim 109:22)."

642.label: Yoma 22b
642.rest: — "For six months David was stricken with tzaraas, and the Sanhedrin separated from him." And of the episode of Bas Sheva: "There, he was punished for it, as it is written, 'And he shall pay for the lamb fourfold' (II Shmuel 12:6) — the child, Amnon, Tamar and Avshalom."

643.label: Sanhedrin 107a
643.rest: — "'Against You alone have I sinned' (Tehillim 51:6): David said before the Holy One: It is revealed and known before You that had I wished to subdue my inclination, I could have subdued it; but I said: Let them not say, the servant defeated his master."

644.label: Shabbos 30a
644.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: What is meant by 'Make me a sign for good, that those who hate me may see and be ashamed' (Tehillim 86:17)? David said before the Holy One: Master of the world, forgive me for that sin. He said: It is forgiven you. He said: Make me a sign in my lifetime. He said: In your lifetime I will not make it known; in the lifetime of Shlomo your son I will make it known."

645.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 21, 57b
645.rest: — "Purim is named after Yom HaKippurim (a day 'like Purim'), for in the future they will delight on it and change it from affliction to delight."

646.label: Megillah 12a
646.rest: — "The students of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai asked him: Why were the enemies of Israel in that generation liable to destruction? He said to them: You tell me. They said to him: Because they partook of the feast of that wicked one… He said to them: Because they bowed to the image."

647.label: Shabbos 88a
647.rest: — "'They stood beneath the mountain': this teaches that the Holy One held the mountain over them like a barrel and said, 'If you accept the Torah, good; if not, there will be your burial'… Rava said: Even so, they accepted it again in the days of Achashveirosh, as it is written, 'The Jews fulfilled and accepted.'" Rashi: out of love for the miracle done for them.

648.label: Megillah 7b
648.rest: — “Rava said: A person is obligated to become intoxicated on Purim until he does not know between ‘cursed is Haman’ and ‘blessed is Mordechai.’”

649.label: Yoma 81b
649.rest: — "Chiya bar Rav of Difti taught: 'And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth' (Vayikra 23:32) — do they fast on the ninth? Do they not fast on the tenth? Rather, to tell you: whoever eats and drinks on the ninth, Scripture regards him as though he fasted on the ninth and the tenth." Rashi: prepare yourself on the ninth so that you will be able to fast on the tenth.

650.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 9b (s.v. ke'ilu)
650.rest: — According to Rabbi Yishmael there is no such exposition; "and with this it is well that it does not say there, 'All agree regarding Erev Yom Kippur that we also require "for you,"' as it says there regarding Atzeres."

651.label: Pesachim 68b
651.rest: — “Mar son of Ravina fasted throughout the year, except for Shavuos, Purim, and the eve of Yom Kippur. Shavuos is the day on which Torah was given. Concerning Purim it is written, Days of feasting and joy. Concerning the eve of Yom Kippur, Chiyya bar Rav of Difti taught: Whoever eats and drinks on the ninth, Scripture accounts it to him as if he had fasted on the ninth and tenth.”

652.label: Sanhedrin 104a
652.rest: — "'She has become like a widow' (Eichah 1:1): Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: Like a widow, but not an actual widow; rather, like a woman whose husband went to a country overseas and intends to return to her."

653.label: Tur, Orach Chaim 604
653.rest: — It is a mitzvah to eat and to make the meal plentiful on Erev Yom Kippur; and the Midrash tells of the tailor who bought a fish for twelve dinars on Erev Yom Kippur, and was rewarded for honoring the day.

654.label: Zohar III 65b (Acharei Mos)
654.rest: — "After she gave birth, she brought forth a male son and set him before her, and the vav must be written; he inherits the inheritance of father and mother… and from him the daughter is nourished. Therefore vav-hei must be written together, just as the first yud-hei are together and must not be separated."

655.label: Tosafos, Rosh Hashanah 27a (s.v. kemaan)
655.rest: — Both views are the words of the living God: in Tishrei it arose in His thought to create the world, and it was not actually created until Nissan.

656.label: Rosh Hashanah 16b
656.rest: — "Rabbi Kruspedai said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Three books are opened on Rosh Hashanah: one of the completely wicked, one of the completely righteous, and one of the intermediate. The completely righteous are written and sealed immediately for life; the completely wicked are written and sealed immediately for death; the intermediate are held in suspense from Rosh Hashanah until Yom Kippur: if they merit, they are written for life; if they do not merit, they are written for death."

657.label: Shabbos 118b
657.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: Whoever gives delight to the Shabbos is granted the wishes of his heart, as it says, 'Delight in Hashem, and He will give you the wishes of your heart' (Tehillim 37:4). This delight — I do not know what it is; when it says, 'And you shall call the Shabbos a delight' (Yeshayahu 58:13), it is the delight of Shabbos." Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: he is saved from the subjugation of the exiles.

658.label: Zohar III 29b (Tzav)
658.rest: — "So Torah scholars, the children of the King and the Queen, are called Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim. They have nothing of their own, for they are not craftsmen like other servants… their reward is in this world and in the World to Come, to delight them with every kind of food and drink and to honor them with fine garments, like Shabbos, of which it is said, 'Honor it with clean clothing'; whatever a person does for Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim he should do for them."

659.label: Pesikta Rabbasi 47
659.rest: — "'From there he searches out food (chafar ochel)' (Iyov 39:29) — from there he would scout out for himself the food of the year, whether it would be good or bad… and chafar is a term of scouting, as in 'and let them search out (vayachperu) the land for us' (Devarim 1:22)."

660.label: Beitzah 16a
660.rest: — "All of a person's sustenance is allotted to him from Rosh Hashanah until Yom Kippur, except for the expense of Shabbosos, the expense of Yamim Tovim, and the expense of his children's Torah study: if he spends less, they give him less; and if he spends more, they give him more."

661.label: Bava Metzia 114b
661.rest: — "Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says: The graves of idolaters do not defile, as it says, 'And you, My flock, the flock of My pasture, you are man (adam)' (Yechezkel 34:31) — you are called 'adam,' and idolaters are not called 'adam.'"

662.label: Rashi, Yoma 81b (s.v. kol ha'ochel)
662.rest: — And so the verse means, "You shall afflict yourselves on the ninth": that is, prepare yourself on the ninth so that you will be able to fast on the tenth; and since the verse put it in the language of affliction, it teaches that it is as if he fasted on the ninth.

663.label: Rosh, Yoma 8:22
663.rest: — It is a mitzvah to eat and drink much on Erev Yom Kippur; and he brings from the Midrash the story of the Jewish tailor who bought a fish for twelve dinars on Erev Yom Kippur, and was rewarded for honoring the day.

664.label: Zohar III 68b (Acharei Mos)
664.rest: — "'You shall afflict your souls (nafshoseichem)' (Vayikra 16:29) — 'your souls' it says, for Israel are found meritorious before the holy King and their will is toward the Holy One, to cleave to Him so that their sins be atoned. Therefore whoever eats and drinks on the ninth and delights his soul with food and drink is found on the tenth with affliction of the soul in two portions, and it is as though he fasted the ninth and the tenth."

665.label: Zohar III 68b (Acharei Mos)
665.rest: — "'You shall afflict your souls' (Vayikra 16:29)… and therefore whoever eats and drinks on the ninth and delights his soul with food and drink, on the tenth there is found an affliction of the soul in two portions, and it is as though he fasted the ninth and the tenth."

666.label: Yoma 86a
666.rest: — "If one transgressed a positive commandment and repented, he does not move from there before he is forgiven, as it says, 'Return, wayward children' (Yirmeyahu 3:22). If one transgressed a negative commandment and repented, teshuvah suspends and Yom Kippur atones, as it says, 'For on this day He shall atone for you' (Vayikra 16:30). If one transgressed [sins punishable by] kares or death by beis din and repented, teshuvah and Yom Kippur suspend and suffering cleanses, as it says, 'Then I will visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with plagues' (Tehillim 89:33)."

667.label: Zohar III (Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas)
667.rest: — "And they are four faces, Yud-Hei-Vav-Hei, and four wings, Adnus — corresponding to the four garments of gold and the four garments of white that the Kohen wore to atone for Israel."

668.label: Zohar II (Va'era)
668.rest: — "'And you shall love Hashem your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might' (Devarim 6:5): 'with all your heart' — the right and the left, which are called the good inclination and the evil inclination; 'and with all your soul' — the soul of David, which was given between them; 'and with all your might' — to include them above, in the place that has no measure."

669.label: Bechoros 55a
669.rest: — "The essence (zachrusa) of the blood is the liver, in line with Rabbi Yitzchak, for Rabbi Yitzchak said: A liver that dissolved defiles in the measure of a revi'is."

670.label: Berachos 61a–b
670.rest: — "The kidneys counsel, the heart understands, the tongue shapes [the words], the mouth completes them… the liver angers, the gall drops a drop upon it and calms it."

671.label: Tosafos, Sotah 5a (s.v. adam), citing Rabbeinu Chananel
671.rest: — "This is the clear blood from which the heart is founded; there is in it only the weight of twenty-five sela'im, which is a revi'is of a log."

672.label: Berachos 17a
672.rest: — “Rav would often say: The World to Come is unlike this world. In the World to Come there is no eating or drinking, no procreation, no commerce, no jealousy, no hatred, and no competition. Rather, the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads and delight in the radiance of the Divine Presence, as it is said: 'They beheld God, and ate and drank.'” Rav Tzadok identifies these crowns with those bestowed at Sinai and destined to be restored; that identification joins this statement with the Shabbos 88a passage quoted earlier.

673.label: Berachos 57b
673.rest: — “Shabbos is one-sixtieth of the World to Come.”

674.label: Shabbos 86b
674.rest: — “The Rabbis taught: On the sixth of the month the Ten Commandments were given to Israel; Rabbi Yosei says, on its seventh. Rava said: All agree that they came to the wilderness of Sinai on Rosh Chodesh. ... And all agree that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbos. ... Their dispute concerns the fixing of the month.”

675.label: Shabbos 86b
675.rest: — “All agree that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbos.”

676.label: Bava Kamma 60b
676.rest: — "The Holy One said: I must pay for the fire that I kindled. I kindled a fire in Tziyon, as it says, 'And He kindled a fire in Tziyon, and it consumed its foundations' (Eichah 4:11), and I will rebuild it with fire, as it says, 'And I will be for her a wall of fire all around, and for glory I will be in her midst' (Zechariah 2:9)."

677.label: Gittin 68a–b
677.rest: — The account of Ashmedai, who cast Shlomo out of his kingdom and sat upon his throne, while Shlomo went about saying, "I, Koheles, was king over Israel in Yerushalayim" (Koheles 1:12).

678.label: Yoma 75b
678.rest: — "'Man ate the bread of the mighty (abirim)' (Tehillim 78:25) — bread that the ministering angels eat; the words of Rabbi Akiva. When this was said before Rabbi Yishmael, he said: Go and tell Akiva: Akiva, you erred! Do the ministering angels eat bread? Is it not said, 'I did not eat bread or drink water' (Devarim 9:9)? Rather, 'abirim' means bread absorbed in the 248 limbs (evarim)."

679.label: Zohar III 230a (Pinchas, Ra'aya Meheimna)
679.rest: — "He is truth (emes), and She is faith (emunah)."

680.label: Pesachim 56a
680.rest: — "Yaakov wished to reveal to his sons the end of days, and the Shechinah departed from him… His sons said to him: 'Hear, Israel, Hashem is our God, Hashem is One' — they said: Just as in your heart there is only One, so in our heart there is only One. At that moment Yaakov Avinu opened and said: Blessed is the Name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever."

681.label: Etz Chaim, Shaar 1, Anaf 2
681.rest: — The kabbalists were divided: some wrote that the ten sefiros stand in order, one below the other; others wrote that they are arranged in lines, right, left and middle: Chochmah, Chesed, Netzach one above the other in the right line; Binah, Gevurah, Hod in the left line; and Daas, Tiferes, Yesod, Malchus in the middle line; and others say they are in the form of concentric circles.

682.label: Chagigah 3a
682.rest: — "Rava expounded: What is meant by 'How beautiful are your feet in sandals, O daughter of the noble (bas nadiv)' (Shir HaShirim 7:2)? How beautiful are the feet of Israel when they go up for the festival! 'Daughter of the noble' — the daughter of Avraham Avinu, who is called noble, as it says, 'The nobles of the nations are gathered, the people of the God of Avraham' (Tehillim 47:10) — the God of Avraham and not the God of Yitzchak and Yaakov? Rather, the God of Avraham, who was the first of the converts."

683.label: Shemos Rabbah 33:8
683.rest: — "When the Holy One spoke to Moshe about the Mishkan, he said: Master of the world, are Israel able to make it? The Holy One said to him: Even one of Israel can make it, as it says, 'From every man whose heart moves him' (Shemos 25:2)."

684.label: Shabbos 31a
684.rest: — "Reish Lakish said: What is meant by 'And He shall be the faith of your times, a strength of salvations, wisdom and knowledge' (Yeshayahu 33:6)? 'Faith' — this is the order of Zera'im; 'your times' — the order of Mo'ed; 'strength' — the order of Nashim; 'salvations' — the order of Nezikin; 'wisdom' — the order of Kodashim; 'and knowledge' — the order of Taharos."

685.label: Tosafos, Shabbos 31a (s.v. emunas)
685.rest: — "'Faith (emunas)' — this is the Order of Zera'im: the Yerushalmi explains, that he trusts in the Life of the worlds and sows."

686.label: Avos 4:1
686.rest: — "Ben Zoma says: Who is wise? One who learns from every person… Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination, as it says, 'Better is one slow to anger than a mighty man, and one who rules his spirit than one who captures a city' (Mishlei 16:32)."

687.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
687.rest: — "Chesed is the right arm, Gevurah the left arm, Tiferes the body, Netzach and Hod the two thighs, Yesod the completion of the body, the sign of the holy covenant; Malchus is the mouth — we call it the Oral Torah."

688.label: Chullin 91b
688.rest: — "'Israel, in whom I glory' (Yeshayahu 49:3) — you are the one whose image is engraved above."

689.label: Sukkah 52a
689.rest: — "Our Rabbis taught: To Mashiach ben David, who is destined to be revealed speedily in our days, the Holy One says: Ask of Me something and I will give it to you… And when he sees that Mashiach ben Yosef was killed, he says before Him: Master of the world, I ask of You only life. He says to him: Before you said it, David your father already prophesied of you, as it says, 'Life he asked of You; You gave it to him' (Tehillim 21:5)."

690.label: Avodah Zarah 4b
690.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: David was not fit for that deed, nor were Israel fit for that deed. David was not fit for that deed, as it is written, 'And my heart is slain within me' (Tehillim 109:22)."

691.label: Avodah Zarah 5a
691.rest: — "As Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonasan: What is meant by 'The utterance of David son of Yishai, and the utterance of the man raised on high (hukam al)' (II Shmuel 23:1)? The utterance of David son of Yishai, who raised up the yoke (ullah) of teshuvah."

692.label: Yoma 86b
692.rest: — “Rabbi Meir would say: Great is repentance, for on account of one individual who repents the whole world is forgiven, as it is said, I shall heal their backsliding; I shall love them freely, for My anger has turned away from him. It does not say from them, but from him.” The identification of that individual with Mashiach, who awakens repentance in all Israel, is Rav Tzadok's development of this teaching.

693.label: Yerushalmi, Yoma 5:2
693.rest: — "Every year that I entered the Holy of Holies, an old man dressed in white and wrapped in white would enter with me and leave with me… They asked before Rabbi Abahu: But it is written, 'And no man shall be in the Tent of Meeting when he comes to atone in the Sanctuary, until he goes out' (Vayikra 16:17) — even those of whom it is written, 'and the likeness of their faces was the face of a man' (Yechezkel 1:10), shall not be in the Tent of Meeting!"

694.label: Zohar III, 201b (Balak)
694.rest: — “These three mouths were created on the eve of the Sabbath at twilight. When the day became holy, the mouth appointed over all the other mouths ascended. Which is it? That day which ascended and became holy in everything, which is called ‘the mouth of the Lord.’ ... When the day became holy, the mouth that rules over everything ascended: the mouth of the Lord.”

695.label: Sefer Yetzirah 4
695.rest: — "He made the letter tav king… and formed with it… the day of Shabbos in the year, and the mouth in the soul."

696.label: Zohar I 47b (Bereishis)
696.rest: — “‘And God finished on the seventh day’: this is Torah she'b'al peh, which is the seventh day.”

697.label: Zohar II 205a (Vayakhel)
697.rest: — "This day is a day of souls and not a day of the body, for it is the dominion of the bundle of souls, and upper and lower beings all stand in one union, in the crown of the holy supernal additional spirit."

698.label: Yoma 52b (Mishnah)
698.rest: — "He reached the Ark, placed the firepan between the two poles, heaped the incense upon the coals, and the whole house filled with smoke. He went out by the way he had entered, and prayed a short prayer in the outer chamber; and he did not prolong his prayer, so as not to frighten Israel."

699.label: Mishnah, Yoma 1:3
699.rest: — "The elders of the court said to him: My master, Kohen Gadol (ishi kohen gadol), read with your own mouth, perhaps you have forgotten or perhaps you never learned."

700.label: Yoma 71a
700.rest: — "If he found him in the marketplace, he would say to him: My master the Kohen Gadol, we have done your mission. If he found him in his house, he would say to him: [To] the One Who gives life to the living, we have done His mission." Rashi: the One Who gives life to the living — the Holy One, blessed be He.

701.label: R. Yisrael of Kozhnitz, Avodas Yisrael, Yom Kippur
701.rest: — On Yoma 71b (“Let the descendants of the nations come in peace, who do the deed of Aharon”): “Our master the Maggid explained of Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha, who entered to offer the incense and saw Achtariel, that although he was great among the sages, he merited that wondrous vision not by his own merit alone but through the Tanna of his generation, who raised him in his holiness. Accordingly, the Kohen in the days of Shemaya and Avtalyon, in the Second Temple, who was not so worthy, merited to enter the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur only through Shemaya and Avtalyon, the heads of the generation, who raised him to that level. Therefore they answered the Kohen Gadol that he should not be haughty toward them, for they ‘did the deed of Aharon’ — the essence of the service was through them.”

702.label: Yoma 71b
702.rest: — "At last Shemayah and Avtalyon came to take leave of the Kohen Gadol. He said to them: Let the descendants of the nations come in peace. They said to him: Let the descendants of the nations come in peace, who do the deed of Aharon; and let not the descendant of Aharon come in peace, who does not do the deed of Aharon." Rashi: the deed of Aharon — pursuing peace.

703.label: Rashi, Rosh Hashanah 9a (s.v. kol ha'ochel)
