1197.rest: — “In Taanis: ‘Great is the day of rain like the day the Torah was given, as it says, “My lesson (likchi) shall drop as the rain” (Devarim 32:2)… Rava said: more than the day the Torah was given.’ This alludes to the festival of Shemini Atzeres, which they called ‘the day of rain’ because on it we bless ‘Who makes the rain fall’… Therefore Chazal alluded: ‘Great is the day of rain’ — Shemini Atzeres — ‘like the day the Torah was given,’ which is Shavuos; but Rava disagreed and said its level is greater, for on it the Oral Torah drips down drop by drop, as is known.”

1198.label: Taanis 7a
1198.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said: The day of rain is as great as the day the Torah was given… Rava said: Greater than the day the Torah was given, as it says, 'My teaching (likchi) shall drop like the rain' (Devarim 32:2) — who is compared to whom? The lesser is compared to the greater." Rashi: the verse compares teaching to rain.

1199.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 13, 29b
1199.rest: — "Shemini Atzeres is a festival in its own right; on it is the welling forth of the Torah, to water the tree that is planted in the garden, and its roots and branches are like the circle (chug) of the earth, for all the festivals are celebrated in it."

1200.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a
1200.rest: — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

1201.label: Zohar I 117a (Vayera)
1201.rest: — "And in the six hundredth year of the sixth [millennium] the gates of wisdom above and the springs of wisdom below will be opened, and the world will be prepared to enter the seventh… and your sign: 'In the six hundredth year of Noach's life… all the springs of the great deep were split open' (Bereishis 7:11)."

1202.label: Taanis 2a
1202.rest: — "From where do we know it is with prayer? As it was taught: 'To love Hashem your God and to serve Him with all your heart' (Devarim 11:13) — what is the service that is in the heart? You must say: this is prayer."

1203.label: Zohar III 96a (Emor)
1203.rest: — "'On the eighth day an Atzeres' — what is Atzeres? The place where all are bound as one is called Atzeres, a gathering… All those days were the days of the meals of the branches of the Tree, and therefore seventy bulls; afterward is the joy of the body of the Tree itself and the joy of the Torah, and for its sake it is one day, Atzeres — the joy of the Torah."

1204.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 13, 29b
1204.rest: — "Shemini Atzeres is a festival in its own right; on it is the welling forth of the Torah, to water the tree that is planted in the garden, and its roots and branches are like the circle (chug) of the earth, for all the festivals are celebrated in it."

1205.label: Berachos 5b
1205.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Granted Torah and kindness, as it is written, 'Through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned' (Mishlei 16:6): 'kindness' is acts of kindness… and 'truth' is Torah, as it is said, 'Buy truth and do not sell it' (Mishlei 23:23)."

1206.label: Pesachim 68b
1206.rest: — "One verse says, 'an assembly to Hashem your God,' and one verse says, 'an assembly shall it be to you.' Rabbi Eliezer holds: either all of it for Hashem or all of it for you; Rabbi Yehoshua holds: divide it — half for Hashem and half for you." The Gemara continues: all agree that on Atzeres (Shavuos) "for you" is also needed. Rashi: that one rejoices on it with food and drink.

1207.label: Zohar II 186a (Tetzaveh)
1207.rest: — "'This month shall be for you' (Shemos 12:2): it is Mine, but I have handed it to you, so it is yours openly; but the seventh is Mine, therefore it is concealed. Your month follows the order of the letters — Aviv, which is Alef-Beis-Gimmel in order; but the seventh month, which is Mine, is from the end of the letters — Tishrei. Why? You from below to above, and I from above to below."

1208.label: Sotah 5a
1208.rest: — "'With the crushed and lowly of spirit' (Yeshayahu 57:15): Rav Huna and Rav Chisda — one says, 'With Me is the crushed,' and the other says, 'I am with the crushed.'" Rashi: "With Me is the crushed" — I raise him up until he dwells beside Me; "I am with the crushed" — I lower My Shechinah to be beside him.

1209.label: Mechilta, Beshalach, Shirah 3
1209.rest: — "'This is my God and I will glorify Him' (Shemos 15:2). Rabbi Eliezer says: From where do you say that a maidservant saw at the Sea what Yeshayahu and Yechezkel did not see? For it says, 'and through the prophets I was imaged' (Hoshea 12:11)… When the Holy One, blessed be He, was revealed at the Sea, no one needed to ask, 'Which is the King?'"

1210.label: Tikkunei Zohar (77b)
1210.rest: — "'Let there be light' — this is Pesach, the night of the fourteenth; 'and there was light' — Rosh Hashanah, of which it says 'and it was the day.'" These words stand in Tikkun 36 (77b); the printed reference says Tikkun 30.

1211.label: Taanis 30b
1211.rest: — "Granted Yom Kippur, because it has pardon and forgiveness, and it is the day on which the second Tablets were given; but the fifteenth of Av — what is it? Rav Yehudah said in the name of Shmuel: It is the day on which the tribes were permitted to marry into one another."

1212.label: Shabbos 30a
1212.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: What is meant by 'Make me a sign for good, that those who hate me may see and be ashamed' (Tehillim 86:17)? David said before the Holy One: Master of the world, forgive me for that sin. He said: It is forgiven you. He said: Make me a sign in my lifetime. He said: In your lifetime I will not make it known; in the lifetime of Shlomo your son I will make it known."

1213.label: Rosh Hashanah 25a
1213.rest: — "Rabbi Chiya saw the old moon still standing on the morning of the twenty-ninth. He threw a clod at it and said: Tonight we are to sanctify you, and you stand here?! Go, hide! Rebbi said to Rabbi Chiya: Go to Ein Tov, sanctify the month, and send me the sign: 'David, King of Israel, lives and endures.'"

1214.label: Avodah Zarah 11a (so too Berachos 57b)
1214.rest: — "'Two nations (goyim) are in your womb' (Bereishis 25:23): Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav: Do not read goyim but ge'im (proud ones) — this is Antoninus and Rebbi, from whose tables neither lettuce nor cucumber nor radish ever ceased, neither in summer nor in winter."

1215.label: Kesubos 104a
1215.rest: — "At the time of Rebbi's passing he raised his ten fingers upward and said: Master of the world, it is revealed and known before You that I toiled with my ten fingers in Torah and did not benefit even with my little finger; may it be Your will that there be peace in my repose. A heavenly voice went forth: 'He shall come in peace; they shall rest on their beds' (Yeshayahu 57:2)."

1216.label: Taanis 5b
1216.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Yaakov Avinu did not die. He was asked: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed and the buriers buried? He answered: I am expounding a verse, as it says, 'And you, fear not, My servant Yaakov… for behold, I save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity' (Yirmeyahu 30:10) — it compares him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too he is alive." Rashi: he lives forever; they embalmed him because they thought he had died.

1217.label: Zohar III 104b (Emor)
1217.rest: — "'On the eighth day it shall be an assembly (atzeres) for you' (Bamidbar 29:35) — for this day is of the King alone, His joy with Israel. A parable of a king who invited guests, and all the members of his palace occupied themselves with them. Afterward the king said: Until now you and I occupied ourselves with the guests, and you offered offerings for the other nations every day; from now on, you and I will rejoice one day."

1218.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 13, 29b
1218.rest: — "Shemini Atzeres is a festival in its own right; on it is the welling forth of the Torah, to water the tree that is planted in the garden, and its roots and branches are like the circle (chug) of the earth, for all the festivals are celebrated in it."

1219.label: Midrash Tehillim 114:4
1219.rest: — "'The sea saw and fled' (Tehillim 114:3): the sea saw Israel contending with one another to sanctify His Name… Another explanation: it saw the coffin of Yosef descending into the sea. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Let it flee before the one who fled, as it is written, 'and he fled and went outside' (Bereishis 39:12)."

1220.label: Moed Katan 16b
1220.rest: — "Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonasan: What is meant by 'The word of David son of Yishai, and the word of the man who was raised on high (hukam al)' (II Shmuel 23:1)? The word of David son of Yishai, who raised up the yoke (ullah) of teshuvah." Rashi: he repented first and opened the way for penitents.

1221.label: Sukkah 48a
1221.rest: — "From where are these words? As our Rabbis taught: 'And you shall be only (ach) joyful' (Devarim 16:15) — to include the night of the last Yom Tov of the festival."

1222.label: Sukkah 2a
1222.rest: — "Rava said: From here: 'In sukkos you shall dwell seven days' (Vayikra 23:42) — the Torah said: All seven days, leave your permanent dwelling and dwell in a temporary dwelling."

1223.label: Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah 3
1223.rest: — "David the King further said: I feared out of my joy, and I rejoiced out of my fear, and my love rose above them all."

1224.label: Sukkah 29b
1224.rest: — "Rav said: Because of four things the property of householders goes to the treasury…; and haughtiness outweighs them all. But of the humble it is written, 'And the humble shall inherit the land and delight in abundant peace' (Tehillim 37:11)."

1225.label: Pesachim 68b
1225.rest: — "Both expounded one verse. One verse says, 'an assembly to Hashem your God' (Devarim 16:8), and one verse says, 'an assembly shall it be to you' (Bamidbar 29:35). Rabbi Eliezer holds: either all of it for Hashem or all of it for you; Rabbi Yehoshua holds: divide it — half for Hashem and half for you." Rashi (on "for you" in the next line): that one rejoices on it with food and drink.

1226.label: Sukkah 27a
1226.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak: It says here 'the fifteenth,' and it says 'the fifteenth' regarding the festival of matzos: just as there the first night is obligatory and from then on optional, so here the first night is obligatory and from then on optional."

1227.label: Rambam, Sefer HaMitzvos, Shoresh 2
1227.rest: — Not everything derived through one of the thirteen principles of exposition is counted among the 613; whatever is not heard explicitly at Sinai is "of the words of the Scribes" (divrei soferim), unless the transmitters stated explicitly that it is Torah law.

1228.label: Berachos 34a
1228.rest: — "The Rabbis taught: Three things — a lot of them is harmful and a little is good: leaven, salt, and refusal." (Rashi has no comment on this line.)

1229.label: Rambam, Hilchos De'os 2:2
1229.rest: — How are they healed? One prone to anger is told to train himself that even if struck or cursed he will feel nothing… and so with every trait: if he was far toward one extreme, he distances himself to the other extreme and conducts himself so for a long time, until he returns to the good path, the middle measure of each trait.

1230.label: Arachin 32b
1230.rest: — Ezra prayed for mercy regarding the inclination for idolatry and abolished it, "and his merit shielded them like a sukkah."

1231.label: Pesachim 68b
1231.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said: All agree regarding Atzeres that we also require 'for you.' What is the reason? It is the day on which the Torah was given. Rabbah said: All agree regarding Shabbos… Rav Yosef said: All agree regarding Purim." Rashi: one should rejoice with food and drink, to show that this day on which the Torah was given is pleasing and welcome to Israel.

1232.label: Taanis 2a
1232.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Three keys are in the hand of the Holy One that were not entrusted to an agent, and these are they: the key of rain, the key of childbirth, and the key of the revival of the dead."

1233.label: Moed Katan 28a
1233.rest: — “Rava said: Life, children and sustenance do not depend upon merit; they depend upon mazal. For Rabbah and Rav Chisda were both righteous Sages: one prayed and rain came; the other prayed and rain came.”

1234.label: Shabbos 156a
1234.rest: — "Rabbi Chanina says: Mazal makes wise, mazal makes rich, and Israel has a mazal. Rabbi Yochanan said: Israel has no mazal… as it says, 'Thus says Hashem: Do not learn the way of the nations, and do not be dismayed by the signs of the heavens, for the nations are dismayed by them' (Yirmeyahu 10:2) — they, and not Israel." Rashi: through prayer and merit their mazal is changed for the good.

1235.label: Tosafos, Taanis 2a (s.v. sheloshah mafteichos)
1235.rest: — And if you ask: it says (Sanhedrin 113a) that the key of rain was handed over to Eliyahu, and likewise the key of the revival of the dead… One may answer: "they were not handed over to an agent" does not mean they were never handed over, for those of revival and of rain were handed over; rather, they were not handed over to an agent to be appointed over them permanently.

1236.label: Berachos 10b
1236.rest: — "'And Chizkiyahu turned his face to the wall (kir)' (Yeshayahu 38:2) — what is 'kir'? Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: From the chambers (kiros) of his heart."

1237.label: Taanis 7a
1237.rest: — "Rav Yehudah said: The day of rain is as great as the day the Torah was given… Rava said: Greater than the day the Torah was given, as it says, 'My teaching (likchi) shall drop like the rain' (Devarim 32:2) — who is compared to whom? The lesser is compared to the greater." Rashi: the verse compares teaching to rain.

1238.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 13, 29b
1238.rest: — "Shemini Atzeres is a festival in its own right; on it is the welling forth of the Torah, to water the tree that is planted in the garden, and its roots and branches are like the circle (chug) of the earth, for all the festivals are celebrated in it."

1239.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
1239.rest: — "It is the watering of the tree, to its arms and branches, like water that waters a tree, and it grows through that watering."

1240.label: Zohar III 80b–81a (Kedoshim)
1240.rest: — "He said to him: 'The fear of Hashem' is written, not Torah! He answered: So it is indeed, for the Torah comes from the side of Gevurah… as it is written, 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem' (Tehillim 111:10)." Yitzchak, the "Fear of Yitzchak," is the chariot of Gevurah.

1241.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a
1241.rest: — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

1242.label: Sukkah 48a
1242.rest: — "From where are these words? As our Rabbis taught: 'And you shall be only (ach) joyful' (Devarim 16:15) — to include the night of the last Yom Tov of the festival."

1243.label: Yoma 39a
1243.rest: — "Our Rabbis taught: 'And you shall sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy' (Vayikra 11:44) — a person sanctifies himself a little, and they sanctify him much; below, and they sanctify him above; in this world, and they sanctify him in the World to Come."

1244.label: Zohar III 104b (Emor)
1244.rest: — "And this day, Yaakov is at the head of the rejoicing, and all those guests rejoice with him; therefore it is written, 'Fortunate are you, Israel; who is like you' (Devarim 33:29), and it is written, 'And He said to me: You are My servant, Israel, in whom I glory' (Yeshayahu 49:3)."

1245.label: Midrash Tanchuma, Pinchas 15
1245.rest: — “It would have been fitting for the assembly after Sukkos to be fifty days after the festival, just as the assembly after Pesach is fifty days later. But the Holy One, blessed be He, said: ‘It is winter, and they cannot leave their homes to come here. Instead, while they are with Me, let them hold the assembly.’” The Midrash explains Shemini Atzeres by the difficulty of returning in winter. Rav Tzadok invokes this as an example of the burden of travel in the present order of things.

1246.label: Mechilta, Beshalach, Shirah 3
1246.rest: — "'This is my God and I will glorify Him' (Shemos 15:2): a maidservant saw at the Sea what Yeshayahu and Yechezkel did not see."

1247.label: Rema, Orach Chaim 1:1
1247.rest: — "When a person takes to heart that the great King, the Holy One, blessed be He, whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and sees his deeds, as it says, 'Can a man hide in secret places that I shall not see him? says Hashem' (Yirmeyahu 23:24) — immediately awe and submission will come upon him, in dread of Hashem Yisbarach, and he will be ashamed before Him constantly."

1248.label: Berachos 34b
1248.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani said: … a king, once he bows, does not straighten up again [until the end], as it says, 'And it was when Shlomo finished praying… he rose from before the altar of Hashem, from kneeling on his knees' (I Melachim 8:54)."

1249.label: Shabbos 114a
1249.rest: — "What are 'builders'? Rabbi Yochanan said: These are Torah scholars, who are occupied with the building of the world all their days."

1250.label: Zohar III 104b (Emor), on Shemini Atzeres
1250.rest: — "And on this day Yaakov is the head of the joy, and all those guests rejoice with him; and therefore it is written, 'Fortunate are you, Israel, who is like you' (Devarim 33:29), and it is written, 'And He said to me: You are My servant, Israel, in whom I take glory' (Yeshayahu 49:3)."

1251.label: Pesachim 68b
1251.rest: — "Rabbi Elazar said: All agree regarding Atzeres that we also require 'for you.' What is the reason? It is the day on which the Torah was given. Rabbah said: All agree regarding Shabbos… Rav Yosef said: All agree regarding Purim." Rashi: one should rejoice with food and drink, to show that this day on which the Torah was given is pleasing and welcome to Israel.

1252.label: Taanis 26b (Mishnah)
1252.rest: — "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: There were no festive days for Israel like the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur, on which the daughters of Yerushalayim would go out in borrowed white garments, so as not to shame one who had none… And so it says, 'Go forth and gaze, O daughters of Tziyon, upon King Shlomo, upon the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart' (Shir HaShirim 3:11): 'on the day of his wedding' — this is the giving of the Torah; 'and on the day of the joy of his heart' — this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash, may it be rebuilt speedily in our days."

1253.label: Zohar II 82b (Yisro)
1253.rest: — "For we learned: six hundred and thirteen kinds of counsel (eitin) the Torah gave to a person, to be whole with his Master, for his Master wishes to do him good in this world and in the World to Come."

1254.label: Berachos 21a
1254.rest: — "From where is the blessing over the Torah before it from the Torah? For it says, 'When I call the Name of Hashem, ascribe greatness to our God' (Devarim 32:3)."

1255.label: Berachos 6a
1255.rest: — "From where do we know that even one who sits and occupies himself with Torah, the Shechinah is with him? As it says, 'In every place where I cause My Name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you' (Shemos 20:21)."

1256.label: Pesachim 119b
1256.rest: — “Rav Avira expounded: What is meant by ‘The child grew and was weaned’? In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a feast for the righteous on the day that He bestows His kindness upon the descendants of Yitzchak. After they eat and drink, they give Avraham our father a cup of blessing with which to recite the blessing. ... They say to David: Take it and bless. He says to them: I shall bless, and it is fitting for me to bless, as it is said, ‘I shall raise the cup of salvations and call in the name of Hashem.’” The Gemara’s account contains both eating and drinking and a cup of blessing. That concrete imagery is relevant to the Rambam–Raavad discussion that follows.

1257.label: Sanhedrin 99a
1257.rest: — "What is 'No eye has seen, O God, but You' (Yeshayahu 64:3)? Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: This is the wine preserved in its grapes from the six days of Creation."

1258.label: Sanhedrin 38b
1258.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: [Adam] drew his foreskin forward, as it is written here, 'But they, like Adam, transgressed the covenant' (Hoshea 6:7), and it is written there, 'he has broken My covenant' (Bereishis 17:14)."

1259.label: Zohar I 93a (Lech Lecha)
1259.rest: — "'Your people are all righteous' (Yeshayahu 60:21): are all Israel righteous? There are so many sinners among them! Rather… once they are circumcised they enter the good portion of the Holy One, of whom it is written, 'The righteous is the foundation of the world' (Mishlei 10:25); since they have entered this portion of the Tzaddik, they are called righteous — all of them."

1260.label: Nedarim 31b
1260.rest: — “If one vows, ‘I may not benefit from the uncircumcised,’ he may benefit from uncircumcised Israelites but may not benefit from circumcised members of the nations. If he vows, ‘I may not benefit from the circumcised,’ he may not benefit from uncircumcised Israelites but may benefit from circumcised members of the nations. For uncircumcision is used as the designation of the nations, as it says, ‘All the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised of heart.’” The Mishnah is interpreting the communal language of a vow. Rav Tzadok draws from it the distinction between the physical operation alone and entry into Israel’s covenant.

1261.label: Megillah 17b
1261.rest: — "And why did they see fit to place healing as the eighth blessing? Rabbi Acha said: Because circumcision, which requires healing, was given on the eighth day, therefore they set it as the eighth."

1262.label: Zohar III 256b (Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas)
1262.rest: — "'On the eighth day an assembly… one bull, one ram' (Bamidbar 29:35–36) — the masters of the Mishnah explained it as a king who invited guests; after he sent them off, he said to the members of his household: You and I will make a small meal… And Israel are accustomed to make rejoicing with her, and it is called Simchas Torah, and they adorn the Sefer Torah with its crown."

1263.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 21, 56a
1263.rest: — "At that time of Simchas Torah… a crown rests on the head of every tzaddik above, 'with the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart' (Shir HaShirim 3:11): 'on the day of his wedding' — this is the lower Shechinah; 'and on the day of the joy of his heart' — this is the upper Shechinah."

1264.label: Sukkah 37b
1264.rest: — "In the West they taught thus: Rabbi Chama bar Ukva said in the name of Rabbi Yosi son of Rabbi Chanina: One moves them forth and back in order to hold back harmful winds, up and down in order to hold back harmful dews."

1265.label: Zohar III 80b–81a (Kedoshim)
1265.rest: — "He said to him: 'The fear of Hashem' is written, not Torah! He answered: So it is indeed, for the Torah comes from the side of Gevurah… as it is written, 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem' (Tehillim 111:10)." Yitzchak, the "Fear of Yitzchak," is the chariot of Gevurah.

1266.label: Berachos 5b
1266.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Granted Torah and kindness, as it is written, 'Through kindness and truth iniquity is atoned' (Mishlei 16:6): 'kindness' is acts of kindness… and 'truth' is Torah, as it is said, 'Buy truth and do not sell it' (Mishlei 23:23)."

1267.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a
1267.rest: — “You brought forth ten arrangements, and we call them ten sefirot, through which to direct concealed worlds that are not revealed and worlds that are revealed. ... Malkhut is the mouth: we call it Oral Torah.” The specific formula “Malkhut is the mouth, Oral Torah” is found in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar, in Patach Eliyahu. It complements the preceding Zohar passage about the seventh day.

1268.label: Zohar III 104b (Emor)
1268.rest: — "And this day, Yaakov is at the head of the rejoicing, and all those guests rejoice with him; therefore it is written, 'Fortunate are you, Israel; who is like you' (Devarim 33:29), and it is written, 'And He said to me: You are My servant, Israel, in whom I glory' (Yeshayahu 49:3)."

1269.label: Sanhedrin 103b
1269.rest: — "Our Rabbis taught: Menasheh would study fifty-five facets in Toras Kohanim, corresponding to the years of his reign; Achav, eighty-five; Yeravam, one hundred and three." Rashi: every year he would innovate in the book of Vayikra and expound it with his dialectic.

1270.label: Mechilta, Beshalach, Vayassa 3
1270.rest: — "The Torah was given to be expounded only to those who ate the manna."

1271.label: Bava Kamma 92a
1271.rest: — "'And this for Yehudah… Hear, Hashem, the voice of Yehudah' (Devarim 33:7)… His limbs came into place, but they would not bring him up to the Heavenly Academy — 'and bring him to his people'; he did not know what the Rabbis were saying, to deliberate with the Rabbis — 'his hands shall contend for him'; he could not bring a teaching to its halachic conclusion — 'and You shall be a help against his adversaries.'"

1272.label: Menachos 29b
1272.rest: — "He said: Master of the world, show him to me. He said: Turn around. He went and sat at the end of eight rows and did not understand what they were saying, and his strength waned. When they reached a certain matter, his students said to him: Rebbi, from where do you know this? He said: It is a halachah to Moshe from Sinai — and Moshe's mind was settled." Rashi: since it was said in his name.

1273.label: Sotah 12a
1273.rest: — “The Sages say: When Moshe was born, the whole house filled with light. Here it is written, She saw that he was good; and there it is written, God saw the light, that it was good.” The association of good with light is explicit in the Gemara. Rav Tzadok reads Moshe's original spiritual portion through this image of light preceding encounter with evil.

1274.label: Pesachim 38b
1274.rest: — "When I came and presented these words before Rabbi Eliezer, he said to me: It is a covenant — these are the very words that were said to Moshe at Sinai… and it does not require a reason."

1275.label: Gittin 14a
1275.rest: — "Mar Zutra said: These three matters the Rabbis made like a halachah without a reason." Rashi: as though Moshe received it as a halachah from Sinai, needing no reason to be given.

1276.label: Nedarim 38a
1276.rest: — "Rabbi Yosi son of Rabbi Chanina said: The Torah was given only to Moshe and his seed, as it says, 'Write for yourself' (Shemos 34:27), 'Carve for yourself' (34:1) — just as the chips are yours, so is the writing yours; but Moshe dealt generously with it and gave it to Israel… Rather, it was only the pilpul [the dialectic] that was given to him."

1277.label: Sotah 21b
1277.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Words of Torah endure only in one who makes himself as one who is not, as it says, 'And wisdom — from where (me'ayin) shall it be found?' (Iyov 28:12)." Rashi: from one who makes himself as nothing (ayin).

1278.label: Shabbos 30a
1278.rest: — "Whereas Moshe Rabbeinu decreed many decrees and instituted many enactments, and they endure forever and ever."

1279.label: Bava Basra 8a
1279.rest: — "After he left, Rebbi sat and was distressed and said: Woe is me, that I have given my bread to an am ha'aretz! Rabbi Shimon son of Rebbi said before him: Perhaps it is Yonasan ben Amram your student, who never in his days wished to benefit from the honor of Torah. They checked and found it so. Rebbi said: Let everyone enter."

1280.label: Bava Metzia 33b
1280.rest: — “‘And to the house of Yaakov their sins’ (Yeshayah 58:1) — these are the amei ha’aretz, whose deliberate sins are counted for them as unwitting ones.”

1281.label: Bava Kamma 92a
1281.rest: — "Rava said to Rabbah bar Mari: From where is this thing that people say, 'Along with the thorn, the cabbage is struck'? He said to him: As it is written, 'Why do you contend with Me? You have all rebelled against Me, says Hashem' (Yirmeyahu 2:29)."

1282.label: Berachos 17a
1282.rest: — "Rabbi Alexandri, after his prayer, would say: Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that our will is to do Your will; and who holds us back? The leaven in the dough and the subjugation to the kingdoms." Rashi: the leaven in the dough — the evil inclination in our hearts, which sours us.

1283.label: Sukkah 38a
1283.rest: — "Rav Acha bar Yaakov would move [the lulav] forth and back and say: This is an arrow in the eye of the Satan. But it is not proper, for it comes to provoke him."

1284.label: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2
1284.rest: — "Rabbi Yehudah says: At the time Israel heard 'I am Hashem your God' (Shemos 20:2), the study of Torah was implanted in their heart, and they would learn and not forget. They came to Moshe and said: Moshe our teacher, be an intermediary between us, as it says, 'You speak with us, and we will hear' (Shemos 20:16)… and they returned to learning and forgetting."

1285.label: Zohar III 104b (Emor)
1285.rest: — "And this day, Yaakov is at the head of the rejoicing, and all those guests rejoice with him; therefore it is written, 'Fortunate are you, Israel; who is like you' (Devarim 33:29), and it is written, 'And He said to me: You are My servant, Israel, in whom I glory' (Yeshayahu 49:3)."

1286.label: Sifrei, Devarim 342
1286.rest: — "'And this is the blessing' (Devarim 33:1) — this adds to the first blessing with which Yaakov their father blessed them… We learn that from the place where Yaakov Avinu finished blessing Israel, from there Moshe began to bless them."

1287.label: Zohar I 120a (Vayera)
1287.rest: — "Why did he depart from the shining speculum in this matter? Because this was the level of Yaakov, and since Yaakov had not yet been born, it was not yet found at this level."

1288.label: Yevamos 49b
1288.rest: — "All the prophets gazed through a speculum that does not shine; Moshe Rabbeinu gazed through a speculum that shines."

1289.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 21, 56a
1289.rest: — "At that time of Simchas Torah… a crown rests on the head of every tzaddik above, 'with the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart' (Shir HaShirim 3:11): 'on the day of his wedding' — this is the lower Shechinah; 'and on the day of the joy of his heart' — this is the upper Shechinah."

1290.label: Rema, Orach Chaim 1:1
1290.rest: — "When a person takes to heart that the great King, the Holy One, blessed be He, whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and sees his deeds, as it says, 'Can a man hide in secret places that I shall not see him? says Hashem' (Yirmeyahu 23:24) — immediately awe and submission will come upon him, in dread of Hashem Yisbarach, and he will be ashamed before Him constantly."

1291.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
1291.rest: — "Chochmah is the brain, which is thought within; Binah is the heart, and with it the heart understands; and of these two it is written, 'The hidden things belong to Hashem our God' (Devarim 29:28)."

1292.label: Bava Kamma 92a
1292.rest: — "'And this for Yehudah… Hear, Hashem, the voice of Yehudah' (Devarim 33:7)… His limbs came into place, but they would not bring him up to the Heavenly Academy — 'and bring him to his people'; he did not know what the Rabbis were saying, to deliberate with the Rabbis — 'his hands shall contend for him'; he could not bring a teaching to its halachic conclusion — 'and You shall be a help against his adversaries.'"

1293.label: Avos 1:1
1293.rest: — "Moshe received the Torah from Sinai and transmitted it to Yehoshua, Yehoshua to the elders, the elders to the prophets, and the prophets transmitted it to the Men of the Great Assembly. They said three things: Be deliberate in judgment, raise up many students, and make a fence for the Torah."

1294.label: Tanchuma, Noach 3
1294.rest: — Israel accepted the Written Torah willingly, but not the Oral Torah, which requires toil and suffering; and for it the Holy One held the mountain over them like a barrel. The Oral Torah is not found with one who seeks the pleasures of the world.

1295.label: Zohar III 193a (Balak)
1295.rest: — "When the Holy One wished to give the Torah to Israel, He went and invited the children of Esav, and they did not accept it, as you say, 'Hashem came from Sinai and shone forth from Seir to them' (Devarim 33:2)… He went to the children of Yishmael, and they did not wish to accept it… Since they did not wish it, He returned to Israel." From those nations Israel received gifts and presents.

1296.label: Sanhedrin 39b
1296.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: This is what people say: From the forest itself let the axe go into it."

1297.label: Kiddushin 30b
1297.rest: — "I created the evil inclination; I created Torah as its antidote… The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: My son, if this repulsive one accosts you, drag him to the beis midrash: if he is stone, he will melt; if he is iron, he will shatter, as it says, 'Is not My word like fire, says Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?' (Yirmeyahu 23:29)." Rashi: "this repulsive one" is the evil inclination provoking you.

1298.label: Sanhedrin 75a
1298.rest: — "As Rabbi Yitzchak said: From the day the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed, the taste of relations was taken away and given to transgressors, as it says, 'Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant' (Mishlei 9:17)."

1299.label: Avos 4:1
1299.rest: — "Ben Zoma says: Who is wise? One who learns from every person… Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination, as it says, 'Better is one slow to anger than a mighty man, and one who rules his spirit than one who captures a city' (Mishlei 16:32)."

1300.label: Kiddushin 30b
1300.rest: — "So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: My children, I created the evil inclination and I created Torah as its antidote; if you occupy yourselves with Torah you will not be delivered into its hand, as it says, 'If you do good, you shall be lifted up' (Bereishis 4:7)." Rashi: lifted above your inclination.

1301.label: Chullin 91a
1301.rest: — "Rav Shmuel bar Acha said before Rav Pappa in the name of Rava bar Ulla: He appeared to him as a Torah scholar."

1302.label: Yoma 86b
1302.rest: — "Rav Huna said: Once a person has committed a transgression and repeated it, it becomes to him as permitted."

1303.label: Sifrei, Bamidbar 77 (Behaaloscha)
1303.rest: — "'And on the day of your rejoicing' (Bamidbar 10:10) — these are the Shabbosos."

1304.label: Taanis 15a
1304.rest: — "Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I too say: not all are for light and not all are for gladness. The righteous are for light, and the upright for gladness: the righteous for light, as it is written, 'Light is sown for the righteous' (Tehillim 97:11); and the upright for gladness, as it is written, 'and for the upright of heart, gladness.'"

1305.label: Taanis 8b
1305.rest: — "Rabbi Yitzchak said: Sun on Shabbos is charity for the poor, as it says, 'And for you who fear My Name a sun of righteousness shall shine, with healing in its wings' (Malachi 3:20)." Rashi explains "those who fear My Name" as those who keep the Shabbos.

1306.label: Yerushalmi, Demai 4:1
1306.rest: — "The awe of Shabbos is upon the am ha'aretz": on Shabbos even an unlearned person will not lie about whether his produce was tithed.

1307.label: Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah 3
1307.rest: — "David the King further said: I feared out of my joy, and I rejoiced out of my fear, and my love rose above them all."

1308.label: Zohar I 5b (Introduction)
1308.rest: — "'You shall fear My Sanctuary' (Vayikra 19:30) — this is the Shabbos of Friday night, which is fear, and fear dwells in it."

1309.label: Kiddushin 32b
1309.rest: — "Rav Ashi said: Even according to the one who says that a nasi who forgoes his honor, his honor is forgone — a king who forgoes his honor, his honor is not forgone, as it says, 'You shall surely set a king over you' (Devarim 17:15): that his awe be upon you."

1310.label: Zohar III 103a (Ra'aya Meheimna, Emor)
1310.rest: — "'In sukkos you shall dwell seven days' (Vayikra 23:42): this commandment is to dwell in the sukkah… to show that Israel dwell in the secret of faith without any fear, for the accuser has departed from them. And whoever is in the secret of faith sits in the sukkah, as it is written, 'Every native in Israel shall dwell in sukkos' — whoever is of the secret of faith, of the seed and root of Israel, shall dwell in sukkos."

1311.label: Zohar III 103a (Ra'aya Meheimna, Emor)
1311.rest: — "'In sukkos you shall dwell seven days' (Vayikra 23:42) — the mitzvah to dwell in the sukkah, to show that Israel dwell in the secret of faith without any fear, for the accuser has departed from them; and whoever is in the secret of faith dwells in the sukkah."

1312.label: Rema, Orach Chaim 1:1
1312.rest: — "When a person takes to heart that the great King, the Holy One, blessed be He, whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and sees his deeds, as it says, 'Can a man hide in secret places that I shall not see him? says Hashem' (Yirmeyahu 23:24) — immediately awe and submission will come upon him, in dread of Hashem Yisbarach, and he will be ashamed before Him constantly."

1313.label: Sukkah 48a
1313.rest: — "From where are these words? As our Rabbis taught: 'And you shall be only (ach) joyful' (Devarim 16:15) — to include the night of the last Yom Tov of the festival."

1314.label: Zohar III 104b (Emor)
1314.rest: — "And this day, Yaakov is at the head of the rejoicing, and all those guests rejoice with him; therefore it is written, 'Fortunate are you, Israel; who is like you' (Devarim 33:29), and it is written, 'And He said to me: You are My servant, Israel, in whom I glory' (Yeshayahu 49:3)."

1315.label: Zohar III 269a–b (Va'eschanan)
1315.rest: — "Afterward all of them are included in the left arm, which is called oz (strength), and it is written, 'and by the arm of His strength (oz).' And there is no oz but Torah, and there is no oz but tefillin."

1316.label: Zevachim 116a
1316.rest: — The nations asked Bilam, "What is the sound of this tumult that we heard? He said to them: He has a precious treasure in His storehouse, which was stored with Him nine hundred and seventy-four generations before the world was created, and He wishes to give it to His children, as it says, 'Hashem will give strength to His people' (Tehillim 29:11). Immediately they all opened and said, 'Hashem will bless His people with peace.'"

1317.label: Sukkah 52a
1317.rest: — “Shlomo called it ‘enemy,’ as it says: If your enemy is hungry, feed him bread.”

1318.label: Bereishis Rabbah 54:1
1318.rest: — "'When a man's ways please Hashem, even his enemies He makes at peace with him' (Mishlei 16:7). Rabbi Yochanan said: this is the evil inclination… 'If your enemy is hungry, feed him bread' (Mishlei 25:21) — the bread of Torah; 'and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink' — the water of Torah."

1319.label: Zohar I, Mikeitz 202a
1319.rest: — “We learned: A person should always rouse the good inclination against the evil inclination and strive against it. If it departs from him, well; if not, he should occupy himself with Torah, for there is nothing that breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death in order to break it.” The Zohar gives a sequence of active resistance, Torah and remembrance of death. Rav Tzadok emphasizes the Oral Torah's lived study as the means of transforming the inward enemy.

1320.label: Berachos 28b
1320.rest: — When R. Yochanan ben Zakkai fell ill, his students asked for a blessing. He said: "May it be [His] will that the fear of Heaven be upon you like the fear of flesh and blood." They said: "Only that much?" He said: "If only! Know that when a person sins, he says: Let no person see me." Rashi: would that you refrained from sin as you do before people. (Rav Tzadok attributes it to R. Eliezer.)

1321.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 41, 81a
1321.rest: — In "Bereishis" are the letters of Tishrei, and this is the second arm, the second day; "He made (yashes) darkness His hiding place" (Tehillim 18:12): remove yashes from bereishis and reish remains — Rosh Hashanah.

1322.label: Zevachim 116a
1322.rest: — The nations asked Bilam, "What is the sound of this tumult that we heard? He said to them: He has a precious treasure in His storehouse, which was stored with Him nine hundred and seventy-four generations before the world was created, and He wishes to give it to His children, as it says, 'Hashem will give strength to His people' (Tehillim 29:11). Immediately they all opened and said, 'Hashem will bless His people with peace.'"

1323.label: Megillah 16b
1323.rest: — “‘Words of peace and truth.’ Rabbi Tanchum said, and some say Rabbi Assi: This teaches that the Megillah requires ruled lines, like the truth of Torah.” The physical ruling of the scroll expresses its affinity with a Torah text. The maamar develops the deeper permanence signified by its being granted a written form.

1324.label: Yoma 28b
1324.rest: — "Rav said: Avraham Avinu fulfilled the entire Torah, as it says, 'Because Avraham listened to My voice and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes and My Torahs' (Bereishis 26:5). Rav Shimi bar Chiya said to Rav: Perhaps only the seven mitzvos? — There was milah too! — Perhaps seven and milah? — If so, why 'My commandments and My Torahs'?"

1325.label: Avos 4:1
1325.rest: — "Ben Zoma says: Who is wise? One who learns from every person… Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination, as it says, 'Better is one slow to anger than a mighty man, and one who rules his spirit than one who captures a city' (Mishlei 16:32)."

1326.label: Sanhedrin 90a (Mishnah)
1326.rest: — "All Israel have a share in the World to Come, as it says, 'And your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of My planting, the work of My hands to be glorified' (Yeshayahu 60:21). And these have no share in the World to Come: one who says there is no resurrection of the dead from the Torah, that the Torah is not from Heaven, and an apikoros."

1327.label: Taanis 5b
1327.rest: — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Yaakov Avinu did not die. He was asked: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed and the buriers buried? He answered: I am expounding a verse, as it says, 'And you, fear not, My servant Yaakov… for behold, I save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity' (Yirmeyahu 30:10) — it compares him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too he is alive." Rashi: he lives forever; they embalmed him because they thought he had died.

1328.label: Yoma 28b
1328.rest: — "Rav Chama bar Chanina said: From the days of our forefathers yeshivah never departed from them… Avraham Avinu was an elder sitting in yeshivah, as it says, 'And Avraham was old (zaken)' (Bereishis 24:1); Yitzchak Avinu was an elder sitting in yeshivah, as it says, 'And it was when Yitzchak was old' (27:1); Yaakov Avinu was an elder sitting in yeshivah, as it says, 'And the eyes of Israel were heavy with age' (48:10)."

1329.label: Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Pasach Eliyahu)
1329.rest: — "Chesed is the right arm, Gevurah the left arm, Tiferes the body, Netzach and Hod the two thighs, Yesod the completion of the body, the sign of the holy covenant; Malchus is the mouth — we call it the Oral Torah."

1330.label: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefas Emes, Elul
1330.rest: — “[Elul is] by the power of the awakening of teshuvah. The essential revelation of the Thirteen Attributes is in Tishrei, as the holy Zohar says, and it is the aspect of ‘when He may be found’: since the world was created then, His outstretched hand is revealed to receive those who return. But in Elul the revelation comes through the awakening of Israel. This is ‘I am my Beloved's and my Beloved is mine’: ‘my Beloved is mine’ is in Tishrei, for as the awakening is in Elul, so does one merit in Tishrei.” Connection: Sefas Emes, like Rav Tzadok on the shofar of Rosh Chodesh Elul, places Elul's work in an awakening from below that prepares what is revealed in Tishrei.

1331.label: R. Zev Wolf Einhorn, Maharzu on Shemos Rabbah 17:2
1331.rest: — “‘Like an apple among the trees of the forest, so is my Beloved among the sons’ (Shir HaShirim 2:3); see Shabbos 88a, ‘Why were Israel compared to an apple?’ ‘To the eye it is nothing’: there are apples that are not beautiful to look at, yet they have taste and fragrance. The taste is in Torah, as it says, ‘Teach me good taste and knowledge’ (Tehillim 119:66); and so ‘Taste and see that Hashem is good’ (Tehillim 34:9) — through the Torah, which is called ‘good.’” Connection: The apple's taste is identified with Torah, which is called “good,” just as Rav Tzadok reads the “good year” asked for over the apple.

1332.label: Ramban, Devarim 28:13
1332.rest: — “The meaning of ‘a head and not a tail’: some explain, a head to all the peoples and not a tail to any one of the nations, for it is possible to be a head over many peoples and a tail to one people more honored than it. But the correct explanation is that He will make you a head from now on, and not a tail forever, at any time; and so ‘only above,’ always, and you will never be below.” Connection: Ramban reads the blessing behind the Rosh Hashanah custom as a permanent, unbroken standing, the sense Rav Tzadok draws from the seventh blessing of Ki Savo.

1333.label: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Agra DeKala, Bereishis
1333.rest: — “First we preface the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua whether the world was created in Tishrei or in Nissan (Rosh Hashanah 11a). The masters of truth wrote that the matter stands: these and those are the words of the living God. In Tishrei was the thought, as the Arizal explained ‘Hayom haras olam’ (Mussaf of Rosh Hashanah) as a term of pregnancy and conception, for there was not yet revelation in deed; and in Nissan was the actual deed. And it is known that the days of Tishrei are days of judgment and Nissan days of mercy.” Connection: Following Tosafos, he adds the Arizal's reading of “haras olam” and the judgment of Tishrei against the mercy of Nissan.

1334.label: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Likkutei Torah, Rosh Hashanah
1334.rest: — “‘Let Your ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications’ is the lowest level of all: one who asks for himself, and does not arouse mercy for the Divine portion within him, which has descended from a high roof to a deep pit. Therefore it says ‘to the voice of my supplications,’ and not ‘to my voice’; and such a prayer does not fly upward of itself. So he says, ‘Let Your ears’ — the angels, called the ears of Hashem — ‘be attentive to the voice of my supplications’ specifically, my own petition for myself, that they raise the prayer.” Connection: Likkutei Torah reads the same pasuk as a ladder of levels of prayer, ending with the request that even the lowest be heard.

1335.label: R. Moshe of Trani (Mabit), Beis Elokim, Shaar HaTefillah 8
1335.rest: — “One who prays in a high place appears as though he brings himself near to the place of the Shechinah so that his voice will be heard. Therefore one should pray from a low place, to show that the whole earth is full of His glory; and though the chief dwelling of His Shechinah is above, He hears those who cry to Him from below, from a lowly place. This is ‘A Song of Ascents: from the depths I called You, Hashem’ (Tehillim 130:1).” Connection: The Mabit reads “from the depths” as the lowliness of the one praying, which Rav Tzadok makes the condition of being answered in the days of teshuvah.

1336.label: R. Avraham Dov of Ovruch, Bas Ayin, Haazinu
1336.rest: — “[The verse] warns about the matter of resolution, how one should accept upon himself not to do again. ‘Ashur will not save us’: that he accept upon himself not to trust any more in the king of Ashur to save him; ‘we will not ride upon horses’: not to trust in the king of Egypt for help — which is only a light transgression, a flaw in trust, yet he must accept not to do it, and all the more not to do a graver sin; and then, ‘we will no longer say “our god” to the work of our hands.’” Connection: Bas Ayin also reads the three clauses as a graded list of falls, from a slight lapse in trust to idolatry, each needing its own resolution.

1337.label: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Rosh Hashanah
1337.rest: — “The one who says ‘corresponding to the Ten Commandments’ gives the reason for the ten Zichronos: to recall the merit of Israel, who received the Torah and said ‘we will do and we will hear,’ unlike the nations, who refused to receive it. And the one who says ‘corresponding to the ten utterances with which the world was created’ gives the reason for the ten Malchuyos, for this is the purpose of the world's creation: that He be called King.” Connection: Shem MiShmuel assigns each of the Gemara's reasons to one of the three blessings, the approach Rav Tzadok takes.

1338.label: Sefer Baal Shem Tov, Rosh Hashanah
1338.rest: — “Is not Rosh Hashanah a Yom Tov — the Mishnah (Rosh Hashanah 29b) says ‘the Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah’ — and a day of joy, so that we say Shehecheyanu? What the Arizal wrote, to weep, is because of the exile of the Shechinah, and so that Hashem will judge us favorably. And this is what is written: ‘Go eat rich foods… and do not be saddened, for the joy of Hashem is your strength’ (Nechemiah 8:10). The weeping one weeps is a weeping of joy, over ‘Who has kept us alive and brought us to this time.’” Connection: The same tension between the poskim's weeping and Nechemiah's command to rejoice, resolved here as tears of joy.

1339.label: Pri Tzaddik, Bamidbar 9
1339.rest: — “‘And do not be saddened, for the joy of Hashem is your strength’: through fear, which brings uprightness of heart and joy, this is also the joy of Hashem, for through action below, action above is aroused; and ‘it is your strength’ — He sends you strength and might, to be ‘who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination.’ And afterward it is written, ‘And all the people went to eat and drink… and to make great joy, for they understood the words.’ The completeness of joy in holiness is when it comes out of fear, as it says (Tanna D'vei Eliyahu 3): ‘My joy is out of my fear.’” Connection: Rav Tzadok's own reading of the same pasuk: the joy of Rosh Hashanah grows out of its awe.

1340.label: Arizal, Pri Etz Chaim, Shaar Rosh Hashanah 7
1340.rest: — “On Rosh Hashanah there are four ‘U'vechein,’ which are four 72s, as is known, corresponding to the four legs of the Chariot. The first, ‘U'vechein yiskadash,’ corresponds to Avraham, who sanctified His Name in the world, which is Chesed — the letters of the verse ‘Vayisa’; ‘U'vechein tein pachdecha’ is the Fear of Yitzchak, Gevurah, corresponding to the 72 letters of the verse ‘Vayavo,’ which is in reverse; ‘U'vechein tein kavod’ corresponds to Yaakov, who said ‘Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever.’” Connection: The Arizal's account of the “U'vechein” as 72 and as the Avos, which Rav Tzadok builds on from the Zohar.

1341.label: R. Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, Toldos Yaakov Yosef, Pinchas
1341.rest: — “The first day of Rosh Hashanah is harsh judgment, like shevarim; therefore ‘whom Hashem loves He rebukes,’ and judges him on the second day of Rosh Hashanah, which is soft judgment, like teruah, called ‘dina rafya,’ as explained in the writings. With this understand ‘Fortunate is the people who know the teruah’: more fortunate is the people whose judgment is on the second day, called soft judgment, and they know the teruah, to appease their Creator with the teruah specifically, since it is soft judgment.” Connection: Toldos also divides the two days of Rosh Hashanah into harsh and soft judgment, as the Zohar Rav Tzadok cites does.

1342.label: R. Zev Wolf Einhorn, Maharzu on Vayikra Rabbah 21:4
1342.rest: — “‘My light’ — on Rosh Hashanah, as it says, ‘Fortunate is the people who know the teruah; Hashem, in the light of Your countenance they walk’ (Tehillim 89:16): so there is light on the day of teruah. ‘And my salvation’ — on Yom Kippur: the salvation of the true soul, the atonement of sins, and salvation from the Satan and from the princes of the nations, who come and accuse.” Connection: The commentary on the Midrash Rav Tzadok cites explains why Rosh Hashanah is light and Yom Kippur salvation.

1343.label: R. Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, Toldos Yaakov Yosef, Pinchas
1343.rest: — “‘For You hear the sound of the shofar’ — from afar, for the tzaddik; ‘and give ear to the teruah’ — from near, for the baal teshuvah. This seems contrary to nature, and the answer is that in truth there is none like You in this, out of Your mercy. And with this the words of the Rambam are understood, that the mitzvah is not to blow but to hear the teruah of the shofar: for through hearing the sound of the shofar, which wakes the sleepers from their slumber, a person returns in teshuvah; and this is called ‘the teruah of the shofar,’ which is the essence of the mitzvah.” Connection: Toldos divides the closing words of Shofaros between tzaddik and baal teshuvah, as Rav Tzadok weighs what is heard when the shofar is not blown.

1344.label: Pri Tzaddik, Masei 1
1344.rest: — “The second Shabbos comes with greater holiness than the Shabbos before it. All a person's days are so: the weekdays are journeying and walking in the service of Hashem, and when Shabbos comes, rest comes, for then he is in the aspect of rest; as it says, ‘For man goes to his eternal home’ (Koheles 12:5), and in the Gemara (Shabbos 152a), each tzaddik has a dwelling of his own.” Connection: Rav Tzadok elsewhere joins the same Gemara on “going” to the tzaddik's own dwelling with the ascent of each Shabbos, the key to “And Moshe went.”

1345.label: R. Moshe of Trani (Mabit), Beis Elokim, Shaar HaYesodos 43
1345.rest: — “Shabbos came upon him [Adam] when he was sent from Gan Eden at twilight, the twelfth hour of the sixth day, when he was banished. He saw that on the sixth day he and his wife were formed, and on the seventh nothing was created or made with him; and he knew that on this day, once its sun had set, God rested from all His work that He had made in the six days. So he rested with Him, and sang ‘A Psalm, a song for the Shabbos day,’ though he had not been commanded in it.” Connection: The Mabit too places Adam's first Shabbos right after his creation and sin, as Rav Tzadok does with the first Shabbos of the year.

1346.label: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefas Emes, Shabbos Shuvah
1346.rest: — “In the Pesikta the Holy One says, ‘I return to you’; so it is written, ‘Return to Me and I will return to you’ (Malachi 3:7). For through sin the illumination of the soul departs; therefore one must return to repair the body, so that it be ready to receive the soul's illumination. Shabbos Shuvah is in the aspect of the soul, and the weekdays are for repairing the body — ‘Create a pure heart for me’ — and through this, ‘renew a steadfast spirit within me.’ The teshuvah of the body is teshuvah from fear, and the teshuvah of the soul is from great longing.” Connection: Sefas Emes divides teshuvah between the weekdays and Shabbos as Rav Tzadok divides the weekday blessings from the prayer of Shabbos.

1347.label: Radak, Yeshayahu 55:7
1347.rest: — “‘Let the wicked forsake his way’ — in deed and in speech; and so let him forsake his evil thoughts, for teshuvah in what is seen does not avail unless it is also in what is hidden. A person's good and evil depend on the hand, the mouth and the heart, and teshuvah is needed from all three. ‘For He will abundantly forgive’ — even though the person has done much evil.” Connection: Radak reads “way” and “thoughts” as two layers of teshuvah, outer and inner, the distinction Rav Tzadok develops.

1348.label: R. Zev Wolf Einhorn, Maharzu on Bereishis Rabbah 22:13
1348.rest: — “‘And I made a compromise’: the intent is that it was decreed on him ‘a wanderer and an exile,’ and after the teshuvah it is written ‘and he dwelt in the land of Nod’ (wandering) — as in Devarim Rabbah, beginning of chapter 8, that prayer accomplishes half. ‘And he said, A psalm, a song’: the explanation of this saying I learned from Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer ch. 19, and so it is in Midrash Tehillim 92, which teaches that all generations will learn from it.” Connection: Maharzu explains Kayin's partial pardon and why Adam answered it with the Psalm for Shabbos, the passage Rav Tzadok expounds.

1349.label: R. Eliyahu de Vidas, Reishis Chochmah, Shaar HaTeshuvah 2
1349.rest: — “[One who betroths] ‘on condition that I am a tzaddik,’ even if he was wicked, she is betrothed, for perhaps he had a thought of teshuvah. So by a moment's thought he rose up to the Throne of Glory, to be called a complete tzaddik, for the Throne is the quarry of the souls of the tzaddikim. Both explanations are revealed in the Pesikta Rabbasi 44: ‘Great is the power of teshuvah: as soon as a person thinks in his heart to do teshuvah, it immediately rises and stands before the Throne of Glory — “Return, O Israel, up to Hashem your God.”’” Connection: Reishis Chochmah, like the explanations Rav Tzadok weighs, reads “up to the Throne” as the height the penitent reaches in a single moment.

1350.label: R. Chanoch Zundel, Etz Yosef on Bereishis Rabbah 22:13
1350.rest: — “[Kayin was reconciled] through confession and teshuvah; immediately [Adam] stood and said, ‘A psalm, a song for the Shabbos day: It is good to give thanks (lehodos) to Hashem’ — that is, it is good to praise, to return and to confess before the Holy One. ‘I did not know’ — and what is said in Eruvin, that he sat 130 years in teshuvah, was after he learned the power of teshuvah from Kayin.” Connection: Etz Yosef reads “lehodos” in the Psalm for Shabbos as confession, the link between Shabbos and teshuvah that Rav Tzadok draws from the same Midrash.

1351.label: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Sisa 5
1351.rest: — “[Man was made] after the pattern above, as it says, ‘Let us make man in our image’ (Bereishis 1:26). And as they said (Shemos Rabbah 30), the Holy One keeps the mitzvos, and what does He do? He tells Israel to do and to keep them. And so it says, ‘And you shall walk in His ways,’ to be like a monkey before a man, as they said (Bava Basra 58a): ‘Man before the Shechinah is like a monkey before a man.’” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other treatment of the Midrash that Hashem keeps His own mitzvos, read as the root of man's imitation of Him.

1352.label: Rabbeinu Yonah, Shaarei Teshuvah 1:42–45
1352.rest: — “‘And a generous spirit will sustain me’ (Tehillim 51:14): Behold, I have been diminished by my sins and I am not worthy of Your miracles, nor that Your holy arm be revealed upon me; and if You bear the iniquity of my sin, I am not worthy to be loved and accepted as in days of old. But sustain me with a generous spirit, for there is no end to Your generosity and goodness. And on this matter Hoshea said, ‘I will heal their backsliding; I will love them freely (nedavah)’ (Hoshea 14:5).” Connection: Rabbeinu Yonah reads Hoshea's words of return as a plea for undeserved love, the approach the Pesikta's “words to say” teach.

1353.label: Radak, Hoshea 14:2
1353.rest: — “‘Return, O Israel… for you have stumbled in your iniquity’: since you see that you have stumbled in your iniquity, you must return to Hashem, for nothing raises you from your stumbling except your return to Him. ‘Up to (ad)’ is like ‘to (el)’… and our Rabbis said: ‘Great is teshuvah, for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory, as it says, “up to Hashem your God.”’” Connection: Radak gives the plain sense of the verse the Gemara cites, and shows how the Sages' “up to the Throne” rests on the word “ad.”

1354.label: R. Eliyahu de Vidas, Reishis Chochmah, Shaar HaTeshuvah 1
1354.rest: — “When we say ‘Return us’ and ‘Forgive us,’ an awakening from below is necessarily needed, as it says, ‘Return to Me and I will return to you’ (Malachi 3:7). With this understand the Midrash Eichah on ‘Return us, Hashem, to You, and we shall return’ (Eichah 5:21): Knesses Yisrael said before the Holy One, ‘Master of the world, it is Yours: return us.’ He said to them, ‘It is yours: “Return to Me and I will return to you.”’ She said before Him, ‘Master of the world, it is Yours…’” Connection: Reishis Chochmah sets out the same exchange over who must begin the return, which the “time of favor” of Rav Tzadok's Midrash resolves.

1355.label: Matnos Kehunah on Vayikra Rabbah 21:12
1355.rest: — “[Shimon HaTzaddik] went out of the category of man into the category of an angel. In the Yerushalmi, Yoma (chapter Hotziu Lo), they asked before Rabbi Abahu: Is it not written, ‘And no man shall be in the Ohel Moed’ — not even those of whom it is written, ‘and the likeness of their faces was the face of a man’? He said to them: I say it was the Holy One in His glory…” Connection: The commentator draws out from the Yerushalmi that the Kohen Gadol in the Holy of Holies stood above even the angels, as Rav Tzadok explains.

1356.label: R. Shlomo Ephraim of Luntschitz, Kli Yakar, Vayikra 23:27
1356.rest: — “‘Whoever eats and drinks on the ninth, Scripture credits him as if he fasted the ninth and the tenth.’ And so that you not err and say: since the ninth too is reckoned as if he fasted on it, perhaps it too atones like the tenth — therefore it says, ‘But (ach) on the tenth of the month,’ to tell you that the tenth alone [is the day of atonement].” Connection: Kli Yakar marks the line between the eating of the ninth and the atonement of the tenth, the line Tosafos and Rav Tzadok explore.

1357.label: R. Shalom Buzaglo, Mikdash Melech on Zohar III 214b
1357.rest: — “‘Afterward the right comes’ — these are the chassadim that enter on Sukkos; ‘afterward she is joined with the body’ — on Shemini Atzeres. [The Zohar says] ‘like this order of these days,’ meaning that she receives an illumination not found at other times as in these days, from Rosh Hashanah until the festival of Atzeres. ‘On another day is His union’: on Yom Kippur she is joined with Binah, as said below, ‘for the supernal Mother lights her face,’ to place the left [beneath her head].” Connection: A Kabbalistic commentary on the very Zohar Rav Tzadok cites, assigning each stage, from Rosh Hashanah to Shemini Atzeres, its day.

1358.label: R. Kalonymus Kalman Epstein, Maor VaShemesh, Additions
1358.rest: — “In Shabbos 118b Abaye said: ‘May it come to me, for when I saw a young scholar who finished his tractate, I made a festive day for the Rabbis.’ The matter is this: we find that the Gemara in Rosh Hashanah expounded ‘These are the festivals of Hashem which you (atem) shall proclaim’ — even unwittingly, even misled, even deliberately. We learn that the Sages of the generation have the power to make a Yom Tov according to the time that seems right to them.” Connection: Maor VaShemesh grounds the scholars' private festival in the Sages' power to fix festivals, the kind of “festive day” Rav Tzadok finds in the Kohen Gadol's celebration.

1359.label: Maharsha, Chidushei Aggados, Yoma 85b
1359.rest: — “[The purification is] of body and soul. Sprinkling is from the pure upon the impure, done by another, and immersion in water is done by oneself before the Pure One; so here: ‘I will sprinkle pure water upon you’ (Yechezkel 36:25) — from the Pure One, the Holy One, upon the impure, to purify the soul; and ‘you shall be pure from all your impurities’ — the impurity of the body. That is: ‘Before Whom are you purified?’ — from the impurity of the body; ‘and Who purifies you?’ — from the impurity of the soul.” Connection: Maharsha splits Rabbi Akiva's two questions between the purification man does and the one Hashem does, the division Rav Tzadok draws from the mikveh and the sprinkling.

1360.label: R. Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, Ben Poras Yosef, Shabbos Shuvah
1360.rest: — “‘To purify you’ and ‘you shall be purified’ (Vayikra 16:30) is a doubling, and one difficulty explains the other. The meaning is: ‘On this day He will atone for you, to purify you from all your sins,’ whether between man and God or between man and his fellow. When does He atone? If the sins are ‘before Hashem,’ between him and God, then ‘before Hashem you shall be purified’ — purifying himself through teshuvah; but not so when [the sin is against his fellow].” Connection: The same verse behind Rabbi Akiva's teaching, read as two partners in purification, the penitent's teshuvah and Hashem's atonement.

1361.label: Shelah, Shaar HaOsiyos, Kedushas HaAchilah, citing R. Shem Tov ibn Shuaib on Koheles 9:7
1361.rest: — “‘Go, eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a good heart’: the verse does not depart from its plain meaning. Shlomo warned a person to rejoice in what Hashem has graciously given him, to eat his bread with joy and drink his wine with joy; and in this is a repair of body and soul. A repair of the body, for it is known in medicine that when a person eats in joy the food is digested well, and in worry the opposite; and the repair of the soul…” Connection: The Shelah gives the plain sense of the verse the heavenly voice proclaims, the joy of eating that Rav Tzadok places after Yom Kippur.

1362.label: Maharal, Derush LeShabbos Shuvah
1362.rest: — “[Yaakov] is complete in his soul, for the sin, which is an addition to him, does not join with him; therefore Yom Kippur removes the sin. But Esav was ‘a hairy man,’ for hair has no completeness of its own; therefore the sin, an addition from outside, joins with him completely and is not separated from him. Therefore he is compared to the curly-haired man, the chaff of whose hair stays in his hair and cannot be separated from it.” Connection: Maharal reads the same Midrash of the curly-haired and the bald man as Rav Tzadok does, as the difference between Yaakov, whose sins can be removed, and Esav.

1363.label: Abarbanel, Yeshayahu 1:18
1363.rest: — “Even if their sins be like scarlet — red with the blood of the slain and the oppressed — as soon as they accept the rebuke they will become white as snow and as wool, and no trace will remain, for whiteness indicates purity. We can also explain ‘kashanim’ as actual years (shanim); and so Chazal expounded (Shabbos 89b): Rabbi Yitzchak said, the Holy One said to Israel, ‘If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of Creation…’” Connection: Abarbanel brings the same Gemara on sins that become “ordered like the years,” which Rav Tzadok reads as sins turned into merits.

1364.label: Sefer Baal Shem Tov, Emor
1364.rest: — “‘In sukkos you shall dwell seven days’ (Vayikra 23:42): by the plain sense it should have said the reverse, ‘seven days you shall dwell in sukkos.’ Rather, this is its meaning: you, human beings, see that in the sukkos you seat, through your deeds, the seven supernal days, that is, the seven supernal guests, as is known.” Connection: The Baal Shem Tov reads the same verse, as the Zohar does, as the seating of the seven supernal guests through one's deeds.

1365.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 46
1365.rest: — “‘Then you shall delight upon (al) Hashem’ (Yeshayahu 58:14), as the holy Zohar says (end of Acharei) that ‘al Hashem’ is Atika, as it is written, ‘And Chanah prayed al Hashem,’ and ‘Cast your burden al Hashem’; that is, it is above the Name Havayah — the crown of the yud, for the Name Havayah includes the nine middos.” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other treatment of the same two Zohar passages, joining Avraham's “delight upon Hashem” to the level above the Name.

1366.label: Nefesh David on the Zohar
1366.rest: — “He merits to see children… as it brings the verse ‘His seed shall be mighty in the land’ (Tehillim 112:2); he merits in this world — this is ‘wealth and riches are in his house’; and he merits the World to Come — this is ‘and his righteousness stands forever.’ After it is written, ‘Light shines in darkness’ (Tehillim 112:4): darkness is turned to light, and all the masters of judgment cannot [harm him] — this is ‘gracious, merciful and righteous,’ that all is turned for him to mercy.” Connection: A commentary on the Zohar reading the same verses as three successive rewards, the three gifts Rav Tzadok finds in the mizmor.

1367.label: R. Moshe Chaim Ephraim of Sudilkov, Degel Machaneh Ephraim, Emor
1367.rest: — “‘Every native (ezrach) in Israel shall dwell in sukkos’: as in the holy Zohar, Emor: whoever is of the holy stock and root of Israel sits in sukkos under the shade of faith… Eliezer, Avraham's servant, because he served Avraham, sat under the shade of faith and merited to go out from the category of ‘cursed’ to the category of ‘blessed’; and whoever sits under the shade of faith inherits freedom for himself and his children forever. And this is ‘every ezrach in Israel’: whoever has in him the aspect of Avraham, who is called ‘ezrach,’ as in ‘Eisan HaEzrachi.’” Connection: The Degel reads “ezrach” as Avraham, as Rav Tzadok does, and makes the sukkah the shade of his faith.

1368.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach 6
1368.rest: — “[Avraham merited] the Torah, and merited everything. Yitzchak merited might, as it says, ‘Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination’; and this too was from the hand of the Holy One, for were it not that the Holy One helps him, he could not overcome it (Sukkah 52b); and it comes through the power of Torah, for nothing breaks the evil inclination but Torah (Zohar I 202a). And Yaakov merited wealth, for though all the Avos were rich…” Connection: Rav Tzadok elsewhere divides the gifts of wisdom, might and wealth among the Avos, the division he reads into the verses spoken by Yitzchak.

1369.label: Maareches HaElokus 8
1369.rest: — “Of the great attainment the righteous will attain in the future, our Rabbis said in an aggadah: Gavriel will make a hunt with the Leviathan, and were it not that the Holy One helps him he could not overcome it, as it says, ‘He that made him can bring near His sword’ (Iyov 40:19). With Gavriel they alluded to the attribute of Gevurah, from which desire comes; and with the Leviathan to Tiferes, the male Leviathan; and they alluded that when the righteous eat [of it]…” Connection: Maareches HaElokus reads the feast of the Leviathan as an inner attainment, the conquest of desire, as Rav Tzadok reads the future feast.

1370.label: Malbim, Vayikra 23:43
1370.rest: — “[The dispute over] the sukkah depends on this. The one who says ‘so that the sun not strike’ holds they were Clouds of Glory, and the one who says ‘a temporary dwelling’ holds they were actual sukkos. For according to the one who says actual sukkos, [the purpose is] that later generations not grow proud at the harvest, when their houses are full of good, and think this world their home and purpose; let them know and take to heart that ‘in sukkos I made the Children of Israel dwell,’ to awaken the ear that this world is [only a temporary dwelling].” Connection: The Malbim ties each side of the Gemara's dispute to a lesson of the sukkah, as Rav Tzadok does with the two opinions.

1371.label: R. Avraham Azulai, Ohr HaChammah on the Zohar, Vayishlach
1371.rest: — “Between the verse ‘And Yaakov came whole (shalem)’ and the verse ‘And His sukkah was in Shalem’ it is all one matter and one secret. The verse ‘And Yaakov came whole’ means that then faith joined with him, when he was whole, crowned in the place fitting for him; and ‘His sukkah was in Shalem’ means that then this sukkah was crowned.” Connection: The commentary links Yaakov's wholeness to the sukkah, as Rav Tzadok links “Yaakov came whole” to his journey to Sukkos.

1372.label: R. Chanoch Zundel, Etz Yosef on Bereishis Rabbah 68:2
1372.rest: — “‘A song for ascents’: Scripture speaks of Yaakov, as it says, ‘the Guardian of Israel.’ ‘To the mountains (harim)’: he expounds harim as horim, parents, as the Sages said, ‘leaping over the mountains — these are the Avos’; ‘to my teachers’ — my rabbis who teach me the ways of Torah; ‘and to those who formed me’ — those who guide me in the service of Hashem, in keeping His mitzvos.” Connection: The commentator on the Midrash Rav Tzadok cites explains its two terms as the teachers of Torah and the guides in avodah.

1373.label: R. Yosef Gikatilla, Shaarei Orah, Ninth Gate
1373.rest: — “Around the letter vav of the Name all the princes of the nations surround, and from the letter vav upward, which is the secret of Yah, they have no ascent. [Of this it says,] ‘And you shall tread upon their high places’ (Devarim 33:29), and ‘I will make you ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed you the heritage of Yaakov your father’ (Yeshayahu 58:14).” Connection: Shaarei Orah explains the verse of Shabbos that Rav Tzadok cites as Israel rising to a place where the princes of the nations have no hold.

1374.label: R. Naftali Tzvi Yehudah Berlin, Haamek Davar, Devarim 16:15
1374.rest: — “The verse does not depart from its plain meaning either: the term ‘tachog’ implies joy that comes with dancing and circling, as I wrote on ‘that they may celebrate (veyachogu) for Me’ (Shemos 5:1) — rejoicing in dance before Hashem, ‘rejoicing with trembling’ of holiness… And this is what is in the Rabbah, Emor 30, on ‘fullness of joys before You,’ that on Sukkos there are seven joys.” Connection: The Netziv ties the Midrash of the seven joys Rav Tzadok opens with to the plain sense of “you shall celebrate.”

1375.label: R. Shalom Buzaglo, Mikdash Melech on Zohar III 259a
1375.rest: — “Through the great illumination of the rivers of pure balsam revealed on the festival, [the waters] do not overcome the love of Israel: ‘they cannot extinguish the love.’ ‘A man’ — this is S"M, of whom the verse speaks; and the meaning of the verse is: ‘If a man’ — S"M — ‘would give all the wealth of his house for the love’ with which the Holy One loves Israel, so as to have a portion with them, ‘they would utterly scorn him,’ for he has no [share in it].” Connection: The commentary on the Zohar Rav Tzadok cites explains how the light of the festival keeps the accuser from buying a share in Israel's love.

1376.label: R. Zev Wolf Einhorn, Maharzu on Vayikra Rabbah 30:1
1376.rest: — “[‘Take’ is a gezeirah shavah] alluding to the taking of Torah and mitzvos, which are called ‘lekach,’ as it says, ‘For I have given you good lekach,’ and ‘Take My instruction.’ ‘And not silver’: certainly the verse does not come to forbid earning silver permissibly, and ‘Why do you weigh silver’ — is it forbidden to weigh silver? Therefore he expounds: so that you will not need to give silver to your enemy in the exile of Seir. ‘Because you were not satisfied with its wine’ — as Chazal said in Berachos, ‘and you will be satisfied’ refers to drinking.” Connection: Maharzu explains why the Midrash Rav Tzadok cites reads “take” of the four species as the taking of Torah.

1377.label: R. Yosef Gikatilla, Shaarei Tzedek 1
1377.rest: — “Of Pesach it says, ‘On the seventh day an Atzeres to Hashem your God’; and of Sukkos it says, ‘On the eighth day an Atzeres shall be for you’ — Shemini Atzeres is truly ours. Consider: the seventh is Atzeres, and its day is the Tzaddik, Yesod Olam, who is seventh… and on Sukkos the eighth Atzeres is ours, and this is Malchus, the Shechinah that dwells in Israel.” Connection: Gikatilla explains the two verses of Pesachim 68b, “to Hashem” and “for you,” through the sefiros of the seventh and eighth days, the contrast Rav Tzadok builds on.

1378.label: R. Chanoch Zundel, Etz Yosef on Bamidbar Rabbah 21:24
1378.rest: — “‘Rather, I add for you festivals to rejoice in, as it says, “On the eighth day an Atzeres shall be for you”’: that is, I have added Shemini Atzeres for you, besides the offerings of all the days of the festival, which are offerings for the abundance of good for the whole world. ‘Seventy bulls for the seventy nations,’ to bring them near to faith; and on the first day they offered thirteen bulls…” Connection: Like the Zohar Rav Tzadok cites, Etz Yosef sets the seventy bulls offered for the nations against the eighth day that belongs to Israel alone.

1379.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 13
1379.rest: — “But Yom Tov, which is a ‘holy convocation’ that Israel sanctify, bringing holiness from the supernal Holy into the Yom Tov — its meal is called the meal of the Holy One and His Shechinah, for immediately on Yom Tov Hashem dwells among the Children of Israel. It is called ‘of the Shechinah,’ and not of the Field of Holy Apples, for immediately all the holinesses rest upon Israel.” Connection: Rav Tzadok's own explanation, elsewhere, of why every Yom Tov meal is called the meal of the Holy One and His Shechinah.

1380.label: R. Yosef Chaim of Baghdad, Ben Yehoyada, Sukkah 55b
1380.rest: — “‘Make me a small meal, so that I may have enjoyment from you’: if the meal is large, people will say he came because of the enjoyment of the meal, since it is great; but if the meal is small, with no real measure of enjoyment, they will not say he came for it, but ‘I came for your sake.’ And so it is in what the parable represents.” Connection: Ben Yehoyada explains why the meal of the eighth day is small: its smallness shows that the bond itself is the point, as Rav Tzadok explains the day that belongs to Israel alone.

1381.label: R. Menachem Recanati, Recanati on the Torah, Re'eh
1381.rest: — “‘Six days you shall eat matzos, and on the seventh day an Atzeres to Hashem your God’: the great Rav [Ramban] wrote that by the way of truth, Atzeres is Knesses Yisrael, and the verse comes to teach us the secret of the day. But it is not equal to Shemini Atzeres, for the eighth is a festival in its own right, and its offering [is different].” Connection: Recanati contrasts the Atzeres of Pesach with Shemini Atzeres, the two verses whose dispute in Pesachim 68b Rav Tzadok explains.

1382.label: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Tishrei 13:5
1382.rest: — “The rejoicing of the Torah, and they rejoice on that day with the Torah — it appears to me according to the Zohar, Emor 104b: ‘Therefore it is written Atzeres, which is translated “gathering”; and on that day Yaakov is the head of the rejoicing, and all those guests rejoice with him; and so it is written, “Fortunate are you, Israel; who is like you,”’ and therefore on this day they read this parashah in the Torah; and it is written, ‘And He said to me: You are My servant, Israel, in whom I take glory.’ And since Yaakov is the attribute of truth, ‘Give truth to Yaakov’…” Connection: Bnei Yissaschar reads the same Zohar as the root of Simchas Torah and of reading Vezos HaBerachah, as Rav Tzadok does.

1383.label: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Shemini Atzeres
