1383.rest: — “Therefore Shemini Atzeres, which alludes to the future — and the harp of the days of Mashiach will have eight strings — has nothing to do with a temporary dwelling at all; on the contrary, then a permanent dwelling is called for, for all the conduct of the whole year will be by way of miracle. To allude to this is the counsel that we leave the sukkah to rejoice on the eighth: ‘And you shall be only joyful’ — to include the night of the last Yom Tov in the rejoicing.” Connection: Shem MiShmuel explains the joy of the eighth day, derived only from “ach same'ach,” as the joy of the future, the same verse Rav Tzadok explores.

1384.label: Malbim, Shmuel I 2:6
1384.rest: — “‘Hashem kills’ the children of the one with many children, ‘and gives life’ to the children of the barren one; and she adds that He also ‘brings down to She'ol and raises up’ the dead himself, to revive him, which is the resurrection of the dead. She means that three keys were not given into the hand of an agent — childbirth, the resurrection of the dead, and rain — as at the beginning of Taanis; and since she counted here childbirth and rain, which is sustenance, she counted the resurrection too.” Connection: The Malbim finds the three keys of Taanis 2a together in Chanah's song, the same three keys Rav Tzadok links to the rain of Shemini Atzeres.

1385.label: Maareches HaElokus 13
1385.rest: — “Since each day of the seven days of the festival alludes to one circuit [of the seven thousand years], therefore each day we circle the altar once, to allude that all the worlds will celebrate and circle around the supernal altar. And we make this circuit with the lulav and its species, for the lulav is four species in general and seven in detail, corresponding to the building [of the sefiros], which is four in general and seven in detail.” Connection: Maareches HaElokus gives the Kabbalistic root of the seven circuits with the lulav's seven species, the structure Rav Tzadok builds on.

1386.label: R. Zev Wolf Einhorn, Maharzu on Bereishis Rabbah 100:12
1386.rest: — “Where one finished, the one after him began, as in the Zohar on this verse and at the beginning of Bamidbar: Avraham sealed with ‘and he gave,’ and Yitzchak opened with ‘and may [God] give’; and so ‘Yitzchak called [Yaakov] and blessed him,’ and Yaakov called his sons and blessed them.” Connection: Maharzu shows the chain of blessings in which each blessing begins where the last ended, the principle of the Sifrei Rav Tzadok cites for Moshe's blessing.

1387.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah 3
1387.rest: — “And it says, ‘and with good deeds’: one who did not merit Torah, to meditate in it day and night, will merit through good deeds also the first three, as it says, ‘The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem; good understanding to all who do them’ — it does not say ‘to those who study them’ but ‘to those who do them’ (Berachos 17a)… And this is why the Midrash afterward brings the verse, ‘For the thing is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it.’” Connection: Both bring “in your mouth and in your heart, to do it” together with Berachos 17a's “to those who do them.”

1388.label: Pri Tzaddik, Re'eh 4
1388.rest: — “This is what he took in the parable, that the wicked prosper and the righteous suffer: ‘for two or three days’ they suffer in this world, that is, in the fourth millennium and the fifth… but their end is to rejoice at the last.” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other reading of “to do good for you at your end” (Devarim 8:16), suffering that is for the sake of the final good.

1389.label: Pri Tzaddik, Sukkos 45
1389.rest: — “And they make seven circuits, that the holiness of the seven shepherds should help to bring words of Torah into the heart; and this is Simchas Torah, for every year on Rosh Hashanah there is a renewal in words of Torah, as we always say…” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “the renewal in words of Torah that there is on Rosh Hashanah.”

1390.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Sivan 2
1390.rest: — “The main counsel for words of Torah to be absorbed in the heart is through longing and thirst for words of Torah; and this is ‘on this day,’ that words of Torah be new to you as if they were given today, and the longing be renewed. So every year, even though the Torah was already given, one must strive to attain a renewed longing and thirst for words of Torah, and through this he will merit to taste a renewed taste in words of Torah, that is, the reasons of the Torah, as it says, ‘More to be desired than gold… and sweeter than honey and the drippings of the honeycomb.’” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other reading of the same verse as the taste renewed in Torah, which he asks for here in “a good and sweet year.”

1391.label: Pri Tzaddik, Mishpatim 2
1391.rest: — “And afterward it is written, ‘And they went out into the wilderness of Shur,’ and it says in the holy Zohar (II 60a), ‘They went out to the wilderness to gaze at the Holy One… and they did not find Him’; and this is ‘and they found no water,’ and water is only Torah… That is, it was very bitter to them that the perception they had had departed from them, and they could not drink the waters of Marah, for they could not perceive at all. ‘And Hashem showed him a tree,’ and tree is only Torah.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “the bitterness Israel had at Marah”; both read the sweetening at Marah as Torah.

1392.label: Pri Tzaddik, Bamidbar 9
1392.rest: — “And this is what it says (Nechemiah 8:9), ‘For all the people wept’: on Rosh Hashanah teshuvah and regret came to them, which is through fear, through picturing that the King of kings stands over him and sees his deeds… And this is what he told them, ‘Do not be saddened, for the joy of Hashem is your strength’: through fear…” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other reading of Nechemiah's Rosh Hashanah, joining fear and teshuvah to the joy of Hashem, as he does here.

1393.label: Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 7
1393.rest: — “And in Bereishis Rabbah (17) there is a dispute… and so in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 27a)… and we said that both are the words of the living God, according to what Tosafos wrote (Rosh Hashanah 27a) on the dispute of R. Eliezer and R. Yehoshua.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “in thought the world was created in Tishrei, and in actuality in Nissan”; both resolve the dispute through Tosafos' reading.

1394.label: Pri Tzaddik, Mikeitz 12
1394.rest: — “The three prayers correspond to the Avos (Tikkunei Zohar 18)… And the aspect of fear we find in all the Avos: of Avraham Avinu it is written, ‘Now I know that you fear God,’ and Yitzchak's attribute is fear, ‘the Fear of Yitzchak.’” Connection: Both treat the attribute of “the Awesome” and find awe in each of the three Avos.

1395.label: Pri Tzaddik, Va'eschanan 2
1395.rest: — “May a man of Israel pray in a loud voice?… Chazal said, one who raises his voice in prayer is of those of little faith. And elsewhere they said, ‘The voice is the voice of Yaakov’ — the voice of Torah and the voice of prayer; and we say in the Shemoneh Esrei, ‘Hear our voice’… So too it is said of the Men of the Great Assembly, ‘And they cried out with a loud voice.’ Certainly, ordinary prayer to Hashem should not raise the voice… but sometimes, when a person is in great distress and can no longer contain…” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “sounding the voice from the depths of the heart in prayer”; both weigh the voice that breaks out from the depths.

1396.label: Machshavos Charutz 15
1396.rest: — “Through innovations in Torah one can draw new abundance from the supernal Mazal; and this is the manna itself, ‘bread from heaven,’ which came in the merit of Moshe, that is, through the power of the Torah… and this is the sustenance we ask for every day, to merit through prayer even one who is not worthy, for ‘a prayer of the poor man… rises above all prayers’ (Tehillim 102:1; Zohar I 168b), for the essence of prayer is from poverty.” Connection: Both tie the plea for sustenance to the supernal Mazal above the merits.

1397.label: Pri Tzaddik, Tazria 6
1397.rest: — “‘The mountain of Hashem's house shall be established at the head of the mountains’: who is the head of the mountains? This is Avraham the elder, the great priest, the head of all… according to what is said in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 36), ‘mountains — these are the Avos,’ and Avraham, first of the other mountains, is called the head of the mountains.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “Avraham's Chesed is called zakein.”

1398.label: Pri Tzaddik, Yisro 1
1398.rest: — “It is brought from the holy Arizal that R. Akiva was the root of the Oral Torah… and that Matan Torah is set in the chapter of R. Akiva in Maseches Shabbos because R. Akiva, the root of the Oral Torah, was the son of converts… And it says in the Gemara (Gittin 57b): ‘Of the descendants of Sisera…’” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “Sisera and the Oral Torah”; both see the Oral Torah drawn from afar, from the descendants of Sisera.

1399.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Rosh Hashanah 23
1399.rest: — “‘Fortunate is the people who know the teruah’: it does not say ‘who hear’ or ‘who blow’ the teruah, but ‘who know the teruah’ (Zohar III 231b)… for we learn both [the moaning and the wailing] from their opposite, as it says in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 33b): ‘A day of teruah shall it be for you,’ which the Targum renders ‘a day of yevava.’” Connection: Both read “who know the teruah” as an inner knowing of the teruah that goes beyond the act of sounding it.

1400.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Rosh Hashanah 23
1400.rest: — “As explained in the Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 55): tekiah is from the side of the right, shevarim from the side of the left, and the shalsheles, which is teruah, from the side of both. That is, tekiah alludes to the trait of Avraham our father, which is Chesed… and through the trait of Yitzchak, which is Gevurah… and teruah from the side of both, for Yaakov our father shines in the world so that even in the divisions of this world His glory is found in complete unity.” Connection: Both set tekiah, shevarim and teruah against Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov from the same passage of the Tikkunim.

1401.label: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 9
1401.rest: — “The first three blessings are the holiness of the Avos: ‘Shield of Avraham,’ then ‘You are mighty’ corresponding to the Fear of Yitzchak, then ‘You are holy’ corresponding to Yaakov, as it says, ‘They will sanctify the Holy One of Yaakov’… and afterward the twelve middle blessings corresponding to the holiness of the twelve tribes, as written in the Raya Mehemna (Zohar III 4a).” Connection: Both map the blessings of the Amidah onto the Avos and the tribes to explain where each insertion belongs.

1402.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah 15
1402.rest: — “It is brought in the Tikkunim that the Ten Days of Teshuvah correspond to the ten utterances, which correspond to the ten sefiros, and corresponding to these are the ten verses of Malchuyos; that is, we crown the Creator in these ten days, saying ‘the holy King,’ for the glory of His kingship is revealed upon us from above to below.” Connection: Both tie the tens of Rosh Hashanah to the ten utterances of creation.

1403.label: Pri Tzaddik, Chukas 1
1403.rest: — “About this it says ‘He has not done so for any nation’… even regarding the judgments, which the intellect agrees with and which some of them keep by reason, it is written ‘and judgments they have not known’: even if they keep the judgments, they do not bring da'as into them… whereas Israel, who act only because of the command of the Omnipresent, the judgments bring da'as into them and teach them.” Connection: Both read “and judgments they have not known” as the da'as that only Israel draws from the mitzvos.

1404.label: Pri Tzaddik, Bamidbar 9
1404.rest: — “As we find in the verse (Nechemiah 8:10): ‘Do not be saddened, for the joy of Hashem is your strength’… for the completeness of joy in holiness is when it comes from within fear, as it says (Tanna DeVei Eliyahu Rabbah 3): ‘I rejoiced from within my fear.’” Connection: Both read Nechemiah's “joy of Hashem” as joy that grows out of fear.

1405.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 27
1405.rest: — “In the holy Zohar (II 121a): ‘And wisdom, from where is it found?’ — wisdom comes forth from the place called Kodesh HaKodashim; ‘from where’ (me'ayin) is the hidden Ancient One of all hidden things, who is called Ayin.” Connection: Both bring this Zohar to identify the Kodesh HaKodashim with the hidden source above Chochmah.

1406.label: Pri Tzaddik, Shemos 8
1406.rest: — “The shofar indicates fear, as it says, ‘If a shofar is blown in the city, will the people not tremble?’ (Amos 3:6)… and through fear one comes to teshuvah, for ‘fear’ is expounded as teshuvah (Avodah Zarah 19a; Berachos 17a): through fear he remembers, regrets his sins and returns from them.” Connection: Both tie the shofar to fear and see that fear as what brings teshuvah.

1407.label: Pri Tzaddik, Motzaei Yom Kippur 9
1407.rest: — “It is brought in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 36): ‘And there was light’ — this is Rosh Hashanah, as it says, ‘And it was the day’; and everywhere ‘vayehi’ is an expression of distress. For Rosh Hashanah is ‘this day, the beginning of Your works’… but in order that it flow into this world to the one receiving, it must come through contraction.” Connection: Both read “vayehi” as distress on Rosh Hashanah, through which its light comes to be received.

1408.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah 21
1408.rest: — “In the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 18a) they expounded the verse ‘Seek Hashem while He may be found, call Him while He is near’ as referring to the Ten Days of Teshuvah for the individual, and right after it is written, ‘Let the wicked forsake his way’… the prophet taught us the order of prayer to Hashem while He is near to us in the Ten Days of Teshuvah: ‘Let the wicked forsake his way,’ for this shall be the prayer, that Hashem help us toward teshuvah.” Connection: Both expound “Seek Hashem while He may be found” on the Ten Days of Teshuvah.

1409.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah 16
1409.rest: — “It is brought in the Midrash that a king of flesh and blood decrees decrees and does not keep them himself, but the Holy One, blessed be He, keeps all the mitzvos; and so it says in the Gemara that the Holy One, blessed be He, puts on tefillin and prays… all the mitzvos and decrees of the Holy One, blessed be He, He, as it were, fulfills them first.” Connection: Both build on the Midrash that Hashem Himself fulfills the mitzvos He commands.

1410.label: Pri Tzaddik, Beha'aloscha 1
1410.rest: — “Between level and level there is a journey, in which he goes and travels to reach that level, and then he is in turmoil; and when he reaches the level he is at rest. And this is all of man all the days of his life: in the days of action he is in turmoil, and that is preparation to come to Shabbos.” Connection: Both describe man in this world as one who keeps going from level to level.

1411.label: Pri Tzaddik, Devarim 10
1411.rest: — “And this is what they said (Nedarim 22b): ‘Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah… and the book of Yehoshua,’ which is the Oral Torah that Moshe received from Sinai and handed to Yehoshua.” Connection: Both expound this Gemara on the Oral Torah contained within the Written Torah and handed down through Yehoshua.

1412.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Elul 3
1412.rest: — “And it says afterward, ‘good understanding to all who do them’; ‘good’ is Torah, as they said, ‘there is no good but Torah.’ And it concludes there… ‘it does not say to those who learn them, but to those who do them’… for they said (Sanhedrin 99b): ‘as if he made them,’ regarding words of Torah, for it says, ‘and you shall keep the words of this covenant and do them.’” Connection: Both expound Berachos 17a's “to those who do them” on Torah study that becomes deed.

1413.label: Pri Tzaddik, Va'eschanan 12
1413.rest: — “It is in the Pesikta (Shuvah): Rabbeinu HaKadosh expounded, Great is the power of teshuvah, for as soon as a person thinks in his heart to do teshuvah, it immediately rises for him up to… and stands before the Throne of Glory.” Connection: Both hold that a thought of teshuvah in the heart already takes effect at once.

1414.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah 13
1414.rest: — “In the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 22): Adam HaRishon met him and said to him, ‘What became of your judgment?’ He said, ‘I did teshuvah and was reconciled.’ Adam HaRishon began to strike his face and said, ‘Such is the power of teshuvah, and I did not know!’ Immediately he opened and said, ‘A psalm, a song for the day of Shabbos: It is good to give thanks to Hashem.’” Connection: Both build the Shabbos of teshuvah on Adam's discovery of the power of teshuvah and his song for Shabbos.

1415.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 8
1415.rest: — “In the psalm of Shabbos it is written, ‘It is good to give thanks to Hashem and to sing to Your Name, O Most High.’ ‘It is good to give thanks’ is the aspect of teshuvah, as it says (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 19) that whoever confesses his transgressions is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom, as it says, ‘He who confesses and forsakes shall obtain mercy.’” Connection: Both read “lehodos” in the Shabbos psalm as confession and teshuvah that Shabbos itself awakens.

1416.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayechi 10
1416.rest: — “On the day of Shabbos we grasp that everything is only for good, even though we do not understand the good. And about this it says, ‘For I know the thoughts that I think concerning you, says Hashem, thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you a future and hope’; and we believe this even though we do not grasp and understand how and what.” Connection: Both bring Yirmiyahu 29:11 to say that Hashem's thoughts toward us are good even when we cannot see it.

1417.label: Pri Tzaddik, Matos 11
1417.rest: — “Although there it is written ‘he who confesses and forsakes’ and here it is written ‘it is good to give thanks,’ and forsaking is not mentioned, this is because on Shabbos the words themselves are effective, so that they enter the heart and he forsakes the evil of himself… and this is in the manner of what they said (Ta'anis 8a): ‘They beguiled Him with their mouth,’ etc., ‘and yet He, being merciful, forgives iniquity.’” Connection: Both teach that on Shabbos words of confession alone are effective, citing “they beguiled Him with their mouth.”

1418.label: Pri Tzaddik, Eikev 11
1418.rest: — “And about this it says, ‘My speech shall drip like the dew,’ which is the aspect of the Oral Torah, which is like dew: it is not seen as it falls, but only from what we see afterward, that the earth is moist, is it recognized that dew fell. So too the Oral Torah: it seems to a person that he is innovating the words of Torah, but in truth they are the words of the living God.” Connection: Both read “My speech shall drip like the dew” as the Oral Torah.

1419.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeitzei 10
1419.rest: — “Therefore we read the haftarah ‘Return, Yisrael,’ in which Levanon is mentioned three times… ‘and his roots shall strike like the Levanon,’ according to what they said (Yoma 39b): why is it called Levanon? Because it whitens the sins of Israel… and afterward it is written, ‘and his fragrance like the Levanon.’” Connection: Both expound the three mentions of Levanon in this haftarah on sins whitened until they become merits.

1420.label: Pri Tzaddik, Va'eschanan 12
1420.rest: — “As explained in the Reishis Chochmah on what they said (Yoma 86a), ‘Great is teshuvah, for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory,’ meaning that it is effective even for a sin that reached up to the Throne of Glory. And in truth both explanations are in the Pesikta (Shuvah)… ‘even up to the Throne of Glory, and you do teshuvah, I accept you at once.’” Connection: Both weigh the two readings of “teshuvah reaches up to the Throne of Glory.”

1421.label: Pri Tzaddik, Nitzavim 17
1421.rest: — “‘For this commandment… is not in heaven, that you should say, Who will go up to heaven for us and take it for us’… Rashi explained that if it were in heaven you would have to go up after it. And they expounded this from the extra words in this verse… for from the sense of ‘that you should say’ it seems that one would truly need to say so if it were in heaven or across the sea.” Connection: Both expound the extra words of this verse on what a person must do if Torah and teshuvah seem out of reach.

1422.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5
1422.rest: — “And on Shabbos it is written, ‘It is good to give thanks to Hashem,’ and in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (ch. 19): whoever confesses and forsakes is saved, etc.; and so in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah, end of 22): ‘Such is the power of teshuvah,’ etc., he opened and said, ‘A psalm, a song for the day of Shabbos.’” Connection: Both join “one who confesses and forsakes” to Adam's song for Shabbos.

1423.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Hashanah 9
1423.rest: — “On Rosh Hashanah and all the Ten Days of Teshuvah we say the chapter ‘A song of ascents: Out of the depths I have called You, Hashem; my Lord, hear my voice’… the intent is the voice of a cry that comes out of the depths of the heart, so that he cannot even shape it into words with his lips, but cries out in a simple voice from the pain of his heart; and such a prayer is the most accepted.” Connection: Both expound “Out of the depths” as the call of teshuvah from the deepest place.

1424.label: Takanas HaShavin 11
1424.rest: — “And this is through the washing of ‘and I will be whiter than snow,’ that he return far finer than he was before; and so he asked at the start of his words, ‘Wash me thoroughly,’ that He wash him with much washing until he be completely white even from a sin that had become unintentional, for he felt in his soul the awakening of teshuvah out of love.” Connection: Both read David's “Wash me thoroughly… whiter than snow” as a plea for a cleansing beyond what teshuvah alone achieves.

1425.label: Pri Tzaddik, Eikev 18
1425.rest: — “‘A psalm of David: Hashem is my shepherd; I shall not lack… Your rod and Your staff — they comfort me.’ In the Pesikta on this haftarah, ‘And Zion said, Hashem has forsaken me’… what comfort is this to broken hearts, when we see that more than eighteen hundred years have passed and we have not yet been saved?” Connection: Both read “Your rod and Your staff comfort me” as comfort found in the concealment and chastisement themselves.

1426.label: Pri Tzaddik, Va'eschanan 3
1426.rest: — “It is in the Midrash Rabbah on this parashah: the gates of prayer are sometimes open and sometimes locked, but the gates of teshuvah are always open… just as a mikveh is sometimes open and sometimes locked, so the gates of prayer… but the sea is always open, so the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, is always open to receive those who return.” Connection: Both build on Devarim Rabbah 2:12, that prayer needs a time of favor while teshuvah is always open.

1427.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 31
1427.rest: — “It is in the Gemara (Yoma 81b): ‘You shall afflict your souls on the ninth’ — do we fast on the ninth? Do we not fast on the tenth? Rather, to tell you that whoever eats and drinks on the ninth, Scripture considers it as though he fasted the ninth and the tenth… for Hashem set that all the service of man below be directed according to what Hashem is then engaged in above.” Connection: Both ask why eating on the ninth counts as fasting and answer from the inner meaning of the day.

1428.label: Pri Tzaddik, Motzaei Yom Kippur 1
1428.rest: — “To explain the Mishnah, it is brought there (Yoma 71b): the Rabbis taught… and everyone went after him… ‘Let the descendants of the nations go in peace, who do the deed of Aharon’… and what is this story to us, to tell the disgrace of the Kohen Gadol? And what deed of Aharon did they do? But the deed of Aharon was that he loved peace and pursued peace and drew them near to Torah.” Connection: Both expound this Gemara about the Kohen Gadol leaving the Holy on Yom Kippur and Shemaya and Avtalyon.

1429.label: Pri Tzaddik, Beha'aloscha 6
1429.rest: — “…to lean after bodily desire, and especially the desire of eating, for this was the venom of the serpent at first, as it says, ‘that it was a desire… and she took of its fruit and ate,’ and through this death came into the world. And the heart, from which come the issues of life, when it refines itself so as not to be drawn after the feeling of its own pleasure, can of itself reach the level of eternal life.” Connection: Both trace the desire of eating to the serpent's venom and its repair through holy eating.

1430.label: Pri Tzaddik, Beshalach 11
1430.rest: — “And this is what it says (Chullin 89a): ‘When I bestow greatness upon you, you diminish yourselves before Me; I gave greatness to Avraham,’ etc.; that is, the more His Godliness was revealed to them, the more they recognized their own lowliness.” Connection: Both bring Chullin 89a to show that humility grows with the revelation of Godliness.

1431.label: Pri Tzaddik, Acharei Mos 2
1431.rest: — “In the Kodesh HaKodashim it is written, ‘And no man shall be in the Ohel Moed,’ not even angels, for it is written, ‘and the likeness of their faces was the face of a man’ (Yechezkel 1:10)… and yet the Kohen Gadol saw and fed his eyes from…” Connection: Both expound “no man shall be in the Ohel Moed” on the Kohen Gadol on Yom Kippur rising above the human.

1432.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Sukkos 15
1432.rest: — “In the holy Zohar (Pinchas 214b): ‘On Rosh Hashanah the left arm awakens to receive the Matronita… on the first day of the festival the right awakens to receive, in order to embrace’; that is, from Rosh Hashanah the Will, blessed be He, begins to shine without any garment… and on Sukkos the Holy One, blessed be He, holds man, as it is written, ‘and His right hand embraces me.’” Connection: Both expound this Zohar's order from Rosh Hashanah to Sukkos, the left arm and then the right.

1433.label: Pri Tzaddik, Korach 5
1433.rest: — “And this was Korach's mistake, that he disputed Aharon, who loved peace and pursued peace, loved people and drew them near to Torah; that is, his power to bring the words of Torah into the heart of Israel, which is the essence of the Oral Torah, as it says, ‘For the lips of the Kohen guard knowledge, and Torah they seek from his mouth.’” Connection: Both read Aharon's love of peace as his power to bring Israel close to Torah.

1434.label: Pri Tzaddik, Re'eh 14
1434.rest: — “According to what they said (Koheles Rabbah 9:3), that on Motzaei Yom Kippur a heavenly voice goes out and says to them, ‘Go, eat your bread in joy; your prayer has already been heard’… and it is as the verse concludes, ‘for God has already accepted your deeds’; therefore ‘eat your bread in joy and drink your wine with a good heart.’” Connection: Both expound the heavenly voice of Motzaei Yom Kippur as joy that follows from deeds already accepted.

1435.label: Pri Tzaddik, Toldos 2
1435.rest: — “And this is what we find in the Gemara, the expression ‘I would make a festive day for the Rabbis,’ which Rashi explained (Kiddushin 31a) as a meal for the students. And why the expression ‘a festive day’? But the intent is that holiness appears in the meal, and this is ‘a good day,’ the light that ‘was good.’” Connection: Both ask why a celebratory meal is called “a festive day” and find holiness revealed in it.

1436.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeitzei 3
1436.rest: — “And it concludes there that so it is written in Mishneh Torah: ‘because you did not serve Hashem your God with joy and with goodness of heart’; that is, this is the main intent, that the service be in the innermost point of the heart, and from this joy is born in the heart, and through this one is redeemed from all kinds of thoughts that distress and oppress the soul.” Connection: Both expound “with joy and with goodness of heart” as joy born when the service enters the inner heart.

1437.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 36
1437.rest: — “R. Akiva said: Fortunate are you, Israel! Before whom are you purified, and who purifies you? Your Father in Heaven, as it says, ‘And I will sprinkle pure water upon you and you will be pure,’ and it says, ‘The mikveh of Israel is Hashem’: just as a mikveh purifies the tamei, so the Holy One, blessed be He, purifies Israel (Yoma 85b).” Connection: Both expound R. Akiva's “The mikveh of Israel is Hashem” at the close of Yoma.

1438.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Hashanah 27
1438.rest: — “According to the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 21; Shocher Tov 27) on ‘Hashem is my light and my salvation’: ‘my light’ on Rosh Hashanah and ‘my salvation’ on Yom Kippur; that is, on Rosh Hashanah illumination comes to the heart from the revelation of the kingship of Heaven. And this is why it says ‘my light’ specifically, and not another's.” Connection: Both expound this Midrash on “my light” for Rosh Hashanah and “my salvation” for Yom Kippur.

1439.label: Pri Tzaddik, Re'eh 14
1439.rest: — “In all the meals of Shabbos we mention joy… the matter is according to what they said (Koheles Rabbah 9), that on Motzaei Yom Kippur a heavenly voice goes out and says to them, ‘Go, eat your bread in joy; your prayer has already been heard’… and so on Shabbos, for it is expounded on the verse ‘And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good.’” Connection: Both join the feast of Motzaei Yom Kippur to the joy of the Shabbos meals.

1440.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeishev 11
1440.rest: — “In the future Hashem will clarify, through all Israel doing teshuvah out of love, that intentional sins will become like merits. And this is what they said (Shabbos 89b): ‘If your sins are like these years, which have been arranged and coming from the six days of creation until now.’” Connection: Both tie sins becoming merits to what was arranged from the six days of creation.

1441.label: Pri Tzaddik, Shemini 3
1441.rest: — “But the matter is according to what they said (Shabbos 31b): the Holy One, blessed be He, created His world only so that they would fear Him, as it says, ‘And God has made it so that they fear Him’ (Koheles 3:14).” Connection: Both bring Koheles 3:14 on fear of Heaven as the purpose of creation.

1442.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pekudei 9
1442.rest: — “‘And what blessing is it that blesses this table that is set and delighted in properly? Then you shall delight in Hashem,’ for this is said in the verse about one who delights in Shabbos… ‘and you call Shabbos a delight… then you shall delight,’ that is, he merits the revelation of the aspect of Atika, which is called ‘al Hashem,’ above Hashem.” Connection: Both read “then (az) you shall delight in Hashem” as the revelation of Atika above the Name.

1443.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach 6
1443.rest: — “According to the Midrash Rabbah (Matos): three gifts were created in the world… one who merits wisdom merits everything, one who merits might merits everything, one who merits wealth merits everything — when they are gifts of Heaven and come through the power of Torah… Yitzchak merited might, as they said, ‘Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination.’” Connection: Both tie Yitzchak's might and wealth to gifts of Heaven that come through the power of Torah.

1444.label: Machshavos Charutz 19
1444.rest: — “Avraham our father was the beginning of faith, as it says, ‘And he believed in Hashem, and He counted it to him as righteousness,’ which is the beginning of the building of the Israelite nation and of Knesses Yisrael; and since the soul of the convert that he had was not yet clarified, so that he be counted a native (ezrach) in Israel and be called ‘the Ezrachi’ (Bereishis Rabbah 42:8), his faith was not yet complete.” Connection: Both discuss how Avraham the convert came to be called “the Ezrachi,” a native in Israel.

1445.label: Pri Tzaddik, Matos 13
1445.rest: — “And in the Midrash (Rabbah and Tanchuma on this parashah): three gifts were created in the world; one who merits one of them takes the treasure of the whole world. One who merits wisdom merits everything… and might, the essence of might being as it says, ‘Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination’… one who merits wealth merits everything.” Connection: Both expound the Midrash of the three gifts, wisdom, might and wealth, as gifts of Heaven.

1446.label: Pri Tzaddik, Toldos 4
1446.rest: — “And afterward in the holy Zohar: if so, what is the Livyasan and what is the ox?… ‘On that day Hashem will punish… the Livyasan, the straight serpent, and the Livyasan, the twisted serpent’… and the reason is that these three are all from the husk of desire, and therefore they are called ‘straight serpent, twisted serpent.’” Connection: Both read the Livyasan of the future feast as the husk of desire that is overcome.

1447.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach 10
1447.rest: — “‘And Yaakov came whole’: they expounded in the Gemara (Shabbos 33b), whole in his body, whole in his wealth, whole in his Torah. And the three things correspond to what is said, ‘with all your heart, with all your soul and with all your means.’ Whole in his body, that he was healed of his limp.” Connection: Both expound “And Yaakov came whole” after his struggle with Esav's angel.

1448.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeitzei 2
1448.rest: — “R. Shmuel bar Nachman opened: ‘A song of ascents: I lift my eyes to the mountains’ — to the parents (horim), to those who taught me and made me… ‘From where will my help come?’… Eliezer… and I have not even one ring… he went back and said… I will not give up hope in my Creator, but ‘my help is from Hashem.’” Connection: Both expound this Midrash on Yaakov lifting his eyes and finding his help from Hashem alone.

1449.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni 1
1449.rest: — “The time in this month is for wiping out Amalek, who falls only at the hand of the offspring of Yosef, who is the opposite of Esav, as is reckoned in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Ki Seitzei 10); and so Amalek accuses against the holiness of Israel in this.” Connection: Both bring the saying that Esav falls only at the hand of Yosef's offspring.

1450.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeira 1
1450.rest: — “Avraham our father is called the first of the converts (Chagigah 3a), for at first our fathers were idol worshippers… and he merited the name ‘Eisan HaEzrachi,’ who is Avraham our father, as they said, that he merited to be called a native in Israel, meaning one who is from the root and holy stock of Israel, as in the Zohar (Emor); and this is a deep matter, hidden and concealed in this world: how is it possible to change the root?” Connection: Both discuss how Avraham, “the first of the converts,” became “Eisan HaEzrachi,” a native of Israel.

1451.label: Pri Tzaddik, Purim 2
1451.rest: — “The essence in these days is the feast, and this is according to what is said (Zohar III 271b): ‘Come, eat of My bread’ — this is the Written Torah; ‘and drink of the wine I have mixed’ — this is the wine of the Oral Torah.” Connection: Both bring this Zohar reading bread and wine as the Written and Oral Torah.

1452.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pinchas 18
1452.rest: — “As it says in the Raya Mehemna (III 123b): vav and heh, the Torah and the mitzvah, which are son and daughter; that is, vav, the trait of Tiferes, the Name Havayah, indicates Torah, and heh, the trait of Malchus, the Name Adnus, indicates mitzvah. This is according to what is said in the Gemara (Sotah 21a): Scripture likened the mitzvah to a lamp: just as a lamp gives light only for a time, so a mitzvah gives light only for a time.” Connection: Both join the Raya Mehemna's “Torah and mitzvah, son and daughter” to Sotah 21a's lamp and light.

1453.label: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Savo 7
1453.rest: — “And it is in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 75) that Yitzchak said to Yaakov, ‘Come, and I will bless you with the blessing of the exiles’… ‘In six troubles He will save you, and in seven no evil will touch you.’ One may say that ‘six troubles’ alludes to the six exiles, which are Egypt, Ashur of the ten tribes, and the exile of the four kingdoms.” Connection: Both read “in six troubles He will save you” as the six exiles and kingdoms Israel passes through.

1454.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 40
1454.rest: — “On Shemini Atzeres it is written, ‘an assembly shall be for you,’ and here it is written, ‘an assembly to Hashem your God,’ and R. Eliezer and R. Yehoshua disputed this (Pesachim 68b). And in the Tanchuma (Pinchas 15) it says about Shemini Atzeres that it should have been fifty days after the festival, just as Atzeres is fifty days after the festival, but the Holy One, blessed be He, said, it is winter.” Connection: Both build on the two verses “an assembly to Hashem” and “an assembly for you” and the dispute in Pesachim 68b.

1455.label: Pri Tzaddik, Bereishis 6
1455.rest: — “On Yom Tov we say, ‘This is the meal of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah,’ and on Shabbos we say, ‘the meal of the Field of Holy Apples and Ze'ir Anpin,’ which is one matter, the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah… but added on Shabbos is the meal of Atika Kadisha.” Connection: Both compare the Yom Tov meal of “the Holy One and His Shechinah” with the Shabbos meal of Atika Kadisha.

1456.label: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 9
1456.rest: — “And the Written Torah is likened to rain, as it says, ‘My teaching shall drop like the rain,’ and ‘teaching’ (lekach) means only Torah, as it is written, ‘For I have given you a good teaching,’ and this is the Written Torah, which comes down with might from heaven.” Connection: Both read “My teaching shall drop like the rain” as Torah descending from heaven like rain.

1457.label: Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 5
1457.rest: — “It is in the Gemara (Pesachim 68b): all agree regarding Atzeres that we also require ‘for you,’ because it is the day on which the Torah was given… and Rashi explained that he should rejoice on it with food and drink, to show that the day on which the Torah was given is pleasing and accepted.” Connection: Both expound “all agree regarding Atzeres that we require ‘for you.’”

1458.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayechi 11
1458.rest: — “And all three flow from Atika Kadisha, as it says (Mo'ed Katan 28a): ‘Life, children and sustenance do not depend on merit but on mazal’; and it is in the holy Zohar (III 79b) that the holy Mazal is Atika, which is the trait of Ayin.” Connection: Both tie children, life and sustenance to the Mazal above merit.

1459.label: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Seitzei 15
1459.rest: — “In the Gemara (Menachos 29b): when Moshe went up on high he found the Holy One, blessed be He, sitting and tying crowns to the letters… ‘There is a man who will be at the end of many generations, Akiva ben Yosef is his name, who will expound upon each and every thorn heaps upon heaps of laws’… he went and sat at the end of eight rows and did not know what they were saying… We must understand why Moshe Rabbeinu did not understand what even the students of R. Akiva understood.” Connection: Both ask why Moshe did not grasp what R. Akiva's students understood.

1460.label: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Elul 3
1460.rest: — “In Sefer Yetzirah: He made the letter yud king over action… Elul in the year and the left hand in the soul. The letter yud of the holy Name indicates the sefirah of Chochmah, and it is written, ‘How great are Your works, Hashem; You made them all with wisdom.’” Connection: Both build Elul on Sefer Yetzirah's yud, action and the left hand, read as action repaired through wisdom.

1461.label: R. Yosef of Izhbitz, Tiferes Yosef, Rosh Hashanah 21
1461.rest: — “And this is what it says in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 94): they see the ashes of Yitzchak heaped upon the altar; that is, his prayer was effective so that this is always before Him, that He desires the life of Israel. And for this we pray today on Rosh Hashanah, ‘And the binding of Yitzchak remember today in mercy for his offspring,’ and the blessing concludes, ‘Blessed… Who remembers the covenant.’” Connection: Both expound the Akeidah of Yitzchak remembered in Zichronos as the bond that binds Hashem to Israel.

1462.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Rosh Hashanah 15
1462.rest: — “As they said (Rosh Hashanah 16a): Say before Me on Rosh Hashanah Malchuyos, Zichronos and Shofaros: Malchuyos, so that you make Me King over you… Zichronos, so that your remembrance rise before Me for good. And with what? With the shofar… that you contract yourselves to nullify all your will to the simple Will, blessed be He, and this contraction is called shofar.” Connection: Both expound “so that you make Me King over you” and what Malchuyos, Zichronos and Shofaros accomplish.

1463.label: Pri Tzaddik, Acharei Mos 7
1463.rest: — “In the Tanchuma: the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw that the Beis HaMikdash would be destroyed… ‘With what will you be atoned? Occupy yourselves with words of Torah, which are likened to offerings’… and so the prophet says, ‘Take with you words.’” Connection: Both read “take with you words” as words of Torah that atone in place of the offerings.

1464.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 9
1464.rest: — “On Yom Kippur all the details of the twenty-eight times are included together in the root of His unity, blessed be He, which is without limit… and from the awakening of such strength a person could grow bold in his soul with excessive expansion and not contract himself; therefore it is said of this day, ‘He shall not come at all times,’ that is, not with the strength of the inclusion of the times awakened on this day, but ‘with this (zos) shall Aharon come into the Holy.’” Connection: Both expound “with this shall Aharon come” on the Kohen Gadol's entry on Yom Kippur.

1465.label: Tzidkas HaTzaddik 218
1465.rest: — “Only through Torah is the victory, that he desires only words of Torah; of itself he does not desire the matters of this world at all, and does not grow angry over them or envy them except in words of Torah. If so, its victory is through iskafya, subjugation, so that the left is hidden and conquered and does not do its work.” Connection: Both distinguish iskafya, subjugating the evil inclination, from is'hapcha, transforming it.

1466.label: Pri Tzaddik, Toldos 10
1466.rest: — “We ask for the weekdays that they be ‘clinging to Your fear,’ clinging to the trait of Shabbos, which is fear; and so it says in the holy Zohar (I 5b): the Shabbos of Erev Shabbos is fear, and fear rests in it; and as we said, this is why the meal of Motzaei Shabbos is called Melaveh Malkah, for it is joined and clinging to the holiness of the Shabbos meals.” Connection: Both tie the Melaveh Malkah meal to carrying the fear of Shabbos into the week.

1467.label: Pri Tzaddik, Re'eh 13
1467.rest: — “And afterward it says, ‘to do what is upright in the eyes of Hashem your God,’ in the manner of what they said (Ta'anis 15a): the righteous for light and the upright for joy, as it says, ‘and for the upright of heart, joy’; for the tzaddik is one who still has dealings with the evil inclination, so that he must be mighty.” Connection: Both expound Ta'anis 15a's “the righteous for light, the upright for joy” on the levels of tzaddik and upright.

1468.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Sukkos 86
1468.rest: — “My grandfather, the holy gaon, said: after the victory of Israel they go to the sukkah, as we find with Yaakov our father, that after he defeated the angel of Esav it says, ‘And Yaakov journeyed to Sukkos’; and so when Israel defeated Egypt it says, ‘that I made the Children of Israel dwell in sukkos when I brought them out of the land of Egypt.’” Connection: Both see the sukkah completed in Yaakov, who journeyed to Sukkos after defeating Esav's angel.

1469.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Sukkos 88
1469.rest: — “It is brought in the Yerushalmi: if I have become liable to exile, may it be Your will that his going out of his house to the sukkah be counted as though I had gone into exile… for always after Israel win the lot they must enter the sukkah, as we find with Yaakov our father.” Connection: Both explain the prayer that leaving one's house for the sukkah count as going into exile.

1470.label: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 7
1470.rest: — “And this is according to what is said in the Zohar Chadash (Ki Sisa): ‘Remember the day of Shabbos’ — in the secret of the covenant, which is Yesod, to which Yosef holds; and therefore it is called Shabbos, for Yosef is called Kol, and Shabbos too is called Kol; and so it says (there, end of Toldos) that the Musaf of Shabbos corresponds to the tzaddik, foundation of the world.” Connection: Both bring the Zohar Chadash that Yosef is called “Kol” and corresponds to the Musaf of Shabbos.

1471.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Sukkos 28
1471.rest: — “It is brought in the Yalkut Shimoni (Emor) in the name of the Pesikta: whoever fulfills the mitzvah of sukkah in this world, the Holy One, blessed be He, gives him a portion in the future in the sukkah of Sedom… which was covered by seven trees, one above another.” Connection: Both expound the Pesikta's promise of a portion in “the sukkah of Sedom.”

1472.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Hoshana Rabbah 8
1472.rest: — “For only through the last trait, the trait of Malchus, the trait of David, is the whole purpose of the will of Hashem completed perfectly; for through this trait Israel complete the glory of Heaven by the power of the choice of their good will; and therefore the seventh day, which is attributed to David the king, is the day of the aravah.” Connection: Both tie the day of the aravah to David's ushpiza and the trait of Malchus.

1473.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Sukkos 24
1473.rest: — “David the king said, ‘No weapon formed against you shall succeed,’ for he is appointed over all the kinds of the world; that is, David the king always had victory against nature and against all the nations of the world, for in this world Hashem set concealment and darkness… and David the king clarified it according to his strength in this concealment until he showed openly to all eyes that the whole earth is full of His glory.” Connection: Both expound the Zohar's verse for David's ushpiza, “No weapon formed against you shall succeed.”

1474.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Shemini Atzeres 31
1474.rest: — “‘You shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed’: since in this festival, which is the time of ingathering, man's vessel of reception is completed… therefore Hashem teaches man counsel, ‘you shall surely tithe,’ as they explained in the Gemara (Ta'anis 9a): what is ‘aser te'aser’? Tithe so that you become wealthy; for this is the main acquisition, what one can give back to Hashem.” Connection: Both explain why “Aser te'aser” is read on Shemini Atzeres.

1475.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Sukkos 56
1475.rest: — “For the matter of the revival of the dead is that Hashem pours His light into the inanimate, and so is the matter of rain, that His influence descends from above and breaks through all the screens until it reaches man's grasp; and further they said in the Gemara (Ta'anis 7a): Great is the day of rain, more than the revival of the dead, for rain is for all, for the righteous and the wicked.” Connection: Both expound “Great is the day of rain, more than the revival of the dead.”

1476.label: Pri Tzaddik, Sukkos 18
1476.rest: — “The source of the text is the Pesikta: the mitzvah of sukkah comes after Yom Kippur; after the sins have been forgiven, perhaps they have become liable to exile, so let the mitzvah of sukkah be like the exile of Bavel, as it is written, ‘And you shall come to Bavel; there you shall be saved; there Hashem will redeem you from the hand of all your enemies.’ And we must understand why it mentions specifically the exile of Bavel.” Connection: Both expound the Pesikta that likens the sukkah to the exile of Bavel.

1477.label: Pri Tzaddik, Tu B'Av 2
1477.rest: — “In the Mishnah at the end of Ta'anis: there were no festive days for Israel like the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur… and so it says, ‘Go out and see, daughters of Zion… on the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart’: ‘the day of his wedding’ is the giving of the Torah, and ‘the day of the joy of his heart’ is the building of the Beis HaMikdash.” Connection: Both expound “on the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart.”

1478.label: R. Gershon Henoch of Radzin, Sod Yesharim, Simchas Torah 3
1478.rest: — “‘And this is the blessing with which Moshe blessed’: it does not say ‘this is the blessing’ but ‘and this is the blessing,’ to show that it refers to what is said above and adds to it… ‘My teaching shall drop (ya'arof) like the rain’ — ya'arof is from the word for the nape, that is, the words of Torah hold Israel by the nape firmly… for the words of Torah that Hashem gave Israel were engraved on the tablet of their heart.” Connection: Both read Vezos HaBerachah as the blessing that follows the Torah's being engraved in Israel's heart.

1479.label: Pri Tzaddik, Masei 4
1479.rest: — “All the seven nations are called by the name of Canaan, a land of commerce, where one can trade in words of Torah; and the main thing is the Oral Torah, as it says, ‘for its merchandise is better than the merchandise of silver.’” Connection: Both read “its merchandise is better” as the commerce of Torah, above all the Oral Torah.

1480.label: Rashi on Devarim 16:15
1480.rest: — “‘And you shall be only joyful’: according to its plain meaning this is not the language of a command but the language of a promise; and according to its Talmudic exposition they learned from here to include the night of the last day of the festival in the rejoicing (Sukkah 48a).” Connection: Rashi's plain reading, that the verse is a promise rather than a command, is the reading the maamar builds on.

1481.label: Rashi on Bamidbar 29:35
1481.rest: — “‘It shall be an assembly (atzeres) for you’: held back from doing work. Another explanation: ‘atzeres’ — hold back from leaving; this teaches that it requires staying overnight. And its exposition in the aggadah: since all the days of the festival they offered sacrifices corresponding to the seventy nations, and they were about to leave, the Omnipresent said to them, ‘Please, make Me a small feast so that I may have pleasure from you’ (Sukkah 55b).” Connection: Rashi gives the readings of “atzeres” that the maamar draws on, above all Hashem's request that Israel stay for one more day.

1482.label: Rashi on Vayikra 23:43
1482.rest: — “‘That I made [the Children of Israel] dwell in sukkos’: the Clouds of Glory (Sukkah 11b; Mechilta 12).” Connection: Rashi takes the sukkos of the verse to be the Clouds of Glory, the reading behind the maamar's question of why the sukkah commemorates the clouds and not the manna or the well.

1483.label: Rashi on Bereishis 21:8
1483.rest: — “‘A great feast’: for the great men of the generation were there, Shem, Ever and Avimelech (Bereishis Rabbah).” Connection: Rashi reads the greatness of Avraham's feast in the guests who came to it, which bears on the maamar's reading of this verse as the feast of the future.

1484.label: Ibn Ezra on Devarim 31:1
1484.rest: — “‘And he went’: he went to each and every tribe to let them know that he was dying, so that they would not be afraid, and he strengthened their hearts with the words of Yehoshua… and in my opinion it was then that he blessed the tribes, even though their blessings are written later.” Connection: Ibn Ezra answers the plain question of where Moshe went; the maamar takes the unusual word “vayeilech” inward, as the motion of one who goes from level to level.

1485.label: Ramban on Vayikra 23:40
1485.rest: — “And by the way of truth, ‘the fruit of a beautiful tree’ is the fruit in which there is the most desire, and through it Adam HaRishon sinned… and from here you will understand that the esrog is not bound with them in the bundle, yet it is indispensable to them, for it corresponds to the Atzeres… And our Rabbis already alluded to this secret in Vayikra Rabbah (30:9): ‘the fruit of a beautiful tree’ — this is the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, ‘Glory and splendor are before Him.’” Connection: Ramban gives the Kabbalistic reading of the esrog and its place apart from the other species, which the maamar takes up from the Zohar, the Tikkunim and the Arizal.

1486.label: Rashi on Vayikra 16:3
1486.rest: — “‘With this (bezos)’: its numerical value is four hundred and ten, an allusion to the First Temple (Vayikra Rabbah 21). ‘With this shall Aharon come’: and even this not at all times, but only on Yom Kippur, as is explained at the end of the parashah.” Connection: Rashi brings another of the Midrash's readings of “bezos”; the maamar draws on the same Midrash's list of ten merits called “zos.”

1487.label: Rashi on Vayikra 23:24
1487.rest: — “‘A remembrance of teruah’: remembrance through the verses of Zichronos and the verses of Shofaros, to remember for you the binding of Yitzchak, in whose place a ram was offered.” Connection: Rashi ties “a remembrance of teruah” to the Akeidah, as the maamar does in reading it as Yitzchak.

1488.label: Rashi on Bereishis 24:63
1488.rest: — “‘To meditate (lasuach)’: an expression of prayer, as in ‘he pours out his speech (sicho)’ (Tehillim 102:1).” Connection: Rashi reads Yitzchak's going out as prayer, which the maamar places at the site of the Beis HaMikdash.

1489.label: Rashi on Bamidbar 6:11
1489.rest: — “‘For having sinned against the soul’: that he was not careful about the impurity of the dead. R. Elazar HaKappar says: that he afflicted himself from wine (Sifrei; Nazir 19a).” Connection: Rashi brings R. Elazar HaKappar's reading, that self-denial is itself called sinning against the soul, which underlies the Gemara the maamar cites on one who sits in a fast.

1490.label: Rashi on Devarim 32:2
1490.rest: — “‘My teaching shall drop like the rain’: this is the testimony that you shall bear witness: that I say before you, the Torah that I gave to Israel is life for the world, like this rain, which is life for the world… ‘My speech shall flow like the dew’: for everyone rejoices in it, whereas rain is a source of distress to some people, such as travelers on the road.” Connection: Rashi's comparison of Torah to rain and dew is the image the maamar develops, the teaching that depends on the rain.

1491.label: Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 604:1
1491.rest: — “It is a mitzvah to eat on Erev Yom Kippur and to increase the meal.” Rema: “And it is forbidden to fast on it, even a fast over a dream.” Connection: The maamar explains the inner meaning of this mitzvah to eat on the ninth.

1492.label: Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 588:5
1492.rest: — “When the festival of Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbos, the shofar is not blown.” Rema: “And it is forbidden to move it except for the sake of using it or its place.” Connection: The ruling the maamar sets out to explain from within.

1493.label: Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 664:4
1493.rest: — “The size of this aravah is even one leaf on one branch… and he beats it on the ground or on a utensil two or three times.” Rema: “Some say that one must wave it, and the custom is to do both: we wave it and afterward beat it.” Connection: The practice of beating the aravah on Hoshana Rabbah, whose meaning the maamar explains.

1494.label: Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 669:1, Rema
1494.rest: — “And we call the last day of the festival Simchas Torah, because we rejoice and make on it a festive meal for the completion of the Torah; and the custom is that the one who completes the Torah and the one who begins Bereishis pledge donations and call others to make a feast.” Connection: The Rema grounds the Simchas Torah feast in the completion of the Torah, as the maamar does.

1495.label: Halachipedia, “Simchat Torah,” Hakafot §2
1495.rest: — It is customary, at night and by day, to take out all the Sifrei Torah and sing, and to circle the bimah with them just as is done with the lulav during Sukkos and on Hoshana Rabbah (from the Rema, Orach Chaim 669:1). Connection: The practice of the hakafos that the maamar explains through the Raya Mehemna.
